candidates.title: Patch notes for Patch Version: EA 0.4.5 on March 27th, 2018
Patch notes for version EA 0.7.3 – February 15th, 2019
candidates.text: - A fight ends if all characters of one side are unconscious. The still standing and victorious characters can then apply post combat actions on the poor fellows on the ground. - The pre and post combat UI window was completely removed as it was first very interrupting (particularly if you had lots of thieves/robbers) and second it created lots of issues for multiplayer games. -- Before a combat starts the target checks whether it should try to flee or fight. If the character decides to flee, a dice roll is executed. If successful the character runs away. If not, then the fight is started. The surrender action was removed. -- After a victory you can now select the actions Steal, Break Bones, Kill or Kidnap (depending on your character) in the action menu (Attack category) and apply the action you want on the unconscious character. - We also changed that attacking someone is finally illegal. So be careful where you attack someone, guards will not pass by without joining the fight. - Henchmen who are assigned to guard a character or building will also join fights if the guarded building is under attack or if the protected character attacks or is attacked. - The armor system changed as well now. There is a new derivative attribute called damage reduction, which reduces the amount of damage taken. - With EA 0.7.3 we generally added that characters when they die are showing a death animation and are not just vanishing like they did before. - We entirely reworked and fixed the sound system in the game as well. The game before felt really dead without all the ambient and sound effects. We added now sounds to most of the actions, to all scenario maps and buildings and we will add more in the future. Additionally we added voice sets for children and three different sets for male and female characters. As a next step we are going to implement the narrator voice overs to the game.

candidates.title: Patch notes for version EA 0.8.0 – May 3rd, 2019
candidates.text:
Again this can be a really rough move but it can also severely damage your competitors. -- Praise and denounce: You can propose to praise or denounce another family in front of the city. You can determine how strong the praising or denunciation should be. The selected family will, if the council chamber agrees, gain or lose reputation with the entire city. - If a proposal is no longer valid (eg. the to-be banished character is already dead), the office meeting is cancelled. - The AI will determine what to vote for based on their own objectives and based on the relationship to the target or the effect the proposal would have on themselves.

The other big feature we implemented, fixed and improved is the court system. Please check out all the specific changes below. - Before a trial can start there needs to be evidence of a crime. We changed how this evidence is created. If a guard is catching you, a trial will instantly be scheduled. If a non-dynasty lansquenet is interrupting a crime, the evidence will go to the neighborhood and can later still be “found” by the find evidence action. Dynasty victims will get the evidence based on a dice roll. - If characters are caught several times for the same type of crime and the AI or you are using these evidences to lodge complaints, the evidences get added to an already existing trial. The more evidences are handed in for a trial the more severe the expected punishment will be. - In order to make the whole trial scene more understandable we changed some user interfaces. When a trial starts you will receive an information UI which covers all the essential information of the case. If you have a character that can vote in a trial the verdict button will have a golden bevel. You just need to drag and drop it on the verdict you want. At the end of trial you will receive a nice summary of the trial.

candidates.text:
New features
- Multiplayer enabled (in the BETA version, please see above!). So from now on you are able to host and join Multiplayer games. What’s not yet in is the correct host migration, the chat in the game and reconnecting to a MP game but we are currently working on those features. In order to be able to enable MP we further changed:
-- As there were lots of issues related to the game’s speed settings throughout the whole game in multiplayer, we removed the possibility to increase or decrease the game speed in multiplayer games. -- We also updated the way the login flow works. A lobby will only show up after the host has finished loading. As long as a client is connecting to the game, the host can’t start it. -- One bigger change we had to do was the way pausing works in the game. Unfortunately pausing hasn’t really paused the game, which created lots of issues in multiplayer and singleplayer (eg. building placement while paused, buying add-ons while paused, etc.). Unfortunately it’s not a trivial issue. So in order to make especially MP work properly, we changed that while in pause you are not able to use any functionality other than un-pausing the game. You can still hide the UI to take nice screenshots by pressing ALT+h. -- References of destroyed buildings to routes are cleaned up correctly now, so they are properly cleaned up in MP games. -- Props are now correctly synced when they are removed between host and clients. -- Sounds weren’t initialized on clients, so only the host was able to hear sounds. We changed that. -- We added that Multiplayer lobbies are greyed out if the version doesn’t match the version of the client. This way problems of version mismatches can be avoided and you know why you aren’t able to join a particular lobby. PLEASE NOTE: Right now if the host leaves the game or is destroyed, the multiplayer game is over.

candidates.title: Patch notes for version EA 0.8.0 – May 3rd, 2019
candidates.text: You just need to drag and drop it on the verdict you want. At the end of trial you will receive a nice summary of the trial. - There are now 5 different verdicts: Not guilty (character is freed), fine (money costs), public shaming (reputation loss), imprisonment (character goes to jail) and execution (character is publicly hanged). Execution penalty is not available for all the crimes as it would be too powerful. In every trial every judge will decide on a verdict. The final verdict is determined by the average of all 3. This way it is obviously more interesting to have all office seats of a chamber taken by family members. - From now on AI dynasties will also use evidence and initiate trials. So you definitely need to be more careful now as they won’t hesitate to drag you or other dynasties to court. - We also changed how judges are voting and also implemented a system that rewards or punishes judges based on their votes. Basically the citizens always expect a specific verdict. The more a judge deviates from that expectation the more the public will be unhappy with the result and the reputation between the city and the judge will drop. - If there is not a single judge in an office group, a trial will be cancelled when the trial should have taken place. So “silencing” all the judges will make definitely sense ;) Another feature we added is that as soon as a character is imprisoned the character loses the office seat, so it may be beneficial for you to render a very hard verdict (eg. imprisonment), so a competitor loses his or her office seat. - You are now able to hand in your verdict before a trial starts. You can select the case you want to judge in the calendar and click the verdict button.

Developer Note: When Luke Cage debuted, cards that reduced Power weren't popular–Scorpion was played more than any of the other options! We've since added more and made balance adjustments, thus Luke's effect is much stronger. We've also seen him in good decks combining multiple low-Cost "tech" cards to turn off a variety of enemy routes to victory. We've reevaluated the kind of impact low-Cost cards should have, and ultimately don't feel it's healthy for them to shut off multiple higher-Cost investments regardless of their location. In the future, we'll more often "localize" abilities like this one.We're also aware that Luke's prominence affected other balancing, and that some Power-reducing cards may become too strong without Luke to rein them in. We'll be monitoring them closely.

- Shadow King

[/*]
Developer Note: One of the cards benefiting most from Luke's change will be Shadow King. When we last buffed him from 3/3 to 2/3, we thought that might be too aggressive but wanted to be sure he became a meaningful card against powerful decks like Shuri. We're glad we took that chance–it seemed strong, but the metagame also had a lot of Power buffs flying around. However, just facing a lot less Luke and avoiding Luke's location is probably worth a Power, so we're deducting it.

candidates.title: Devblog: Incoming Balance Changes
candidates.text:
[img src="https://europe1.discourse-cdn.com/flex013/uploads/fatshark/original/3X/d/0/d01fb03fcfc31c1ef12a505a38ad2e873259b0c9.png"]

Looking Ahead

This update is the first step of many to improve both gameplay balance and technical performance. In future patches, we will continue refining enemy compositions, adjusting outlier weapons, and improving those that have been falling behind. Darktide is at its best when combat feels intense, responsive, and fair. These changes are aimed at supporting that experience, reducing unnecessary extremes while expanding the number of ways players can succeed.

There are plenty of other mechanics and enemies that we can improve, such as the high density of Ogryn Bulwarks. We’ll talk more about our shielded enemies in the near future.

[img src="https://europe1.discourse-cdn.com/flex013/uploads/fatshark/original/3X/d/0/d01fb03fcfc31c1ef12a505a38ad2e873259b0c9.png"]

We’ll be closely monitoring feedback and performance data as these changes go live, and will continue to iterate based on this! Please let us know what you think of these changes after you’ve had some time testing them out next week.

That’s all for today.

See you on the Mourningstar!

-
The Darktide Team

candidates.text:
Please note - We have been made aware of an issue some users are experiencing in which tasks and buttons may not work. This is caused by Windows having no set time zone. Make sure you have a time zone set in Windows, and please submit another bug report if you continue to experience problems after following these instructions.

No new flashy features this week unfortunately, however - You will be happy to know that the team has been working themselves to the bone this week running what equates to a Quality of Life sweep of the current build of Aim Lab. Spatial sound

After much ado, spatial sound is now in! This change affects primarily tasks like Audiodetection, Audiospatial and any custom tasks that involve sound in a 3d space. This change should make distinguishing sound infront and behind the player far, far easier.

Stability sweep

Our team has been hard at work nailing down a whole host of issues with stability in Aim Lab this week, from performance to full on crashes.

By the end, over one hundred individual stability fixes and tweaks made their way into EB 0.45!

candidates.title: FREE Updates are coming: Welcome to Police Simulator in 2025!
candidates.text:
Fellow Officers,
it's crazy to say this, but 2025 marks the fourth anniversary of Police Simulator: Patrol Officers – what an incredible journey it has been!

From expanding the game based on your feedback during Early Access and launching on consoles to releasing the Highway Patrol Expansion, as a police officer in Brighton you've certainly witnessed plenty of changes throughout your career. What if we told you that this year will be no different?

Today, we're kicking off a new exciting year of Police Simulator:

New, completely free updates are coming for the whole of 2025!

The Police Simulator team can't wait to expand, improve and advance your life as a police officer of Brighton even further – with fresh content, numerous improvements, several quality-of-life enhancements, and much more.

In the recent weeks and months, we've been working on a new roadmap that is now also available on our official Trello which we also overhauled to better reflect the imminent big updates. We wanted to ensure that we're not just introducing new content to expand the Police Simulator universe but also enhance existing systems to make them more enjoyable and seamless to experience.

Here's just a glimpse of what's in store for 2025:

⚡ Preparation Update (ETA: March 2025)

The very first update will be released this month to further polish the game and prepare it for all future updates that will be released in 2025.

🚔 Car Customization (ETA: Q2 2025)

With this update, we will allow for more customization of your vehicles within the garage by enabling the ability to swap tools between vehicles which have previously been exclusive to a specific car model (e.g. speedometer of the Surveillance Police Vehicle), plus the addition of brand new interchangeable attachments like lights, decals, and rims – among other changes.

📈 QOL Improvements (ETA: Q2/Q3 2025)

candidates.title: Out Now: The Garage & Tools Update!
candidates.text:
[img src=" time for a makeover. Inside the garage, there’s now a brand-new customization tab where you can choose between a total of 18 different free attachments which can be applied to all patrol cars – from the Panther Z to the CPV. Which attachments, you might ask? Rims, spoilers, bullbars, lightbars, and stickers! The spoilers also come in a variety of colors while the lightbars now consist of two different light settings, leading to a total of 30 options to customize your patrol cars!

[img src=" did we just say… two lights? Next to the already available blue/white setting, you can now also choose a red/blue one! These are available for every single lightbar and can be adjusted, like all the other options, inside the garage.

In addition, owners of the Unmarked Pack can now choose to remove the lightbar altogether, even in combination with a ‘normal’ police livery. This way, you can finally drive a slicktop police car! You’re welcome, officers.

Gadgets Without Limits

[img src=" the last few years, we’ve released a bunch of amazing patrol cars – and almost all of them came with a unique gadget to improve your life as a patrol officer. However, all gadgets were only usable with the car they were originally designed for. Now, you are able to attach every gadget to every patrol car – with zero limits.

Please note that you must own the gadget via the respective DLC to attach it to other cars.

This means that you can even have all gadgets enabled all at once, smoothly switching between them while on the ride. You’re at an accident site? Turn on the Matrix Sign or use the Winch to tow the car to a different area! Need to catch up to a fleeing car? Let’s grant yourself a boost with Launch Control and tackle them with the Snare Net… the choice is yours.

candidates.title: OUT NOW: The Nightshift with Friends Update
candidates.text:
Fellow officers,

we're pleased to announce that The Nightshift with Friends Update is now available for Police Simulator: Patrol Officers!

[previewyoutube=waMobwc6sSc;full][/previewyoutube]

What's inside The Nightshift with Friends Update?

Well, the name of the update kinda spoils it a little... we now have nightshifts. And a co-op multiplayer mode for two players. Oh and a bunch of other stuff. I hope you're hyped.

Let's start with the Co-Op Multiplayer: You can now patrol through the streets of Brighton as a team - and protect your city, together. You can resolve accidents together. You can drive through the streets in a police car together. You can hand out parking tickets together. Isn't that great?

In addition, we're finally introducing Night Shifts! The night is dark and full of terror... at least that's what they said in Game of Thrones. Not here though! While it can certainly get pretty dark in Brighton, there are some lanterns all around. And if you feel a bit lost anyway, you can now use your new Flashlight! Praise the artificial sun! Ah, yeah, we're also introducing Road Flares which you can use to, for example, mark accident sites more clearly.

That's not all! After reading all your feedback, it became clear that you want to see some new violations as well. So, here they are:

- New Traffic Violation: Smoking Exhaust
- New Traffic Violation: Engine Too Loud
- New Traffic Violation: Driving without Light

Oh, and also a bunch of other stuff. More about that down below.
[previewyoutube=waMobwc6sSc;full][/previewyoutube]

Something else I need to know?

Yes. I hope you've seen our last post in which we've announced that starting with the new update, save games will be handled completely differently from now on.

candidates.title: Out Now: The Garage & Tools Update!

Just this week, we have started our work on the next big update, currently being labeled as the ‘Quality-of-Life Update’. In recent months, we held several polls within the community to better understand how we could improve the game across several aspects – from minor inconveniences to greater overhauls. candidates.title: Police Duties: Stop the speeders on the streets of Brighton City!
candidates.text:
Yes, pulling over! To talk with the sinful driver, you need to get them straight to the sideline. Honestly, what you perform is nothing less but the detention of the person inside the car - which can therefore only be performed rightfully if there's reasonable suspicion. Obviously, driving above the speed limit is... quite a valid reason.

To pull over a car, start your signals when you're driving behind them. This will result in a short sequence of sirens and emergency lights to signal the vehicle in front of you to pull over - and what a signal that is.

Here's another tip from our developers:
„Drivers who were pulled over are released from detainment when police officers remove themselves from the pulled-over car. So make sure to stay close.“One last detail: It's difficult to pull over in a street where there is no free parking spot. So make sure you pull over cars in spots with free parking spots if you want to be as efficient as possible.

A small journey through time

It took quite a while until we got the radar gun to the point where we're pretty satisfied with it. Below, we've included a GIF, showing off how it looked like in previous iterations.

This version isn't too old and looks already close to the current version but still a bit rough around the edges. Oh and yeah, most buildings were just white blobs.

Obviously, compared to the final version, this doesn't look too pretty - but back then this was only meant to demonstrate how the mechanic could look like once it is actually finished. At one point it could literally not take its eyes away from the cars:
„We had a prototype of the radar gun feature where the game camera followed the car. It was later on abandoned, as it was just too unrealistic and took the player's control away.“ - Thomy, Project Manager

More to come

candidates.title: Gears Tactics review
candidates.text: Right of the bat, I got this for $60 CAD bundled with Gears 5 and I haven't played a whole lot of it yet. Here are some things to note:I play on an Asus Predator 3440 x 1440p, 120hz monitor.I have a RTX 2080ti paired with a Ryzen 2700x and 16GB of Ram.All of my games run off of a 1TB SSD.The game itself supports ultrawide not only in game play, but also in the majority of cut scenes. The cut scenes can also be locked to 30 be set to unlimited frame rate if you so desire. There is a built in benchmarking too which is pretty much accurate, except for the GPU usage from what I found. My GPU in Rivia Tuner was saying 95% usage while the in game bench said 88% usage. Its not a huge deal, but something to keep in mind if you worry about that kind of thing. Playing on high settings I was able to get around 80 fps while in ultrawide at 3440 x 1440p. By default with ever preset vsync is turned on so be sure to turn that off if your monitor has gsync or freesync. The majority of the high presets are actually ultra so if you're struggling you may want to actually custom set your visuals for high as opposed to just going with that preset.Game play wise, I used m/kb. Keyboard is used to move the camera (along with the mouse. Its an either or situation) as well as used for hotkey to weapons. the LMB is used to confirm each action. This is pretty basic stuff for a turn based tactics game. The game play loop is your basic Xcom style where you kit out Gears, upgrade their skills, and even recruit new Gears all from your base. Then you go on a mission.

candidates.title: Ruined King: A League of Legends Story™ review
candidates.text: In short, 90% of the gameplay will be 'just hold down the right mouse button', this is split up in two main reasons;First off, about half of this game will be walking. You can hold down right mouse button to walk/run (jog at best). Since there is a ton of backtracking forced on the player to bloat the gameplay, it might even be more than half the game. This is exacerbated by the fact they made 'character specific skills' or 'dungeon abilities' e.g. Braum can knock a wall down. But you likely won't be using braum in the zones where he can knock a wall down so... you guessed it, you have to walk 5 minutes (possibly get stuck fighting) to run to a rest spot where you can swap characters, then run 5 minutes back, to punch a wall. Some of the characters will only require their ability one or two times during the entire game. So why did they even make this a thing? They could have definitely made it so you could use the ability, even with the characters not being on your team currently. The game could have also done without, but it probably adds like an hour or more of gameplay (or wastes over an hour of your time honestly) so they kept it in.Secondly the combat, if you can call it that. Even on the veteran difficulty, every single fight (aside from some bosses with specific mechanics) can be completed by holding down the right mouse button. This speeds up the fighting and automatically makes you use the basic abilities. Because there is so much passive healing through lifesteal mechanics, you outheal a lot of damage already. Add the Illaoi and Ahri passives on top and you literally outheal even all of the bossfights. Just stack some stamina for life(and perhaps some defensive stats on Illaoi for taunts on bosses) and you will literally faceroll the game.

candidates.title: RuneScape ® review
candidates.text: After over 1000 hours of play time I got perma banned from the game because of RuneScape's poor anti-botting detection. So last summer I tried to log into RuneScape once again, but was instead faced with a message telling me that my character was suspended due to serious rule violations. And not just for a period of time, but permanently. What had I done? Well my character report detailing my ban said "Macro Major" which is basically botting. I was vexed and perplexed. I have never used botting software with Runescape and my play time across all my accounts numbers in years and now all of a sudden I get banned from botting.After searching the forums however I found that I was not alone in this as a couple of other players reported similiar cases and not long after I found the reason to my ban. (Note: EVERYTHING ABOUT THE ANTI-BOTTING DETECTION MENTIONED HERE IS BASED ON FORUM THREADS AND I HAVE NO INSIDE INFORMATION OF HOW RUNESCAPE WORKS AS A GAME OR THE SPECIFICS OF THE ANTI-BOTTING DETECTION). With Runescape Jagex seems to be utilising an anti-botting detection method that tracks the mouse movement and/or click rate of the mouse. This means that if you don't move your mouse and just keep clicking the game won't be able to tell you apart from a bot.And there I got my answer. The last day I had watched a two-hour movie while doing high-alching, a very click intensive activity with basically no mouse movement at all. This would not be such a big deal if clicking your mouse would not be the basic premise of the game. So in essence RUNESCAPE, A GAME BASED ON CLICKING YOUR MOUSE, CAN BAN YOU FOR YOU CLICKING YOUR MOUSE.

candidates.title: MONSTER HUNTER RISE review
candidates.text: Monster Hunter Rise has met and exceeded my expectations; it provides a solid way to get into the series for beginners and a throwback to the pre-world days for veterans, with features like key quests and the more gen 4-like layout to how you go into things. candidates.title: MONSTER HUNTER RISE review
candidates.text: Monster Hunter Rise offers a VERY different experience from that of world and what you might expect from a mainline Monster hunter title. Much more faster paced in both game progression as well as combat. Systems like the Palamutes and the Wirebugs make everything feel like much more of a rush and more like you're engaging in a high-pace battle with a monster rather than in games like World and before. There is also a bit less of an emphasis on story. Story is still an important element, yes, but there's much more focus on the ranks and the urgent quests that allow you to progress and it can feel much more like a boss rush sometimes as you go from one dangerous hunt to the next. I can definitely see why some might not like it as much as other titles, the one I'm comparing it the most to being World as they are both 5th gen Monster Hunter titles. The two of them are very far apart, but I still find myself enjoying both quite a bit for the different types of gameplay they offer. Some of my only gripes with Rise is that I feel as if the Rampage mechanic is a bit underwhelming and generally just not very fun unless you're playing it with others--and another thing being the hub quests which are specifically targeted for multiplayer access. Doing them solo is a major difficulty jump and monsters will deal incredibly high amounts of damage with an equally high amount of HP as well. That plus multiplayer can just be a bit of a hassle in this game and it can feel frustrating. Nonetheless I don't think that bogs down the experience too much as you just have to be able to focus on farming and getting better gear to better tackle newer and stronger challenges. All in all, I would definitely recommend, especially to people who might want to get into the series just like with World.

candidates.title: MONSTER HUNTER RISE review
candidates.text: For context I played this game quite a bit on release, then again when the sunbreak expansion hit and now after title update 5 hit. I also played a lot of MH World and Iceborne which was my first MH game.Firstly I have to say that the sheer amount of content in this game is staggering, and the systems that work together to make the "endgame" last a long time are very impressive. There are a lot of individual monsters and variants of other monsters and the roster has been extended with the title updates. On top of that is the anomaly research system which basically is a incremental level grind as the backdrop to the rest of the endgame.When combining this with a huge variance in build possibilities, all the weapon types available and many RNG-based crafting mechanics you have a game that brings most other action RPG games to shame in the longevity department. There are also a crazy amount of sub-systems emphasizing preperations between hunts, which can lead to a lot of flicking through menus. Luckily, I feel that you can choose to engage in these parts of the game at your own leisure. In that regard it makes it even better as there are always new systems to explore more.The combat system is also a masterclass in game design, after 200 hours I still find small quirks about my favorite weapons and have new combos to practice or moves to understand better. It is also one of the more skill-based action games I have seen, the skill of a player is much more impactful than the gear they have acquired. The act of learning a new weapon type in Monster Hunter is like learning a whole new other game in regards to the difference in combat mechanics.I loved MH World but my main gripe with that game was cumbersome multiplayer mechanics when progressing together, luckily this has been fixed for Rise so it is a perfect game to progress with a friend or 3 in coop as well.

candidates.title: MONSTER HUNTER RISE review
candidates.text: Gameplay and combat is some of the most innovative in the series thus far. I truly cannot overstate how enjoyable the combat feels in this game compared to previous entries, and how fast paced the fights are, especially at late game.However, the food is the WORST the Monster Hunter series has ever seen. Dango? That's it? Balls on sticks? We FEASTED in World, dined like KINGS served by the greatest cook Astera had to offer. Now we got ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ balls on sticks and you think that's a meal? You think that's fulfilling?I can assure you my hunts were fueled not by the calories of my meal but by the hatred in my heart.

candidates.title: MONSTER HUNTER RISE review

Thank you, that took me 200 hours to come up with.I think a lot of people actually have that same belief with Monster Hunter World, and they'd be right, but a loud majority of them exclusively mean in graphics.Monster Hunter has this ability to consistently improve and add to the last while also being more accessible. For the people that thought previous games were too slow and clunky, take a dog that lets you sharpen your blade on the move out of danger. Here's a grapple hook, that can also be used to do powerful attacks, or let you recover quicker (after safer) after getting hit. All this to let new players get into the game while still feeling incredibly satisfying when you've applied yourself to know both your own and your enemies entire moveset.With DLC on the horizon, coming out day and date as on the Switch no less, I can't help but highly recommend this. Iceborne was practically a sequel and I have the feeling this DLC will do everything except lower the bar so quit it with the "Make a quality base game before expecting me to spend money" dumb stuff I have heard all too many times. This game is quality, quit comparing it to the past games that have the advantage of years of support and DLC and accept this is the best base game we have gotten.

candidates.title: MONSTER HUNTER RISE review
candidates.text: Finished base Rise and did a bit of Sunbreak. This game is like an unseasoned meal.EDIT: I wrote this comment at about 43.1 hrs into it. I now have 100 hours or so and yes, it is still bland. I know it's a meme to "ReturnToWorld" but if it's your first Monster Hunter game, I recommend playing World instead and *then* if you want more, play Rise.There are a few notable monsters to fight like Lunagaron and Malzeno but that's it, 90% of the monsters are not worth fighting. The Title Update monsters are scaled for after the endgame grind and the Risen Elder Dragons are unlocked at +110 MR. There's no way I'm playing this game for that long to find the "good" stuff.I main Longsword and I really dislike how the weapon plays here too in comparison to World. Either you spam silkbind sakura slash and charge focus slash (and miss) or you quick sheathe everything and do ♥♥♥♥ damage without harvest moon and I can't stand using that move. When monsters are super suped up, you cannot get them to stay in the circle and it's unusable in multiplayer.I unironically returned to world after that and god I missed its playstyle there. You needed to be much more precise with your hits and iai counter felt tight and insanely rewarding due to the damage and high flinch rate.It has its problems of phantom hits still but overall feels better to land than in Rise where it's just foresight slash but better.Helmbreaker also felt great because it does a TON of damage but is extremely slow. I enjoyed figuring out the openings where I could safely land one.In Rise, its easy and fast but does little damage.

candidates.title: Victoria 3 review
candidates.text: This game needs a lot of work. All of the systems are broken. War doesnt work because the fronts split too easily, allowing the AI to take territory back from you because a general can only defend one front at a time, even if they are right next to eachother. The economy WOULD work, if the AI developed its provinces. Because the AI doesn't develop its provinces at all, they basically fall into a death spiral, so the entire world economy is YOU, and a bunch of starving AI nations. The political system doesn't work because interest groups have the memory of a goldfish, I banned slavery in the United States in 1840 and the Southern Planters just forgot about it a few years later. Diplomacy is the most 'functional', but only because it really doesn't exist, its almost entirely opaque and the player barely has any control over how other countries interact with you. However despite all of this when it actually works it is very fun. The problem is that the systems just aren't working. Probably needed a delay, I'd hold off on buying it unless its on sale or the developer does significant updates.

candidates.title: Victoria 3 review
candidates.text: After a little d**king around to learn how the game works (a Paradox tradition) and a full Japan run I feel confident enough to have an opinion on this one. I've been hating on Paradox a lot myself lately across their titles. The meh reviews on the Vicky 3 we waited so long for almost kept me away entirely, but I'm glad they didn't because the game is very well designed. I can't speak to the quality at release which I'm sure was a mess but at this point things work very well overall. They completely obliterated all the worst and most grating aspects of Victoria 2. Production buildings are now very fun and make up the biggest amount of your activity as opposed to being an enigmatic system requiring perfect conditions to do what you want. Resources won't throttle 90% of the world from developing anymore since trade and acquiring them is much more accessible. Things just flow much better.From what I can tell people's gripes mainly seem to be centered around two things. 1: This isn't EU4 and 2: The AI sucks.For me at least with almost 2000 hours in EU4 the last thing I needed Vicky3 to be was similar to it. The unique aspects of diplomacy, war, units, resource management, etc. I find perfect for what Victoria is about. I don't need legions of sprites to cheese with movements and maneuvers, the fronts and invasion system is succinct and effective - if a little hands off. I'm sure war will expand with the traditional train of DLC too.The AI isn't brilliant - it never is - but is also far from brain dead. In my Japan run Prussia managed to quickly form Germany, completely consume the Austro-Hungarians, and more than double British score by the end. Sicily formed Italy, the Qing managed to repeatedly stave off the British using titanic numbers and their deep territory, the Swedes (I think) formed up Scandinavia etc.

candidates.title: Griftlands review
candidates.text: Still, this game has unavoidable fights and talks, which can make that same specialization feel counterintuitive. I suppose you could argue this is their way of encouraging "resource management" with your cards, but that isn't exactly made until you're in that situation. I don't find either the speech or the combat particularly gripping, but I'd give the speech portion a pass before the combat. There are just too many fluff cards with no actual useful incorporation, and frankly, once you know what "works" you're most likely just going to stick with that with the exceptions of more AP and bigger damage dealers. Which is fine because there isn't really any real need for intricacy because the game is so damn short.Story is that potential part that annoys me; I have no idea why they bothered to chop the characters into subplots when none of their stories are more than 3-4 hours long (and it'll be shorter than that once you know what you're doing) and they're all fairly basic. None of them are particularly engaging on their own (though I did enjoy Hector's more for his personality and Rook's more for his implied backstory); it would've been better off being a larger plot that you could play from the characters' different perspectives using their personalities and how THEY would interact with people to help differentiate the experience of playing one or the other. The main draw from what I can tell is the artstyle (OST is fairly basic and forgettable) and some of the dialogue (unfortunately outside of main plot characters and missions you can't really have much of a conversation with anyone during the in-between), but neither of those is enough for this game to have scored as highly as it did when the core gameplay mechanics are so shallow. TLDR; Griftlands as a roguelite bad, but it has the potential for a good story driven RPG (least with this world).

candidates.title: Griftlands review
candidates.text: The design lineage with Slay the Spire is pretty clear, but don't let that cause you to underestimate this game, as there are tons of meaningful innovations here on that design. The most flashy is the two separate battle systems (combat and negotiation, respectively), but the real treat here is the layer of narrative context applied to everything. Klei built a genuinely compelling setting here, and casts you as multiple characters who will interact with that setting from completely different angles. Not only does this give you three functional "classes," but this makes it so that what would just be a node in slay the spire has narrative context, choice-driven branching, and compelling reasons to care about all the characters you interact with. Really a stunning piece of work, and an outright steal at $20 - I'm stunned by *how much game* there is here.Can't recommend this highly enough.

candidates.title: DREDGE review
candidates.text: Great premise, mediocre execution. Gameplay doesn't change much and there was an upgrade in the second area that trivialized money for the rest of the game. The horror elements aren't really expanded upon and certain "horror" mechanics were more annoying than anything else. My playtime probably could have been cut in half if I didn't constantly have to find a dock to rest at for the night. The story is relatively uninspired, with you just exploring the map in a linear manner and fishing up a MacGuffin in each zone. The characters outside of the first town are under-utilized, especially the travelling merchant, as you will interact with her the most out of any NPC by far. With all that said, the game is still decent. To start, it's beautiful both visually and musically. They really went hard on the score. And the gameplay loop is enjoyable despite it not really evolving at all. Inventory tetris is always fun and the fishing minigames are great. The movement in the game is enjoyable as well, especially in more claustrophobic spaces. To top it off, the game is extremely polished and there was only one (minor and easily fixable) bug I experienced in the whole playthrough.7/10. Wouldn't recommend purchasing, but I don't regret buying it

candidates.title: Persona 4 Golden review
candidates.text: Incredibly good story, amazing characters with their own personalities, fun + challenging combat in the dungeons. I played on "Very Easy" to just focus on the story rather than combat, which did make dungeons go by very quickly. Bosses were still a bit of a challenge, nonetheless. The relationships you form throughout the game will feel like you actually made friends, and starting up the game felt like I was hanging out with them again. They will make you laugh, cry, cringe, and smile. The dungeons are fun and have unique level designs, with interesting combat that doesn't feel too repetitive even on "Very Easy". This is my first Persona game, and I highly recommend it for anyone looking for a compelling story with twists and turns and some heart-warming moments. I may play this game again later on, but now I am eager for a possible Persona 5 PC port.

candidates.title: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew review
candidates.text: I hate to see the current state of "Mixed" reviews for this game. If you've played Shadow Tactics Blade of the Shogun or Desparados III you definitely know what you're getting into. If you haven't played those games and you're reading this, you've found a great place to be introduced to this style of game. This Cursed Crew is far more inviting to you and will be easier to get into the game. You'll understand how these games are played and develop good quick saving habits. For you more experienced players don't fret, you'll find more of what you love except...The powers are far more creative and fun to use than this games predecessors. Not only that but the game is designed in such a way that it encourages variance in your crew composition. Instead of bringing the same set of characters or having the game decide what characters you use. Not only that, but you will for the most part decide what order you get your crew becomes available. If you want lore and fluff, the game will allow you to interact with it, but for the most part you can stick to the core gameplay and not interact with it much at all. Without going on too long. If stealth tactics are what you're looking for, give this game a go. It's a great example of the genre and, to me at least, a very fun one too.

candidates.title: Fields of Mistria review
candidates.text: I absolutely adore this game so far. The lore and unique characters are so cool and I can't wait to discover more as I play. I think the best systems (like the magic, stamina/health, crafting) have been incorporated in this game. Small detail, but I LOVE being able to befriend Henrietta and Dozy. (I would start wars over them.) I find that the characters are more fun to interact with than other farming/sim rpgs. I don't feel like I'm getting the same dialogue over and over again, which is refreshing for sure. The Friday nights at the inn are one of my favorite days. I love that the characters all have groups that are playing games or have linear plots that aren't central to my character. The one big issue I'm running into is the game crashing on me every so often. I'd say it's maybe happened 3-5 times since playing and often happens before I'm able to save. The only other thing is, every so often, my character will lag and move incredibly slow, although, that could just be my sub-par laptop. I have total faith that this is something that will be fixed in the future and don't want that to dissuade anyone from getting this adorable game.

Oddly enough, the battles get easier as you get deeper into the loops, but then the mystery gets more complex. I suggest making yourself a map of the castle because it isn't that big, and you'll be glad to have a reminder of interesting things you found.The game is so heartfelt, little things like how Siffrin (protag) is genuinely a huge dork that uses puns for all their attack names. Or how Mirabelle is that one friend that is super sweet and just wants everyone to be happy. The characters feel like real people, and I would love nothing more than to see more of this world.

candidates.title: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog review
candidates.text: While I've only been tangentially interested in Sonic over the years, playing through this was a treat. I found the humor overall enjoyable, so much so that it got a few chuckles and even a singular guffaw. In all, the writing oozes all the charm of a saturday morning cartoon cast that the blue blur and friends bring to the table along with some well-framed visual novel jokes sprinkled in as well. There is plenty of optional banter to be found with Tails and the rest of the cast, with the highlight by far being with Rouge and Blaze (whom I have no context for but is apparently an extra dimensional being?) that got the most enjoyment out of me. The visual novel itself is worth seeing through to the end just for the humor, but in between story bits you're often tasked with doing some isometric running games to "think" out the investigation. They aren't hard and have enough variety between them that they never feel quite like a chore; although despite the climax, I did come away wishing for less auto-runner and more character bits. In my opinion, there is no higher praise than something leaving you wanting more, and that's what this one has done. Not sure if this means I'm going to play an actual Sonic game for the first time in over a decade, but...maybe!Don't skip this one, it's a gem.

candidates.title: Wildermyth review
candidates.text: I tried my best to like this game, playing through the tutorial and a five-chapter story campaign. Unfortunately I found the writing, which is the most important part, to be underwhelming.People compare this game to XCOM but there is very little in common. This game is all about the story. Things like stats, gear, combat, tactics are an afterthought, seemingly by design. That is fine on its own. The game starts with detailed character creation where you customize not only stats/appearance, but also personality. The game features short segments for every encounter/plot where your characters interact and talk. Their personality influences what they say and do, while the player gets to steer the plot a bit. From a glance this sounds awesome.The problem is that the various character interactions and events come out of the blue. Two characters suddenly have a moment while travelling, and now they're in a relationship (after never having talked before). Two other characters become rivals all of a sudden. Some event comes up and they talk like they've known each other for years, after having been in two fights together. The game expects you to "fill in the blanks" between the story vignettes. It's a game of head-canon. In games like XCOM or Darkest Dungeon where you witness the characters fight through many gruelling missions, you would happily establish the head-canon on your own, shipping your favorite characters etc. Here there is not enough "game" for that head-canon to develop, at least not for me.Each chapter features 5-8 combats which occur over a timespan of several years (??). Then at the end of each chapter you skip another 10 years (?????). I did not find myself feeling much attachment or interest in the characters because I hardly got to see them do anything. It's like the game gave me tiny slivers of insight into what happened during all those years, and expected me to fill in the blanks.

candidates.text: I'm writing this review before a massive upcoming update; I have finished the game three times with different characters. There are new mechanics and 8 different characters, and each one have their own storyline, side quests and different events based on different time cycles. The game has a more friendly introduction, and enemies are easier to defeat than the first game but even the combat have its own new mechanics to learn. Termina is not an easier game; it's a deeper one.The Music in both games were fantastic but they differ slightly from each other. Fear & Hunger music felt darker and grittier While Termina felt like madness, but I like them both to the same degree.Playing Termina, I have not run into any bugs whatsoever. My biggest problem with the first game was the bugs that can easily ruin your whole run. The game runs bugs free, which by far is the biggest step up from the first game.Interactions between characters and the world felt way better. Not that the first game didn’t have that but since Termina have more characters the dialogue between every character, their motivation and their own journey felt more impactful than the first game. The writing felt more humorous, and all characters have their own personality. The lore expanded and the plot was interesting.The game is massive with a Detailed world. Although sometimes it’s not clear what place you should go to in the city.The gameplay is fantastic. Termina added in depth complex mechanics on top of the first game.The art is beautiful, Playing the first game I loved the art and already thought it was unique, but Termina take it to the next level.I prefer the atmosphere of the first game; it felt thicker and darker. candidates.title: Fear & Hunger 2: Termina review
candidates.text: Fear and Hunger 2: Termina builds on what was created in Fear and Hunger, but without someone needing to play the first to enjoy the 2nd. What I love about this series is that it takes the concept of a JRPG and turns it upside down. A lot of the time the best option is to run away rather than fight something. What builds on that is the Rogue-Like aspect of play. Items in the game are important, but you never know what you'll get when you open a chest or a barrel. An entire run can change based on what you find first.This is the ultimate choose your own adventure. The places you go and the people you meet could change how the rest of the game is played. People die before you find them. Monsters are created because you took the road less traveled. Its an ingenious way to create an RPG Maker game and I would highly recommend it to Puzzle loving survival horror fans and people who have enjoyed RPG Maker games in the past.And I didn't even get into how crazy horrific and detailed the lore is! Obvious Dark Souls/Lovecraft influences!

Before starting, wear max weight reducing gear, then at start fill inventory with buckets and fill all buckets with oil. candidates.title: Firework review
candidates.text: 这些片子明确传递着无鬼神的世界观。 而同一时期的港片，则是光明正大讲述各种僵尸复活和厉鬼报仇的故事。 从形式上，它们都有一个特点，就是观众不会感到困惑和错乱，要么接受鬼神的设定（比如“因果报应”），要么坚定无神论的立场（比如“世上无鬼神，人心最恶”）。 而这个游戏，我认为前言不搭后语，游戏人物说出的话，和发生的事情，从根本上就是不能自洽的，特别场景设计整体采用写实风格的同时，游戏立绘却萌萌呆呆，外加各种日式RPG表情气泡飘来飘去，这种不协调，更进一步削弱了人物塑造和气氛烘托的连贯性。 举个例子来说明，游戏开始的时候，我们就能看见“讲科学，破迷信”，当然这个标语是一个时代的特点，可以算作背景的一部分。 不久主角警官很快就明确表达过根本不信鬼神的那一套，但随之而来的诸多超现实场景，鬼打墙，甚至于穿梭于表里世界，在主角看来都毫无波澜，泰然处之。 以至于昏迷醒来后，居然推断自己通过镜子进入了另一个世界，这个就很难自圆其说。 说实话，游戏玩下来，这位主角林警官，就像是一个有些特殊本事的工具人而已，负责串联人物方便作者叙事。 幸亏游戏对于其他人物冲突刻画出彩，主角的存在感本身就显得不那么重要了。 假如说，游戏把所有超现实解释为昏迷做梦或者臆想，那么就是对80年代国内鬼神叙事主旨的回归，否则，就是一种精神错乱。 “中式恐怖”这个标签出现得越来越频繁，在考察了拥有此标签的其他一些游戏和本作后，我粗略地把它总结为一种把民俗文化和传统恐怖元素结合后产出的概念。

candidates.title: Firework review
candidates.text: Don't worry, this isn't a spoiler, and if it is and you decide to play the game then after riding a few waves of convoluted and disorientating exposition you won't remember. Nor will you care.Because there's nothing to care about, no one to root for. I guess, at best, protagonist Lin Lixun is supposed to be like a bland, faceless everyperson through which we can experience the at times evocative landscape of the game. But then there are like weird, distracting details that hint to a backstory and that don't lead anywhere. I can hear for three chapters of the game things that I already know and then suddenly there's a newspaper clipping about Lin's dad and oh wait, that's new - what does that mean? Oh no, no it's gone.And why do they talk to each other like this? I appreciate that some of the nuances were likely lost in translation, but the characters in this version end up like hollowed-out bots loaded up with forensic catchphrases and like a storyboard description of the literal plot. Was that heart photobooth moment with the manic pixie dream ghost supposed to approximate some romantic catharsis between two characters who have shared precisely no feelings with each other?It's okay, it's fine. I'm fine. I do get why people would like this game. It's stylish and has some cool ideas and mechanics; I just don't quite understand the level of recognition and enthusiasm, especially when there have been so many truly excellent games from this category over the last few years (The Darkside Detective, Pentiment, The Curse of the Golden Idol, The Excavation of Hob's Barrow, Chicken Police to name a few) that have received comparatively less attention, and it sort of makes it feel a bit like the emperor's new clothes. Do you like exposition?

candidates.title: Lamps
candidates.text: Lamps are a technology mentioned in passing in several relics in the game. They are able to provide light, heat, and an emergency distress signal from the wearer. Lamps are shown on scouts' backs on some in game images, and are also shown as a handheld version as well as shoulder strapped attachment shown on citizens. They are also used to power the prosthesis in game allowing the amputee to use the limb with almost the same degree of motion as an actual human arm, hand, or leg. The power source of Lamps are unclear but they do not seem to be powered by coal burning directly nor do they utilize Steam Cores as most machinery in Frostpunk does, but the artbook that comes with the Victorian Edition of the game describes the lamp as a "glowworm lamp". While this could indicate the light source it does not explain how the lamp produces heat or a distress signal. The "glowworm lamp" could also simply be a nickname for the lamp rather than an actual description of how it operates. The artbook further makes the statement on the lamp being a universally used piece of technology when it states: "(The Lamp) is one of the most unifying elements, bringing all the characters together. Medics, workers, kids, engineers - everyone needs it."

И вот Вам начинает казаться, что перед Вам появляется история! Вы начинаете игру в 2023 году - в темной, местами освещенной заброшенной станции. Берете свой масляный фонарь Погодите. Берете что? На улице же век технологий! В самой станции есть электричество, камеры и даже дверь на электронном замке, - но вместо верного электрического фонарика герой пользуется масляной лампой?!А что это за странный эффект на экране? Погодите-ка! Это же VHS! Но что он делает в 2023 году, при том - что наш главный герой даже не использует камеру? Ладно, откинем "условности" - возможно разработчик просто взял готовый движок игры и не смог понять как изменить некоторые предметы. На это нам намекают опции - в которых игроку доступно увеличение картинки, вероятно посредством камеры для которой и использовался VHS-фильтр изначально, а также море других действий, что отсутствует в самой игре.Вернемся в метро. Которое наш разработчик не разу в своей жизни не видел. Иначе не объяснить всего того странного дизайна, что он создал. То же самое относится и к "истории второй мировой".

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: I actually didn't realize this is one of those undertale-style games when I bought it, which is really hilarious to me. It's not a bad game. I thought the battle system was a really neat idea and is pretty much the game's best attribute. It's just that the game is really easy and when you're using the same strategy 7 hours straight you tend to realize that there's not much else about the game that's keeping you going. That's when I decided to just quit and watch a video of the ending lol.The story is extremely poorly paced, often stopping you in sections that just meaninglessly drag on for far too long. The characters are pretty bland without much depth, but once you understand what's going on that makes sense so I can't fault it too much. But that leads to the big problem of how predictable the story is. So I don't know really. It's just a pretty simplistic interpretation of its themes. If you're young I can see you really getting into it, but if you have any basic life experience you'll probably stop taking the game seriously a few hours in. One big complaint that I need to say is about the game's environment. You can interact with almost anything you see, which is cool, but the descriptions you get are some of the most bland things I have ever seen in an RPG. You interact with a lamp, the game says "Its a lamp" or sometimes, "Its a strange-looking lamp". It's just bad. If a part of your environment is interactable then make it meaningful or don't do anything at all. Anyways, as I've said, it's not a bad game but it's not for me. It was cool seeing a unique albeit easy battle system and some nice art but I can't recommend a game based on that.

candidates.text: The core idea of peggle rouge like is fun but the rouge like deck building aspect of it ends up being poorly executed. There's a fundamental flaw in that the main way of upgrading your deck (buying new orbs) stops being useful really early on. On top of that the balance is just not there. You can get a relic/orb combo early on that's so busted it trivializes the rest of the run or you can spend whole run trying and failing to get decent build that just doesn't shape up despite your best efforts and there doesn't seem to be a lot of in between. I might be more favorable if this was earlier in development but this late in development I just think there are some fundamental flaw to the game that most likely won't be changed.

candidates.title: Peglin review
candidates.text: TLDR: Peglin has a fun concept, but once you start digging for depth its hard to find any. If all you're looking for is "cute peggle roguelike" then you'll be satisfied. Peglin follows the Slay the Spire formula, but isn't finely tuned enough to make it shine. Instead, the StS formula holds Peglin back from achieving its potential. The overall systems encourage deck building and shifting your strategy as you go, but Peglin's combat seems to actively punish going all-in on a single strategy. This is because the game has so much inherent randomness that no matter what "build" you aim toward, the best strategy will always include the same few items. That randomness is also applied to the map navigation, which can be incredibly frustrating at times. You could argue that it's not "randomness" because yes, there are ways to mitigate it. That is, get Unicorn Horn to expand your "aim line" and clear each battle stage more completely to maximize your chances of going where you want to go. There are times though, like right after a "?" stage or a chest stage, where you really are just up to The Lord's Mercy.There's also a NG+ system similar to StS Ascension: The "Cruciball". However, the first few levels have done nothing to noticeably change the game. Again, I really don't know why they chose to mimic StS systems so much. StS works because you are given incredible amounts of information, and lots of agency to act on that information. Peglin gives you that information, and acts like you're supposed to use it to your advantage, but your ability to do that is restricted by RNG, and the difficulty isn't high enough to warrant the risk of specializing into a specific strategy. I had fun for a few hours, but given whats out there I don't think it was worth my money.

candidates.title: Peglin review
candidates.text: I've played a bunch of Peglin!I do not think I can really recommend Peglin.The core idea is great, and they just had a big content release, which is great support to see. But while there's a greater spread of orbs and archetypes, your ability to actually control the composition of your deck hasn't scaled to match--with the base class Peglin, you'll have four orbs to choose from after a fight, but they're completely random without any kind of reroll available--if you're shooting for something specific, you can easily just have no good options available to you.And while you do have all of those potential builds (if you get lucky enough to actually get the pieces for them)... the game doesn't really actually *reward* most of them. Ballution, the new poison build, gives you... mediocre-to-decent guaranteed damage on orbs that are otherwise hot garbage, with only one AoE option (which is admittedly good but also Quite Rare). Ballwark, the defense mechanic, comes in frankly *piddling* quantities. Your common option, at max level, gives... 1 Ballwark for every 6 pegs you hit. You are, optimistically, getting like 4 Ballwark. That is *nothing*. There's an uncommon that gives 1 for every 3 (so... 8 Ballwark)... but does zero damage no matter what. Wonderful use of a turn. And there's a rare one that actually gives you a decent-ish amount, but provides other disadvantages. And *none* of this helps you kill the enemy because they exchange having good offense for a defensive gimmick that the game actively discourages. The later levels are so bloated in what they ask of you that you really need to have stacking offensive synergies to stand a chance.But wait! There's classes focused on these gimmicks!

candidates.title: Peglin review
candidates.text: Peglin is a delightful blend of classic pachinko mechanics with roguelike gameplay, resulting in a fresh and surprisingly strategic experience. The premise is simple yet fun—you play as a cute little goblin (the titular Peglin) who embarks on a journey through various stages, battling enemies by launching orbs and aiming for pegs to deal damage.The gameplay is both easy to understand and enjoyably challenging. Every level presents new peg layouts and enemy types, making each encounter feel unique. As you progress, you gather different orbs with special effects and relics that enhance your powers, allowing for creative strategies and new approaches each time you play. The game does a great job of balancing luck with skill, so while there’s an element of chance to where your orb lands, the upgrades and your aim add a solid layer of strategy.The art style and animations are charming, adding a lot of personality to the simple gameplay. Peglin is also refreshingly straightforward, making it easy to jump into for short sessions but engaging enough to keep you playing for hours.Overall, Peglin is a well-crafted game that’s both relaxing and exciting, with enough depth to keep players coming back for “just one more round.” It’s a great pick for fans of casual roguelikes and physics-based games alike. Highly recommended!

candidates.title: Peglin review
candidates.text: You'd think "okay well Slay the Spire you get a random hand of cards every turn, so what's the difference?" but the difference is in that game you still have a choice on which cards to play. In Peglin you can skip one orb and then you're just stuck with whatever order the game decided to give you. You also don't get to see that ball until the next reload where it will again be shuffled in a random order. For example one orb does damage based on all the pegs you have hit during the combat. If you get that the first shot it's almost useless so you bin it. Then you don't even see it the rest of the battle because it was shuffled to the end or you finish before you even reload. This could be solved by doing a sort of hand mechanic like a deck builder or even just letting you hold on to an orb instead of binning it completely, swapping it out whenever you want similar to holding a piece in Tetris.If balanced correctly and if the content gets expanded on this would be an easy recommendation but as is I would save your money and wait to see what happens.

candidates.title: Peglin review
candidates.text: Peglin is a roguelite deckbuilder where the player must defeat enemies by firing orbs at pegs. The more pegs an orb hits before it falls off the bottom of the screen, the more damage you’ll deal. Enemies move closer to you each turn, and while melee focused enemies need to be standing next to you to deal damage, ranged enemies can hit you from anywhere.Each peg will disappear after being hit, gradually emptying the board, however each level will contain a few special pegs. Refreshes respawn all pegs, criticals increase your damage multiplier, bombs damage all enemies, and gold can be spent in a shop after each fight to buy new orbs, upgrade orbs, and heal your character.There are several different orbs which have abilities such as splitting into multiple orbs (which should hopefully hit more pegs), increasing the damage value of each hit peg, damaging multiple enemies with a single attack, automatically refreshing the board, or re-entering the top of the board after falling off the bottom. You can also acquire relics which apply passive effects such as damaging all enemies when you refresh the board, or detonating bombs after 1 hit instead of 2.The main reason I’ve given Peglin a negative review is because I feel like the gameplay is too random. All you can do is aim at the first peg you want to hit and hope for the best, because you’ve got no control over where the orb will bounce. Maybe you’ll hit every peg on the board and do hundreds or even thousands of damage, or maybe you’ll only hit a couple of pegs and do basically nothing. Sometimes the layout of the pegs makes lengthy chain reactions less likely, or maybe the special pegs are located in hard to hit places.My complaint isn’t about the game being too hard.

The game suffers from severe performance issues, with frame rate drops and long loading times even on high-end hardware. Some people cannot play the game anymore because of the crashes. The graphics is sometimes blurry thanks to DLSS and car models are obsolete, like some japanese car 3d models coming from Forza Motorsport 2.The multiplayer component is plagued by lag and frequent disconnections, making the online experience frustrating. Online races are more often than not a ramfest if you are unlucky enough to finish in lower Safety Rating. Penalty system is also a joke, where the victim of a crash is often awarded by a multiple seconds penalty.One of the most disappointing aspects concerns the game's content. The career mode is practically NON-EXISTENT, leaving players without significant progression.The events that could be integrated into the career mode are added and removed with each update, forcing players to play every week to avoid missing content. This strategy not only makes the game repetitive but also frustrating, as players are constantly chasing new events without ever feeling truly rewarded or progressed.The lack of a robust career mode and permanent content makes Forza Motorsport an unsatisfying experience. The repetitiveness and the feeling of constantly having to "chase" weekly events without long-term progression alienate a significant portion of the player base seeking a more stable and rewarding experience.In conclusion, Forza Motorsport is a missed opportunity. We hope future patches can address the major issues and improve the content structure, but for now, it is advisable to wait or consider better alternatives.

candidates.title: Information Regarding Career Mode Crashes
candidates.text:
Hello players,
Following the v1.4.0 update to EA SPORTS™ WRC, an unforeseen issue with Career Mode has occurred that is affecting a number of players.
Please see below for further information and what we are doing to resolve it for you all.

What happened:

- The v1.4.0 update was released.
- This update added Central European Rally to the game.
- Central European Rally was also added to Career Mode, both as part of the WRC class, and across several other Championships and Events in Career.
- The addition of Central European Rally caused a mismatch in the game code with a specific set of Benefactor objectives.
- Affected players will experience a 100% crash rate if their Career Mode save features these specific objectives.

How are players affected:

- Career Mode contains hundreds of combinations of Benefactor objectives, specifying which Events and Championships the player must compete in as progression targets.
- These Benefactor objectives are randomly assigned to players at the start of each Career Mode Season.
- Players who have specific combinations of these Benefactor objectives will experience a game crash if they attempt to continue their Career.
- Players who have not started Career, or start a new Career are not affected in Career Mode Season 1.
- Some players may be able to load a Career Mode save without any issue, though this cannot be predicted in advance.
- Players who are currently in Career Mode Season 2 and beyond in WRC2 and Junior WRC are at risk of a crash if they attempt to continue their career.
- Players who are currently in Career Mode Season 2 and beyond in WRC are also at risk, and players in Season 3 and beyond are at a higher risk.
- If a player has experienced this crash, there is a chance that their Career Mode progress has been lost with no ability to recover.

How players can mitigate the issue:

question: What makes Kingdom Rush Vengeance stand out compared to other tower defense games?

candidates.title: Kingdom Rush Vengeance - Tower Defense review
candidates.text: When it comes to the Kingdom Rush series, I've come to expect "the same but more." The maps look different and require different strategies, but it's ultimately the same familiar experience. Vengeance is the first game in the series that legitimately seems to innovate on the series' formula, at least to a small degree. Things start out pretty familiar, just with a villainous coat of paint, but soon you realize that your towers no longer have branching upgrades. Instead, you have a wide range of unlockable towers to choose from and five active tower slots at a time. This additional degree of choice adds a great deal of flexibility in your setup, much more than you normally get by simply choosing your hero. Aside from this change, everything else about the game is what you have come to expect. Despite playing as the bad guys, you're still on the defense, trying to stop waves of enemies from reaching the gate and sapping your hearts away. What does seem a bit different this time around is the difficulty level. The game has four difficulty levels, and even the second easiest is capable of causing some frustration. It's clear they spent quite a bit of time making maps capable of challenging the series' veterans who want a little more from the game. If you've never played a Kingdom Rush game, I'd recommend one of the earlier ones first. If you like the series and wish it had a little something extra to spice it up, this is the one for you. Speaking personally as someone who has played 3 of the 4 titles, this is the one I've enjoyed the most.

The improvement from KR Origins is evident and exciting: better graphics, new map and status display, refined sound effects... All new heroes are unique, have cool personalities and powers - a lot of cool dragons! But the most amazing new feature you will immediately notice in Vengeance is the variety of towers and the possibility to arrange them in whatever way you like. All of them also have fun concepts and you can even choose to arrange them by theme, as if you are decorating the level while you beat your enemies. It's just amazing! I love the KR series since the beginning and Vengeance is the ultimate homage to this game, the pioneer in tower defense quality games. The way Ironhide developed KR through the years, being so true to the original story and playstyle, yet so fresh each time a new sequel was developed, is sensational!

candidates.title: Developer Blog 6 - Looking back & Upcoming Changes in 1.0
candidates.text:
Greetings Jarls!

It’s been almost a year since we released Land of the Vikings into Steam’s Early Access program. Since then, it has seen many major updates that have brought more than 10 new & revamped features, such as the battle and runic systems, heroes, new maps, the building editor, defenses and automation, as well as over 500+ general improvements and bug fixes to the game. We’re extremely grateful to everyone who has played the game during Early Access, and provided feedback and bug reports that shaped the game into what it is now!

So before we cover all the features that’ll be coming with version 1.0, we’d like to reflect and take a look back at all the major updates that have come around during Early Access!

Looking back:

Defense Update - Dec 21, 2022

From the very first major update, we introduced new defensive buildings for you to build, like the wall and watchtowers, to defend your bases against other Viking raids. As these Vikings can now attack you, you get the choice of how you’d deal with these attackers.

Not only that, the Defense update brought in many small improvements and heavily requested features like automated jobs and reassignment that make things easier to manage towards the later stages of the game, as well as reworking the tavern so that Vikings can regain their happiness.

Building Editor Update - Apr 4, 2023

The next major update introduced the building editor, a powerful in-game editor that allowed you to build and personalize the look and feel of an endless variety of buildings and decorations. You can also share your creations with your friends and other players through the Steam Workshop. With over 200 workshop designs from the community, you can subscribe and pick the ones you like best and make your village unique.

Battle & Runic Update - Aug 31, 2023

candidates.title: Developer Blog 6 - Looking back & Upcoming Changes in 1.0
candidates.text:
Lastly, our most recent update introduced many different new features. These include a runic system that grants your village abilities, heroes that will inspire and lead your Vikings into battle, a new currency - gold - that can be used to upgrade your heroes and be spent in the runics system, and a complete overhaul of the battle system that allows you to strategize and calculate the consequences based on soldier types and numbers.

Next to this, we have been meticulously going through more than 11,000 bug reports and feedback to classify, fix, and improve the game as much as we can since the Early Access release in preparation for the 1.0 release. This invaluable input has have sparked numerous quality-of-life improvements, including enhanced camera and in-game speed for specific goods and days, an expanded building editor with more meshes, and new map textures. Additionally, we've tackled various reported bugs, addressing issues such as characters climbing on top of buildings and randomly quitting jobs, save problems, and editor-related glitches. This effort was made possible by your invaluable feedback and support. We simply could not do it without you all!

Moreover, in response to your input and wishes, we brought in features like Steam cloud saves, automated tree-cutting, fresh maps, and UI enhancements aimed at enhancing village interactions.

What’s coming in 1.0:

With just 1 week before the full release, we’ll be adding in the last of the features that we set out to do at the beginning, fulfilling our original vision for the game. Here’s what will be coming in the 1.0:

New Game Mode - Immersive Mode

Take on the mantle of Jarl, and guide your Vikings through glory! In this introductory mode, it's a great starting point for new players to learn how to navigate Land of the Vikings, with more than 25 objectives exclusive to this Viking-themed story.
