candidates.title: SCP: CBM v.1.3.0.0 - Anomaly Ascension Update
candidates.text:
SCP: CBM v.1.3.0.0 - Anomaly Ascension Update

v1.3.0.0 Changelog:

#1: Changed the official & community server-list backend to a more robust and future-proof system. (Client & Server)

#2: Changed the Omni Keycard multipliers for SCP-914 in order to facilitate slightly easier item acquisition. (Client & Server)

#3: The constant "Const func_getplayergasmask" which was removed a few updates ago (likely accidentally), has now been added back, utilizing an empty ID at slot "271". You can now make scripts again which can check whether a player is wearing a Gas Mask or not. (Server only)

#4: In order to allow more than a single player in Breach Multiplayer to bypass the door locks to the "Entry Zone" from the "Heavy Containment Zone", the Level 3 Keycard near SCP-895 has been replaced with a Level 4 Keycard to accommodate for the higher security levels required. (Server only)

#5: Removed a few development comments that could've led to potential Memory Access Violations due to broken characters that weren't even Unicode characters, and as such led to broken comments that nobody could read anyways, thus making them obsolete. (Server only)

#6: Updated and added the functionality to create custom death, kick, join and leave messages. (Server only)

#7: Updated the default options.ini in order to include "borderless windowed = true" as the default option for launching the game, thereby reducing the number of problems many are facing when launching the game first via default Fullscreen. We also disabled "16bit" and "play startup video" by default, however you can enable these manually if you need these. (Client only)

candidates.title: Satisfactory 1.0 out now!
candidates.text:
The servers are now faster to download with a smaller size, and easier to install as they only use port 7777 UDP/TCP. We now correctly bind to IPv4 and IPv6 simultaneously, so you no longer need to use the multihome command line. You can now run it as windowed or as just console. Additionally, there is now TLS support for added security.

We’ve also improved the in-game UI/UX to tweak all the session settings or advanced game settings. Additional to the now-adjustable server settings, you can now also download a save from a server to continue playing locally if you’re the server admin.

We have added support for an HTTP API, so it is now possible to create applications to communicate with the dedicated server for those who are interested in developing tools for it :)

BUG FIXES

This time around, we have fixed such an overwhelmingly massive number of bugs since the last update, at the time of writing we have 3,312 bug tickets marked as fixed and 92,052 submits having been made in our build management system since the last public update (v0.8.3.3).

To make the patch notes more enjoyable for everyone, instead of being 50+ pages of bug fixes which would drown the info about the other goodies, we’ve decided to keep the patch notes more focused on new content and major changes.

This also gives us the opportunity to start fresh with knowing what you all care about for us to fix and for you to let us know if we forgot anything important (or broke it again, whoops).

You can give us all your bug related feedback in our QA Site, we read it every day: https://questions.satisfactorygame.com/

Anything you post here will help us fix those issues in future patches!

candidates.title: Solar Club Letter: Season 4 & Year 2 Reveal Recap
candidates.text:
Season 1 was the launch of TDUSC. It brought over 100 cars at launch with dealerships, workshops, the Solar Hotel which came with 4 liveable spaces, a 6 car garage and an island recreated at 1:1 scale, Hong Kong Island. It also brought the first Solar Pass, live events, and other features. Players often mentioned the physics and car sounds of the game were well created, and it’s something they saw was a good base that we needed to improve on.

🏝️ Season 2

Season 2 brought Ibiza! It was faithfully recreated at a 1:1, but only the town of Evissa was made. This created a great contrast between the two islands, similarly to what TDU2 offered for players. Ibiza welcomes back an old character from the Test Drive franchise, Tess Wintory, and her brand known as Selene which had 6 vehicles customised. It brought a new social hub, clan stores, rotating races, and an increase in the clan influence level cap. We also brought an improvement to the wheel animation with 900 degree steering!

🚗 Season 3

Season 3 was initially planned to be the Clan Wars update, but after player feedback, we decided to delay this update theme and instead bring highly requested features by the community to change the direction of the game. This is where our future started. In Season 3 we brought back:

Car Delivery Missions - A highly requested feature from the past TDU games that is essential to improve the TDU DNA. In this new game mode, you are able to deliver vehicles for customers to the location of their request. We dressed some of these contracts (the name for missions in TDUSC) with some props to make it feel more immersive, especially compared to the previous TDU2 car delivery missions. Players seemed to enjoy this new method of playing, as it took them away from the racing.

candidates.title: Artisan TD review
candidates.text: *Product Refunded*Artisan TD is a competently made game in its own right, especially considering the size of the team. The music is good and the graphics are passable but in the great pantheon of tower defense games its pretty bland and basic. The core conceit of a tower defense game is being able to tailor your defenses and play around with tower combinations. The problem is the game doesn't let you do any of that such that its closer to a puzzle game than a strategy game. Every level pretty much has one optimal solution to it and replaying older levels doesn't let you bring new towers to play around with. And the flow of coin is so constricted, made worse by the fact that selling towers imposes a massive penalty on the cash returned which really restricts how creative you can be with your layouts.If you are into puzzle games go for it but if you are looking for an actual tower defense game I would steer clear.

candidates.title: Artisan TD review
candidates.text: I will start out by saying that I agree with the negative reviews claiming this game is a puzzle game, and not a tower defense game. Even on normal difficulty, you will find yourself trying to find the exact intended strategy instead of reacting to the level like you would in a normal tower defense game. This is because there is effectively no margin for error on any level, even on normal. This is a positive review, because it is a well-made game, and I believe that this game has a lot of good ideas in it and that there is still fun to be had here, despite the over-tuned difficulty. The presence of the ability to retry a level from any wave is a great inclusion, but it is unfortunately a required mechanic of the game for you to trial and error your way to finding the developer's exact intended build pattern, instead of the quality of life feature it would otherwise be.If the developers renamed the normal difficulty to "hard", maybe made the current hard difficulty "impossible" or something, and added a new "normal" difficulty where the player actually has a margin for error to enjoy trying different combinations of towers/placements, I would be able to unambiguously recommend this game. As is, It's unfortunately weighed down by the overly-precise nature of the balance, so I'd recommend watching gameplay of this before you consider buying it.Note: I'm aware that "normal" and "hard" aren't difficulty names in this game. For this review, "normal" = Artisan, because that's the default middle difficulty most people will play.

candidates.title: Deified Releases today!
candidates.text:
DEIFIED RELEASES TODAY!

Hi everyone!

We wanted to drop by with some news because a very important milestone is approaching for our little studio: Deified releases in version 1.0 today, September 21 at 5 PM GMT+1.

We’ve now been working on this game for more than two years, and seeing its full release finally approaching brings a huge sense of relief, a lot of excitement… and, if we’re being completely truthful, a little bit of vertigo too.

Deified is a project that means a lot to us.

With it, we wanted to create a tactical game where building your strategy, experimenting with your Relics, synergies and different builds would be at the heart of the experience. But we also wanted it to have a strong identity of its own, with a world, an art direction and a story that would give a soul to all those gameplay systems.

And most importantly, we didn’t build all of this alone.

Throughout development and Early Access, players have sent us an incredible amount of feedback, reported bugs, discussed balance with us, tested builds we would never have thought of ourselves and, sometimes, completely challenged some of our ideas.

The Deified we are releasing today is a much better game because of them.

If you enjoyed searching for the right combinations, adapting your strategy and experimenting in Artisan TD, we hope you’ll find some of that same enjoyment in Deified, even though this new game will take you on a very different adventure.

Deified releases on September 21, 2026 at 5 PM GMT+1.

Beyond announcing our new game, we also wanted to take this opportunity to thank you.

Thank you to everyone who played Artisan TD, left us a review, sent us a message, told others about the game or simply kept following what Unexpected was working on.

Every game we’ve been able to create exists in part because players decided to follow us from one project to the next.

So thank you for being there for Artisan TD.

candidates.title: Artisan TD review
candidates.text: Simple yet challengingArtisan TD seems like a very simple game but it quickly becomes a big challenge to figure out exactly what tower to place, when and where to place it. If you've played other tower games you might recognize some things in this game but you won't be recruiting troops or get overwhelmed with skill trees.And that's exactly what this game does right. It's simple and has an appealing design. So far I haven't faced any bugs - unless you mean the enemies. I hope more tower defense games take inspiration from Artisan TD - to stay simple and not implement RTS-aspects or making so many skill trees and awards pop up in the playe's face. It's a calm experience but still remains challenging.

candidates.title: Artisan TD review
candidates.text: As a newcomer to the Tower Defense genre, I'm thrilled that Artisan TD is my first experience. This game has provided me with an engaging and accessible entry into the world of TD games.The fantastical universe is beautifully crafted, with stunning graphics and meticulous attention to detail. The maze-building and tower mechanics are intuitive, allowing me to quickly grasp the strategic elements without feeling overwhelmed. The adjustable difficulty levels are a fantastic feature, offering a suitable challenge for beginners while remaining rewarding.Artisan TD also excels in balancing complexity and fun. Each level introduces new mechanics and challenges, keeping the gameplay fresh and exciting. The variety of towers and upgrades offers deep strategic options that kept me hooked with each playthrough.I highly recommend Artisan TD to anyone looking to explore the Tower Defense genre. It’s a well-designed, visually appealing, and incredibly fun game. A superb introduction to this type of game!

candidates.title: Artisan TD review
candidates.text: This is going to be a tough one.The game's graphics are just OK (It's a taste thing so my opinion is entirely subjective). The colors are so saturated and the little fellows who come out of the base are super small so you can barely see them (20+% scale could work).The tower type is a bit weird, you have the option to select archers but if you don't put them on top of a reguar base, it won't work. Each tower should be put as individual type. Also, we should have some indicator like a number on top of each tower type (at the bottom of the screen) to just press a number and select the type of tower. For example (Number 1 = Base, Number 2 = Archers, etc...)The "Play" button and fast forward are too small. One last thing. When you finish each round, the next screen shows the same round (instead of the next one) so I kept going over the same level a few times until I realized "Wait... I'm doing the same stuff over and over". So you have to go back to the map, then select the next level. We should just hit the next level right from the same screen after we finish the level!Overall... other TD's like Bloons TD 6 offer a more fluid experience for less money. I won't refund the game to support the developers, I think this is a good start but there are quite a few things to improve. Keep it up, devs! You can do it!

candidates.title: Artisan TD review
candidates.text: There's very little freedom to create your own solution in Artisan TD. Due to the relatively small maps and nerf/buff tiles you're essentially trying to discover the scripted solution that the Dev seems to want you to use to achieve success. There are fundamental elements missing that you would expect from a 2024, such as the freedom to target closest/strongest/furthest creeps and a panic button on cooldown when that rando creep gets too far ahead.Due to these constraints, it's hard to recommend Artisan TD with so many other, better TD games available that have recently released.

candidates.title: Stoneshard review
candidates.text: 作为一个中世纪风格的游戏粉丝，我非常喜爱这款游戏，但还是有太多缺点需要制作组去完善。 我本想给予差评，但是我真心希望这款游戏能够进步，所以我还是决定留下好评并提出建议。 其实迅速提升玩家游戏体验的方法非常简单，先做到这三点：1.提供类似马匹、马车等交通工具帮助玩家在地图上移动，比如玩家能够骑马，加快在地图上移动的速度，并能在城镇中付钱来坐上马车由一座城市快速旅行到另一座城市。 再不济，模仿天国拯救的大地图快速移动方式也未尝不可。 我不明白为什么制作组要让玩家靠着双腿在地图上奔波，这是完全没有必要的。 2.添加即时存档功能。 我理解制作组想让游戏变得更加硬核，但完全不应该用限制存档这种手段，至少应该给予玩家选择，比如像骑马与砍杀那样的可选择的存档机制。 只能通过睡觉存档，这不是硬核，这是恶心玩家。 3.更新应该着力于扩大地图、增加可探索地点、增加更多职业和自定义职业的模式、完善游戏主线等，以此来提升游戏可玩性，而不是把精力放在过分夸张的“平衡”上。 As a medieval fan, I love the game, but there are still too many flaws for the production team to fix. I wanted to give it a bad review, but I really want the game to improve, so I decided to leave a good review and make suggestions. There are simple ways to quickly improve the player's experience. Provide transportation such as kingdomcome:deliverance to help the player move around the map. For example, the player can ride a horse, speed up the movement of the map, and pay for a carriage to travel quickly from one city to another in towns I don't understand why the production team would want players to run around the map on their legs, it's totally unnecessary 2.

candidates.title: Grand Tactician: The Civil War (1861-1865) review
candidates.text: Like most everyone else, I think this game has amazing potential. If it comes together, it could be the greatest strategy game I've ever seen. That said, there are a few concerns that, for me, could improve the game. First, I'd like to echo another player's experience where armies marched past each other without engaging. Second, it would be great to move army and corps commanders individually around the battlefield, so that a player could exercise close control over the most critical sectors. Third, since the game has so much going on across the campaign map, it would be a big help to be able to make multiple save files. I know it enables save spamming, but this is for fun and restarting my campaign just because I missed something a while back becomes frustrating after a while. If anyone has a solution for these issues, I will appreciate it and change my review accordingly. Final word, I do recommend buying this game, if for no other reason than to support the developer and hopefully see it become what it could be, the greatest strategy game to date.

candidates.title: Aimlabs review
candidates.text: Aim Lab is an outstanding game that offers players a fantastic blend of shooting mechanics, graphics, and gameplay. The game provides an immersive experience for players of all skill levels, making it an ideal choice for anyone looking to improve their aim and hand-eye coordination.One of the things that sets Aim Lab apart from other games is its advanced AI-powered performance analysis system, which allows players to track their progress and see where they need to improve. The system provides detailed insights into key metrics such as accuracy, reaction time, and consistency, allowing players to see their progress and identify areas where they need to focus.Another great feature of Aim Lab is its wide variety of game modes and maps, each of which is designed to challenge players in different ways. From fast-paced action-packed games to slow-paced sniper-style gameplay, Aim Lab has something for everyone. The graphics and visuals are top-notch and provide an immersive experience that truly brings the game to life.Finally, the community aspect of Aim Lab is fantastic. With a large and growing player base, players can connect and compete with others from around the world, as well as share tips and tricks on how to improve their aim.Overall, Aim Lab is an exceptional game that provides a fun and challenging experience for players of all skill levels. Whether you're looking to improve your aim, have some fun, or simply enjoy some great gameplay, Aim Lab is definitely worth checking out.

candidates.title: Wasteland 3 review
candidates.text: Genuinely, very enjoyable!I found it surprising how well the game handles player choice, with a lot of decisions actually making an impact. It should remind certain AAA studios (you know who you are) for forgetting how fun and immersive RPGs can be when the player is given a decent level of agency.Good build variety compliments the equally engaging turn based combat, if you're a fan of that.Well-structured story, without railroading you into certain paths. Wasteland 3 makes you aware of your ultimate goal, but leaves the journey and the methods of play entirely down to the player.Not a huge map, but very dense with content. In my opinion, that is a good game-world. I loved exploring and bumping into various characters and side-quests.That said, it is not a perfect product. It is buggy, but I did not experience the same level of jankiness as other players. Of course, that doesn't mean each user has had the same experience on a technical level. I only played single player for example so my review is based solely on that. I have heard Co-op has mixed results. In terms of DLC, I did not think that the standard of quality is the same as it was for the base game. Therefore, I would not recommend purchasing the extras blind at full price.Overall, a little hidden gem albeit a rough gem.RPG and turn based fans (particularly of the old Fallouts) will probably have a great time with Wasteland 3 if bought at a reduced price.

candidates.title: MARVEL SNAP review
candidates.text: I would not recommend playing Marvel Snap despite it being a simple, fast, fun, and well designed mobile card game. The reason being is a wide number of issues but at its core the LOOT BOX card unlock system (introduced in pool 3 so it is a bit of a bait and trap system) and the wide range of collection level matchmaking in pool 3 since this has questionable balance for new players. To me, these core issues actually make the overall experience in Marvel Snap a more frustrating experience than fun. My experience in pool 3 has been continuously playing against players that have extremely powerful series 3, 4, and 5 cards that I did not access to yet. For series 4 and 5, I likely would not have access to them several months. SNAP is balanced such that these are all counterable cards, but I felt like I had to play to disrupt/counter their decks, rely on luck in lockjaw decks, or play leech decks (quite toxic) to be competitive. Since on raw power alone, my decks generally did not compete with theirs. The LOOT BOX mechanics for cards means that specific cards can't be targeted without use of the overpriced and limited token shop. Further cards are not guaranteed to be unlocked from caches and reserves in pool 3 which also decreases in frequency from 8 to 12 collection levels. This used to be worse, but still feels bad man. Further the new card releases have been very strong and almost exclusively for series 4 and 5 which means I am likely further away from completing my card collection than when I started and will continuously have less competitive options due to power creep of the new cards being introduced. Overall the above issues make the overall journey in this game an frustrating experience that could be a exercise in futility if a full collection is your goal that I would not recommend to others.

candidates.title: Resident Evil 3 review
candidates.text: Back in 2020 I was brimming with excitement regarding the announcement of this remake for very obvious reasons. Resident Evil 2 got a generally well received remake that for the most part captured the exact same essence of the original, but with some added flair regarding its atmosphere, which was pumped with steroids. So how does this remake fair? Well when I went into it back in 2020 I had, I guess, unreal expectations. But when I heard that almost universally, a lot of fans felt the way I did, I knew I was justified with saying this game was disappointing. Don't get me wrong, it still has the beautiful modern grunge that made the RE2 remake work so well, but no amount of visual glimmer can mask what feels like a glorified expansion. Granted the original RE3 was often regarded by some as a sort of “expansion” or “spin-off” but coming hot off of RE2's heels I and many others expected a more opened up/expanded RE2 experience with the one of franchise's favorite baddies Nemesis who looks great in this game but is sorely underutilized, and instead feels like a more scripted Mr. X. Also this game features a LOT of cuts, and when I mean cuts I mean the complete omission of certain parts of the original game like the park and clock tower. I have heard vague rumors that a director's cut was planned to be released, but that rumors hold very little credence to me since it hasn't been confirmed by any official sources. What's even more laughable is how mercenaries was cut, possibly in favor of Resident Evil Resistance, the online game mode that *had* a roadmap that was quickly abandoned. But what's my verdict?

candidates.text: This is an okay game and it's nice to look at. There's some ideas in it that I like. candidates.title: HUMANKIND™ review
candidates.text: There's a lot I love about this game, but it feels like it never left the BETA phase. It's extremely buggy. In late stages of the game combat becomes locked in loops where it won't let you complete a turn: it doesn't freeze, it just won't finish the process. And it's a frequent bug. It also runs painfully slow in comparison to similar games even though visually there is less happening. There are also a host of little decisions they've made that make this game difficult to play: a big one is that visually your districts are barely discernible so at a glance you can't tell what the makeup of your cities is. There are also issues that seem like problems of calibration: inflation of money and influence grows so quick at some point that they are actually harder to utilize at the game progresses. On low skill levels computer players (including barbarians) tend to team up against me and leave one another alone. The only time I won I was doing terribly and ages behind several other players: it's no fun to suddenly be told you've won without a good explanation of why. The game needs a ton of recalibration and tune ups. It's unplayable at this point.

candidates.title: HUMANKIND™ review
candidates.text: This game is officially the bar of too much "for the sake of the game" and too little "for the sake of the theme".Ultimately a lot of the systems are fine, but so disjointed from what you are doing that they play more like the rediculous mini games in German board games. Yes they are novel and interesting at first. If you lean on them too hard though the game starts being about learning 13 different thematically null competitions going on simultaneously. This causes people to shut off rather than engage in systems, causing their experience to suffer.A lot of this seems geared toward multiplayer play as well, and that is a huge miss, as the vast majority of it's players will never experience this, and thus not understand why systems might be a certain way for the sake of competitive game-play.The game is essentially played for points. Long term objectives are very hard to stick to given the systems that are brought to play. This is another source of problems. While yes having risk reward scenarios between getting points and progressing through eras / developing your culture creates interesting tactical choices, they come at the expense of player immersion and fantasy.Going in thinking you are going to play as a certain build (which I found to be fairly limiting from a play style standpoint) hamstrings your ability or desire to engage in a point system that rewards stalling out in eras and NOT picking new civilizations. Meanwhile, the builds them self require a lot of creativity to see the synergies they bring. There aren't really that many science builds because the cultures are chopped up and sprinkled through the era, so specializing is often not possible unless you are always picking your culture first (which is only guaranteed to happen in single-player on a low difficulty setting). Forcing me to pick something else, while interesting if you are up for a challenge and enjoy the pure strategy of the system, generally feels like a load scenario or a restart scenario.

candidates.title: HUMANKIND™ review
candidates.text: Good game, every bit as enjoyable as I had expected it to be from the beta! Definitely has some issues with getting it to run right now, but most of these were highly unexpected and there are workarounds to most from what I've seen.The gameplay itself isn't too far off of Endless Legends with just a sprinkle of Civilization flair on top, so don't be fooled by the paint and start thinking this is something it isn't. candidates.title: HUMANKIND™ review
candidates.text: Before I go into depth, the bones of a truly great 4x game are here. There are plenty of decisions that are made, the combat is complex enough to be engrossing, and while the tech tree is a bit narrow, it isn't missing anything massive. The game is enjoyable, I simply cannot recommend it at the 40 dollar price point in its current state.The issue is simply the game has so many little quirks that you'd think would be caught in playtesting that I'm not sure if it *was* playtested. First and foremost, the UI is simultaneously beautiful and absolutely useless. Information that you need, such as how much stability you currently have or how much of the resources are poduced by the hinterland territories aren't readily available and you need to do the arithmetic yourself. To change your religion from Shamanism or Polytheism to the "real world" organized faiths, you have to wait until you get a tenet, *select a tenet* and then use a little drop down in the confirmation screen. You can find out what infrastructure you've built easily in the city screen, but finding out what districts and how many isn't nearly as easy.Secondly, the AI controlling automated exploration is absolutely trustworthy up until the point you try to use it on a bireme or quadrimme, which will immediately sail into the ocean and sink itself, the captain taking pride in immediately wasting the population point you invested into the unit. This same AI also seems to command aggressive independent countries, who will trudge through two players to attack your single undefended outpost, and then turn right around the moment they see a single scout.There's also an issue with notifcation overload, especially if you have a lot of outposts sitting waiting for you to get another city cap point.

I could go on and on but what you’re getting here is a great card system with amazing mechanics to boot. ACG may be a trusted reviewer for a lot of people but he is 100% wrong about this game. When he says things like “everyone will have the same exact method and go through the same strategies to get to the end game” clearly shows he doesn’t play card games. So you’re telling me a game with many characters and tons of deck combinations will somehow boil down to everyone using the same characters and cards? No, this isn’t MTG or Hearthstone with a meta Lol. Now everyone loves to trash on the dialogue and the story. You know what, you can literally skip everything. That’s what I do, sure I choose what I think would give me friendship points to get better abilities for a character but i’m not going to spend hours listening to banter and superhero social media, although the twitter like network they have does bring some laughs. Regret buying.Update: After a few more hours of gameplay--same thoughts. The game violates the first rule of game design: "Make sure it's the player having fun." Unlocking new skills somewhat dilutes their importance due to randomness, and it is frustrating to have entire team builds ruined do to random relationship changes. Adapting to positive/negative relationships is only slightly interesting/fun. I wish there was more player agency in controlling how relationships form and affect gameplay other than a single +- meter. At this point in the game, I only care about relationships so far as they don't ruin my intended strategies.(2) Boss difficulty. Encountering a boss for the first time is almost always an immediate death sentence since you don't understand the boss's mechanics. Learning is an important part of the game, but it takes significant time to reach a specific boss in order to learn mechanics just to fail. This is very frustrating as there is no incremental or foreshadowed learning to a given boss. At some point, I just read guides to learn about the given boss mechanics, and then develop my own strategies to deal with them. Learning mechanics isn't as fun as the process of developing strategies using them. Why should enemy move sets be hidden until they use them? It's more fun make a plan than to wait around, suffer, and then make a plan after dying.(3) Learning character synergies and skills takes a long time. I wish there was some kind of practice mode where I test out different mechanics on different enemies. Making doomed runs to learn mechanics is very tedious, and at least for me, the symbology/explanations of certain effects are ambiguous. Again, making plans is fun; trying to interpret how skills mix together is not.

candidates.title: Leaf Blower Revolution - Idle Game review
candidates.text: The rare negative review for a game I will continue to play:I'm "over the hump" but the amount of information / signposting / tooltips in the game is insufficient in a way that can be profoundly unfun. You are frequently asked to choose which of many ambiguous upgrades to devote resources to. How to progress the game *at all* can be arcane. Unlocking something you realized you could have and should have (and would have, if you knew what it did) unlocked 48 hours of gameplay ago is pretty frustrating. Unlocking something that seems like it will progress the game, only to realize it does nothing until other progress is made, is also pretty frustrating. Having to reverse engineer (or wiki) which bonuses are additive vs multiplicative is inane. Some amount of exploratory gameplay can be fun, but having to rely on exploratory gameplay for nearly every ambiguous progression decision inflicts recurring psychic damage. The alternative is to dive headfirst into the wiki and into player guides, which reduces fun in proportion to how much it smooths out the player information experience. I'm "over the hump" in the sense that I've made peace with these patterns, but all indications are that they will continue. If you can get past that, it's definitely one of the games of all time.

candidates.title: Creatures of Aether review
candidates.text: I really really wanted to enjoy this game. Rivals is a super fun game that I love playing with my friends but this game seems to not even respect the source material. I think the biggest problem is that the UI, monetization, and way of leveling up makes it feel like a mobile game that I am just playing on PC, and yep look at here it's on the App Store. I don't understand what it is with indie game developers and porting their mobile ports to places like steam when they really should be making dedicated PC versions. I think the fact that only 40% of people got passed the tutorial and only 25% beat their first online match showcases how fast players are dropping off of this game. It's really a shame because I really love the card mechanics but there just isn't enough there to keep me interested. I really feel like there needed to be more features that different cards can give you, like the Rival cards but maybe a little less OP? Not to mention that there is no CPU mode for people who just want to play the game and don't want to bother with online a holes. I don't even care if you made it to were you don't get any XP or money from it just make it a feature for people who don't want to play online.I understand why these choices were made because you wanted to appeal to the casual mobile game crowd but if that's the case you should have made a better version for this PC port. I don't even care if I had to pay $10 for a "plus" version of the game that gave me more features to play around with, maybe even a custom card maker in a similar vain to the Rivals workshop. Creatures of Aether is sadly another mobile game port that doesn't add anything, or take advantage of the fact it's on PC, that didn't need to be made. If you like online puzzle strategy card games then I would recommend a 30 minute playthrough but there isn't that much that will be making you want to come back.

candidates.text: From the bit I've played, it seemed fun. It took me a while to get a basic grasp of the game's mechanics, but I thought it was a simple game that someone can just pick up and play every now and then. Truthfully, I mostly started playing for the sake of the new Rivals of Aether stage skin, but I was willing to stick around for a while.Unfortunately, I simply cannot support the aggressive monetization. I understand that free to play games do need some sort of income, but this game has some of the most eggregious practices that I see common in these sorts of games. Rewards that change daily and caps on non-daily rewards that are only removed by purchasing a premium pass? That's flat out dangerous. The rewards section is even straight up showing you locked content behind the paywall. Even worse, when I first reached that page, I was straight up told that I'd have to pay unless I was okay with missing out on the "cool stuff". The fear of missing out is one of the most often preyed upon fears in these schemes by companies much more insidious.There was another review somewhere that said the single-player dungeons were locked by premium currency. One, I don't think there should even BE a premium currency, and the fact that there are multiple purchaseable currencies feels gross. That's a level of obfuscation that's generally used to hide the fact that you're paying real money for fake money. Two, locking the mode behind premium currency makes the mode significantly less accessible to people who wanted that style of gameplay.With the kind of situations that the video game industry has been finding itself in for a while now, aggressive and exploitative monetization is not the way to go. Rivals of Aether is amazing because it shows that you listen to the fanbase and are interested in making an incredible game. I was more than willing to support that game. I'm also sure Dungeons of Aether will be likewise awesome.

The issue is that while you technically can get every card very easily, what you have the option to spend your real world money on isn't just cosmetics, you can literally pay to unlock "boosters" for your cards, which quite literally increases their power level. This is honestly the worst pay to win system ever, I really would rather have this game take notes from other games like Legends of Runeterra where you also technically can get every card for free, and you can end up building any deck you want pretty early on. The difference there however is you have to play A LOT to get all the cards, so it is genuinely kind of worth it to spend the money to get all the cards if you really enjoy the game in order to have a lot of deck building options, without feeling like you NEED to spend money to enjoy the game. In this game though you literally are paying and grinding in order to get bigger stats on your cards, not to unlock cool new cards to build new decks with, it's super pay to win in the worst way possible.This game is super fun but I can't recommend it for this reason, unless you plan on playing vs the AI and specifically with your other F2P friends, because this pay to win system not oy makes the game feel less competitive, you also just feel like you're not getting rewarded for spending the time playing and getting better.

candidates.title: Library Of Ruina review
candidates.text: Library of Ruina is a special gem that will be most enjoyed if you have ever heard of its prequel game "Lobotomy Corporation". Even for someone like myself that has not played Lobotomy corporation, it stands alone as a strong view into a dystopic world. Created by the Korean developers Project Moon, the game stands out as a product of love by the developers.Library of Ruina is a CCG game that follows Roland, a washed-up Low-grade Fixer in a cold, cruel and dystopian world who finds himself in a mysterious library. Without going too much into details, you are employed as a librarian at the eponymous library. Your task is to put books up on offer to invite stronger people into your library, defeat the guests you invite to the library and turn them into books. You burn these books to obtain books and pages, which are equipped in bookshelves of your librarians and serves as your characters' decks and are used to defeat enemies. You can also use books to invite stronger enemies which in turn grants you stronger books and pages.For a game that is still in development, this is one of the most beautiful experiences I have had in several years, with stunning artwork, great voice acting and an active set of developers who updates the game every single week with new content or bugfixes. The game currently has more hours of gameplay than most Triple-A games, and have hundreds of cards to collect. With the constant touches and hotfixes, the game is a constantly growing experience.The biggest flaw of the game will have to be the underdeveloped Tutorials. The game starts with four large walls of images and text that tries to explain everything at once, and will cause most players to become overwhelmed with information instead of spreading out the tutorials, and a lot of the finer points of the game is left to the players to figure out themselves.

candidates.title: Library Of Ruina review
candidates.text: Having played this game all through early access I can confidently say that Project Moon has done it again. Library of Ruina is the sequel to Lobotomy Corporation and is a expansion to the Project Moon universe. With Library of Ruina is a deck builder with great gameplay and variety in how battles can be approached, the difficulty ramps up steadily but the game always makes sure you have the books to progress. I highly recommend this game for people who have already played Lobotomy Corporation, are fans of or are looking to get into deck builders.

I eventually caved and bought it last month and I'll admit that I was a little let down, but I think that was because I got my own expectations too high.The game is good. Its a point-and-click style game and the controls do take a little time to get a hold of. But it just didn't really work out for me. It took me a while to really understand what was happening and even after I did, it felt like it was a bit of a chore to play. The plot was good and unsettling and the art was as good as it looked on the surface. But in the end, its a game and I wanted to have fun and after playing for a short while, I realized that I wasn't going to have fun. World of Horror is clearly a niche game. I'm absolutely certain that there are going to be thousands who will love this game, but its not for me. Its a slow and complex game. If that sounds like something you'd be interested in, I'd say go for it. Its at least worth a try. But if that's not your style, I say avoid it at all costs.

Em algumas partes ele te dá uma sensação de mistério e incomodo com algumas cenas gores e pesadas que por sinal, são incriveis. O meu maior contra nesse jogo é o fator SORTE estupido que esse jogo tem e mesmo saindo do acesso antecipado pelo visto os criadores ainda continuam gostando disso, e pelo visto, o DOOM também. Basicamente, quando você faz sua progressão explorando o cenário ou dando continuidade as história para zerar, você é interrompido com um 'quadro' do que pode acontecer com você no meio da exploração..ideia legal não é? sim, se não fosse interrompido pelo fator sorte, vou lhe dar um exemplo: Você está a horas jogando o jogo e fazendo sua exploração, com pouco hp ou sanidade e decide apenas dar o próximo passo para finalizar o capitulo, quando você é parado por um 'quadro' que não tem certo ou errado, você cruza os dedos e mesmo assim morre, pelo fator rng. Chato, não? Outra mecanica porca é o DOOM, toda vez que você começa o seu jogo ele vai estar na porcentagem de 0% e a cada ação, rng falhado ou até mesmo descansar aumenta ele e quando se atinge os 100% seu mundo é dominado pela escuridão e você dá game over, pensando assim até que parece algo interessante, mas no fim apenas te impede de realmente usufruir da própria exploração do jogo.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: Disclaimer up front: this game gets more of a neutral opinion than a negative one, the reason I didn't choose to go neutral positive is due to my disappointment after seeing that trailers do not accurately represent actual gameplay. I was very hyped about World of Horror at first glance, the art is beautiful and the Junji Ito/Lovecraft inspirations are very appealing to me, however going into the game after seeing the animated trailers had me expecting an entirely different experience. What I had hoped for and expected was a more classic point and click adventure style game a la Detention, my Halloween purchase from last year, with environments to explore and puzzles to solve. What World of Horror does instead is entirely menu based gameplay where you select different locations in town to roll random encounters on until you reach certain goals within your current mystery, and then after a few mysteries you get to go to the lighthouse and fight a boss. The game isn't bad by any means but I definitely felt heavily mislead and regretted not looking at gameplay on youtube first.As far as what the game does well, the roguelike elements are certainly interesting with a slew of random world effects from different Old Ones, abilities and various debuffs for different characters and events, and a moderate variety of random encounters per location. You might have your character start with a passive ability that encourages collecting npc allies but an old god that reduces your long term DOOM timer so whether or not to spend the extra time to make friends becomes a tough decision. Unfortunately that depth does not extend as much into combat as most encounters I've come across just came down to repeatedly preparing and then launching attacks without much need for any other combat maneuvers. I can't stress enough that the art and just general vibes here are amazing but the gameplay itself really doesn't support it enough for me to recommend despite how much I wanted to like this game.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: Incredibly fun game for its scope, with an impressive visual style and simple but great gameplay. You play as one investigator (up to 14 that you can unlock and choose) trying to stop the end of the world. Its "1 bit" (which can be changed to 2 bit, which I turned on very early and have not turned off since since I wouldn't want the game to look slightly worse) style is impressive, and its art was made in a way that impresses and amazes you with the limited effects that it uses. This game is very clearly inspired by horror artists such as Junji Ito and it shows. I don't think that I've seen another game that captures the uneasiness and terrifying feeling and art that his work gives off...I said all that and yet this is a negative review. This is because its developer is prone to disappearing for months on end. Specified dates were broken again and again on when an update would release. I've never seen a game where people were wondering where its developer went so much that the publisher had to come out and say that they were alive to calm people down before.As of today, July 7th 2024, the last dev update that we received was on the February 27th, talking about game merch and future updates, one of which was supposed to come out on March. March has come and gone and nothing still. I know that it'll eventually get that update and some more probably but to have had situations like that happening and without an official explanation CONSTANTLY is not a good look at all. I've seen many comments of people accusing the dev of taking their money and running since something was promised and it took so long to get an update on it (which is happening again now). When this game was launched on steam in early 2020 on early access it was originally slated to release in late 2020... That did not happen.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: World of Horror is a charming, horror-themed rogue-like game that will certainly resonate with many players. But it's the kind of game where all your mistakes add up, RNG takes a dump on you, and you're never sure where you went wrong exactly but you'll lose and walk away empty-handed most of the time. If a game is going to be this difficult (and boy is it mean), a random unlockable or unlockable currency at the game's end would have made it more accessible and less frustrating than fixed achievements.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: While World of Horror is very fun and I absolutely do recommend it, you should really know what you're getting into before buying it. This game is extremely unorthodox as an RPG when compared to most modern games and this can either be a really fun and bizarre experience or really disappointing depending on who you are.World of Horror is a point and click adventure game which is stylized in both its artstyle and gameplay to emulate old school RPG titles. This means that, while there is combat, it can be very RNG based. While there are branching paths and you do, generally speaking, have some freedom, the game can be extremely linear if you do not fully understand how to venture off the beaten path. While you can make your own decisions, there is an extremely high chance that they will go completely haywire in the most unexpected way which can make the game feel somewhat unfair at times; but this all comes with the territory because World of Horror doesn't try whatsoever to be a modern game.To a lot of people this can be a big letdown as they saw the really cool artstyle and themes which the game presents only to buy it and be disappointed because they did not fully understand what the game really was.I fully recommend World of Horror, it's a campy, weird RPG with a lot of endings and bizarre stuff in it. But before you buy it and give it a negative review because you didn't fully understand how the game works please take a deeper look into the gameplay mechanics first because this game surely isn't for everybody.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: Please disregard all the people complaining about the developers. They did not take the money and run, they did not abandon the game, and it's not just on life support. World of Horror has gotten a major content update every 9~ months since I bought in. Bug fixes are more common. I find the soundtrack to be amazing. The art style is top notch. Mod support is spectacular (cannot say the same about all the mods, but there are some gems). There are secrets and game play mechanics that I'm still discovering, and every run feels challenging and unique.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: "World of Horror" là một game kinh dị do nhà phát triển khối pixel nhỏ hãng Ysbryd Games phát hành. Game này kết hợp yếu tố phiêu lưu và trò chơi nhập vai, với một phong cách nghệ thuật đặc trưng hướng đến phong cách retro của các game máy tính cá nhân từ thập niên 1980.World of Horror có một phong cách nghệ thuật độc đáo, sử dụng pixel art và màu sắc hạn chế để tạo cảm giác bí ẩn và rùng rợn. Âm nhạc cũng rất phù hợp, với nhạc nền huyền bí và sử dụng hiệu ứng âm thanh để tăng thêm sự ám ảnh.World of Horror mang đến cho người chơi một câu chuyện phức tạp với nhiều kết thúc khác nhau, mỗi lần chơi lại mang đến những trải nghiệm khác nhau. Người chơi sẽ phải khám phá và giải quyết các bí ẩn, thử thách từ những sự kiện kinh dị. World of Horror có mức độ khó khăn cao, yêu cầu người chơi phải có chiến thuật và sự thông minh để vượt qua các thử thách. Các quyết định của người chơi ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến kết quả cuối cùng.World of Horror là một tựa game kinh dị đáng chơi đối với những ai yêu thích phong cách retro và tìm kiếm một trải nghiệm game kinh dị độc đáo. Với sự kết hợp giữa nghệ thuật, âm nhạc và yếu tố gameplay sâu sắc, nó mang đến cho người chơi những giây phút thử thách và rùng rợn.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: While this game is decent visually, has excellent music, and has a lot of weird, interesting things in it, it doesn't do anything with what is has.There's a lot of minor complaints I could level with the game but generally I have to say that time should have been taken to figure out what would be enjoyable to play for a mystery, and how to turn that into a basic system that can work for most ideas. If not that, then proper time should have been taken to flesh out each individual mystery and it's consequences on your character's life.I wanted to see something like, how does a school like theirs function if you can stumble upon a body in a pool, or a locker can bite you? How is the populace responding to their kids going missing, whether by the many dozens of monsters filling the game, or by the player outright killing them? How do people deal with the black sludge coming out of their pipes, or people going crazy from the nightmarish ♥♥♥♥ they're encountering? What are the people doing?The game doesn't address it. Instead the whole world exists in a state of limbo where no one knows what's happening but has a vague idea things are off, right up until you run out of time and the world ends. It's like being forever stuck right at the beginning of a horror story, despite some cataclysmic ♥♥♥♥ happening in some. There badly needs to be some connection between the player and the characters in the world, and they almost do that with the player's neighbor, but that exists for only one mystery and really only in passing. The world instead feels like a cardboard cutout of horror media.So much of the game starts interesting, but the follow-through simply isn't there. I get the sense with every mystery that the developer had some ideas, drew them out, left some room to add stuff later, and never went back.

candidates.title: eFootball™ review
candidates.text: Don't let the half hour of playtime I have here tell you about my experience with this game... actually perhaps it should.I've played this a lot more on PS5, thinking it might look or play better but no...Visuals are by-and-large atrocious. Player likenesses are alright, lighting and stadiums are not bad and many of the new cinematic pre-game cutscenes are nice, but that's about it. Grass looks terrible, crowds look terrible, and the presentation is awful (bold blue and bright yellow is everywhere, why?!).The gameplay is also poor. There's some nice ideas in there, but they're all thrown away by bad implementation. An example being; Shielding, new mechanic but it's totally broken and looks unnatural. Passing is slow and methodical, which is nice as a full-manual PES player, but the ball feels like a bowling ball, and passes can very easily be wildly under or over-hit by the same player. The game lacks any responsiveness too, it feels like playing PES Online to me, with a big delay between making the command and seeing the action.Collisions between players are broken right now; they'll often get stuck, get dragged around by invisible magic powers, get caught or just glitched. This plays into the referees too, which will or won't give crazy decisions with this awful collision system.Adding to that, animations are mostly borrowed from PES, but the new ones are janky, and don't add anything worthwhile at all. It's good to have some weight about the players, but none of this feels natural or realistic.Basic stuff like difficulties and match-times aren't properly implemented yet. Regular difficulty, or SuperStar difficulty, no inbetween. 5 minutes match-times only.

candidates.title: Lightyear Frontier review
candidates.text: Pros: The graphics are nice The game has crafting-from-storage (as it rightfully should)Cons: No tutorial to speak of No fast travel system. It can take you 4 minutes to run to a place, then your inventory will probably be full and you'll then move slower due to over-encumbrance, so it will take you 6 minutes to walk back... so you can easily waste 10 minutes on every trip, where as a fast travel system would quickly fix the issue with this game being a at its core. It's far, far too difficult to see if a crop has been watered or not. The game has some incredibly obtuse and unrealistic progression gates in place, such as requiring you to spray water onto noxious sludge from an instead of a regular hose. There is NO difference in the water being sprayed from a regular hose vs. an upgraded hose, yet the devs require you to have an upgraded hose, or else the water that you're spraying doesn't even affect the noxious sludge on the ground. I don't mind progression gating, but when it's just lazy, the player immediately loses interest. Your dwarf, or your mech can't even touch knee-deep water, then you die. The auto-loot range, is very tiny. You basically have to walk through the resources to pick it up. The game is for sale in ruzzia and izraelUntil the devs implement a fast travel system, this game will never be enjoyable. It's really as simple as that... unless they WANT their game to be a walking simulator, in which case, they're doing an amazing job here.For more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:

candidates.title: Hero's Hour review
candidates.text: I don't often write reviews for games, it's just not something I seek out. I did feel it was worth speaking up in this case though. Hero's Hour is a good game. It's fun and has a ton of potential, but that's the problem. While the game has incredible potential, it's still a long way off from being what it promised to be. And that's fine, these things take time. Games are hard to make, and at times it can be a thankless job, so normally I give the benefit of the doubt to developers that are working hard to polish and improve on what they've made.Releasing a paid DLC for what boils down to a new faction, a few new units and skills, and some maps when the game still doesn't even have a single player campaign or story mode of any kind is more than a little rough. Other people have already mentioned the issues with the Bodyguard skill as well, but the issues are more widespread than just reworking that one skill. The meta of Hero's Hour is almost entirely limited to snowballing. Build your big bad hero with all the power ups and units you can cram into it and overwhelm whatever else is out there. There's very little encouragement to use other heroes for much else beyond scouting and collecting resources.These are all issues that could easily be overlooked for a game that's still more or less in it's infancy, but releasing DLC for a game before the core gameplay is finished is somewhat disingenuous. I have almost 100 hours in this game, I really do enjoy it. It's fun, colorful, and has a good depth of mechanics with each faction having somewhat different play styles. It's a good foundation to build something amazing, and I still hope that's what will happen.

candidates.title: Age of Empires IV: Anniversary Edition review
candidates.text: It has the potential to be amazing. But right now I wouldn't buy it especially at this price (SGD 80). There's a lot of gameplay bugs and performance issues and the game feels empty. I played the beta, and unfortunately not much has improved since then, so I don't have high hopes that it'll improve going forward.Some things are great: - Large battles with siege and walls are amazing - Sacred site victory works well - Some of the civ-specific mechanics good - The changes to relics are good - Placing units on walls is coolThe game performs like hot garbage. But I don't mind lowering my settings a bit. Issue is - the low graphics settings are outright broken. If you don't set (and meet) a framerate cap, the game hitches so badly it is unplayable. If you lower the resolution scale, unit healthbars disappear somehow. Shadow acne on the entire terrain. Trees pop in as you pan the camera. Performance issues are especially bad on water maps.But even the performance issues I can ignore. There are numerous gameplay bugs and missing essential features that make the game unplayable for me.Some examples: - Often, I accidentally discover enemy positions when I attempt to place a wall or building in the fog of war. It fails if there's an enemy there. You can absolutely cheat this way. - Often, I see flickers of building in the fog of war, or hear sounds of units marching. - A very large number of upgrades and abilities don't do what they say they do. e.g. Mongol move speed ability says +50%, but is actually +125%. - In team games, you can rush a wonder unreasonably fast. - No ranked matches. No penalty for leaving games. Many team games are ruined by leavers. - The camera is too zoomed in.

candidates.title: Valheim review
candidates.text: The game is honestly a bit of a drag. Perhaps it gets better late game, but I could not justify continuing to drag myself through the progression to get there. This game has a lot of things that I like; the art style, the overall aesthetic, character design, combat, building mechanics. But it all gets held back by unnecessary systems (like the inability to transport metal through portals) which just create artificial padding and difficulty. A big one is the fact that the game has a very specific progression that it wants you to take through its various environments. This already isn't ideal for an open world procgen game, but it can be done well. Valheim does not do it well. What actually ends up happening is you walk around, exploring and looking for resources (as one does in these sorts of games), and end up walking into a new environment where every enemy one shots you. This doesn't feel good, especially when these environments often end up completely blocking your path in one direction, forcing you to turn around. Perhaps my opinion on this is unpopular, but I feel that a mechanic which actively discourages and restricts exploration in a procgen open world game should not be in that game.

candidates.title: Rec Room review
candidates.text: It pains me to write this, but Rec Room has gone from one of the best games for VR to a train wreck by appealing to the lowest common denominator. What used to be a game with a great community and social interaction has become a toxic mess with an utterly broken moderation system. The issues with moderation and the decision to merge teleport players and walking players has just made the game unplayable. It's impossible to join a game and not have a player complain about another player's locomotion method, which generally devolves in to name calling and the kicking of one or more players by mob rule. It isn't fun playing a game where every round is a shouting match. And yes, we're all aware that there are VR specific rooms. They don't help if they're empty, which they virtually always are. So, join, play, and deal with the constant toxicity, or watch the tumbleweeds roll by.

candidates.title: Wingspan review

You see each player's game board individually. When playing with AI, you cannot easily track who gained what food, who drew what cards, so strategizing isn't what it should be. No, having a speech-bubble overview for what each player did on their turn is not sufficient.

candidates.text: The way the play mechanics of this game plays out is very lackluster. The pathing mechanics are very confusing and the wall to wall combat mechanics feels like a trainwreck. It feels like they tried to implement turn-based strategy mechanics into a RTS style game, which is a great concept in theory but I do not feel like they accomplished it properly with this variation of it.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: While this game is decent visually, has excellent music, and has a lot of weird, interesting things in it, it doesn't do anything with what is has.There's a lot of minor complaints I could level with the game but generally I have to say that time should have been taken to figure out what would be enjoyable to play for a mystery, and how to turn that into a basic system that can work for most ideas. If not that, then proper time should have been taken to flesh out each individual mystery and it's consequences on your character's life.I wanted to see something like, how does a school like theirs function if you can stumble upon a body in a pool, or a locker can bite you? How is the populace responding to their kids going missing, whether by the many dozens of monsters filling the game, or by the player outright killing them? How do people deal with the black sludge coming out of their pipes, or people going crazy from the nightmarish ♥♥♥♥ they're encountering? What are the people doing?The game doesn't address it. Instead the whole world exists in a state of limbo where no one knows what's happening but has a vague idea things are off, right up until you run out of time and the world ends. It's like being forever stuck right at the beginning of a horror story, despite some cataclysmic ♥♥♥♥ happening in some. There badly needs to be some connection between the player and the characters in the world, and they almost do that with the player's neighbor, but that exists for only one mystery and really only in passing. The world instead feels like a cardboard cutout of horror media.So much of the game starts interesting, but the follow-through simply isn't there. I get the sense with every mystery that the developer had some ideas, drew them out, left some room to add stuff later, and never went back.

candidates.title: Édouard "Templar" Couteau
candidates.text:
Templar takes heavy inspiration from the Predator (fictional species) Predator species from the franchise baring its Predator (franchise) namesake.
The design of his mask takes inspiration from the original visor design worn by the Predator in the Predator (film) 1987 film.
Both collect trophies from victorious hunts.
After he stabs Ghost and takes his mask, he says "That's one less loose end". This is a reference to an iconic quote from General Shepherd at the end of the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 mission, Loose Ends.
Templar is later betrayed by Ghost in a very similar manner to how Shepherd originally betrayed Ghost and Roach in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2. Both were carrying wounded teammates, asked if they had a DSM, and they were both shot. Unlike Ghost and Roach however, Templar did survive (though his teammate, Vagir Modir, did not.)
Templar's Royal Knight uniform has the Five Knights' logo printed on his cape.
Despite his apparent membership in The Five Knights, he appears to be a gun for hire, as evidenced by his interactions with Dame as well as Gabriel Rorke, who heads the mercs.
Although the AS VAL - Double Edge Mythic blueprint is noted to be one of Templar's weapons, even mentioning him in the blueprint description, he is never seen in the comics using it.
Templar's last name, “Couteau”, translates to "knife" in French.
This is reflected in Templar's skills with the knife in general.

Stansfield was like a father to Templar and he spilled much blood for them.

He goes on to state that he has made many mistakes in his life and is not a good man, but he wishes to give his daughter a better life, the one he never had. Ghost says that they will save her, together, and hunt down the Dark Covenant together as well.

candidates.title: Heroes (Darkest Dungeon)
candidates.text:
Heroes, or Adventurers, in Darkest Dungeon are characters used by the player when assembling parties and expeditions to explore dungeons. They are divided into several classes, specializations that define their appearance and abilities. Each character has different skills and can fill different roles in combat. Each class also has unique barks as a reaction to many situations. Different heroes from the same class have the same base stats and can access the same skills; they differ by what they have learned and (more importantly) what quirks they have.

Characters are available to be recruited free of charge through the Stage Coach, where they are generated with a random name, set of quirks, and class. Pre-made Heroes are also available.

candidates.title: Load Screen Messages
candidates.text:
Can’t decide whether to carry an assault rifle or a shotgun? ¿Por qué no los dos? Every Vladof gun comes with an attached underbarrel weapon for added versatility. It’s like a gun for your gun!
COV guns are engine-driven, and have to be started before they can be fired. Don’t even ask about the gas mileage.
Dahl prides itself on offering better accuracy and recoil than any other manufacturer. Dependability. Double tap. Dahl.
Dahl weapons all feature two of three possible firing modes: single, burst, and full-auto fire. Each has different zoom distances as well, so pick the mode that’s right for the fight!
Got a Tediore gun? When you’re done with your mag, don’t waste time reloading - just throw it at an enemy and a new gun will digistruct right in your hand.
Hyperion guns project a shield when you aim down sights and grow more accurate as you fire, so you can line up the perfect shot from safety and comfort.
Hyperion weapons grow more accurate and handle better with sustained fire, so you have no one to blame but yourself if you miss.
Jakobs guns reward marksmanship with special effects whenever you score a Critical Hit. If you want to be a rootin’, tootin’, sharpshootin’ cowboy, get a Jakobs. And a hat.
Maliwan weapons all come with a bonus to the “Cool” stat. They don’t say that anywhere, though, because if you say you’re Cool, you are totally NOT Cool.
Maliwan weapons have to be charged before firing. Plan accordingly!
Too much ammo and not enough time? Get a Vladof: They boast a higher fire rate than any other manufacturer.

candidates.title: Manufacturer
candidates.text:
In the character info tab, behind the character is the logo of a "favorite manufacturer". This means that the character has fired the most bullets from that specific manufacturer.

Class mods, grenade mods, shields and Action Skills do not affect this. Therefore, it is impossible to get Anshin or Pangolin as a favorite manufacturer.

Most Outrunner-weapons, including those from The Secret Armory of General Knoxx, and the Mulciber Mk2 are considered Tediore-weapons. The only exceptions on this rule are the Blast and Mine seat from the Lancer, which are manufactured by Atlas.

Multipliers such as on a Double Anarchy or a shotgun do not assist in bullet-count. Firing a Dahl Shotgun once only counts as one bullet for Dahl.

candidates.title: Submachine Gun/parts
candidates.text:
Unlike other parts, the accessory part does not have a consistent effect on a weapon's attributes:
some accessories boost tech, some alter recoil, some increase damage.
Some accessories grant a special property to the weapon, Elemental Damage, beyond mere attribute modification;
furthermore, almost all accessories make their weapon eligible for a special name prefix or title describing the weapon's altered behavior,
such as "Relentlesss" or "Double."

Most accessories are easy to differentiate visually. Most of them appear behind the receiver, immediately in the player's view in first-person perspective,
though two (acc1_Relentless and acc2_Ruthless) appear under the barrel similar to a pistol accessory.

PartImage acc1_Relentless acc2_Ruthless acc2_Vector acc3_Corrosiveacc3_Shock acc4_Double acc5_Explosiveacc5_Incendiary

An accessory may or may not be present on any given submachine gun, and no more than a single accessory may be present,
which is why the game will never spawn, for example, a legendary Double Hellfire.

candidates.text: Also known as Alt-Fire, underbarrel attachments allow guns that would not normally have alternative functions to utilize them.

candidates.title: Borderlands 3
candidates.text: There are two new weapon manufacturers: COV (which replaces the Bandits from Borderlands 2 and Scavs from Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel) and Atlas (returning from the original Borderlands). Alternate-fire modes on many weapons, ranging from under-barrel attachments to dual weapon elements and more. Most are limited to a few manufacturers: Maliwan, Vladof, Dahl, Atlas, and Torgue. Manufacturers without an alternate-fire mode instead feature additional perks, such as front-facing shields while scoped (Hyperion) and varying reload-throw modules (Tediore). This is limited to Hyperion, Jakobs, Tediore and COV. Manufacturers now create their own gun parts, causing all guns to have unique parts based on their weapon class and manufacturer. Common gun names are separated by their type of unique barrel (in comparison to Borderlands 2 and The Pre-Sequel, which named their guns based on the manufacturer of the barrel). All weapon classes have 3-4 variants, as opposed to potentially more with all compatible manufacturers. All weapons have a listed "rating" at the top left of their item card, showing their overall effectiveness when compared to other weapons. While they can be somewhat inaccurate, this allows players to quickly gauge the strength of a weapon at a glance. Weapons of higher grades will feature longer and more noticeable beams of light while on the ground, with those of purple and legendary rarities giving unique chimes to signify an extremely rare drop. E-tech weapons have been replaced by a unique "Eridian-merged" alien barrel attached to various weapons, which causes guns to use additional ammo for guaranteed elemental damage and special effects such as a continuous laser, bouncing shots or a chain-lightning elemental ball. Legendary drop rates have been heavily increased.

candidates.title: Borderlands 2 Weapons
candidates.text: They have racing-themed color schemes that increase in detail with increasing rarity. Unlike in Borderlands, Torgue does not produce sniper rifles or submachine guns. Vladof : Vladof weapons are known best for their high rates of fire and no obvious downside. They have a "revolutionary" theme (Glorious, Worker's, etc) and appear similar to Russian/Soviet Cold War-era hardware, with parts based on actual Russian weapons and equipment as well as slavic imagery on some parts of the guns. Higher-rarity Vladof weapons are all-metal and highly polished in appearance. When aiming a sniper you can also read Russian numbers in it regarding height and wind.

candidates.title: Borderlands 3
candidates.text:
Borderlands 3 Weapons

As in previous games, guns are generated with a procedural algorithm. However, unlike in previous installments of the franchise, there is no more mixing of manufacturers' parts. Instead, each manufacturer has multiple variants for each part of a given type of weapon. In addition to this new system, manufacturers have additional gimmicks associated with their products. Grenades use a new parts system as well, as do shields, allowing for much greater variety in both.

candidates.title: Alien Barrel Weapons
candidates.text:
Alien Barrel Weapons are a type of weapon featured in Borderlands 3, featuring a creepy, living-being barrel. Similar to E-tech weapons in Borderlands 2, each type of Alien Barrel Weapon has their own, unique characteristics, always elemental, and consumes extra ammo per shot. Unlike E-tech weapons, they don't come with a unique rarity: Instead, they occur as rare, epic, or legendary. Alien Barrel Weapons may come with sharp shells and spikes as barrel accessories, which also have unique characteristics. Rare alien barrel weapons will not have a barrel accessory, while Epic variants will always have one.

Most manufacturers have their own Alien Barrel Weapon set, except for Atlas and Jakobs. Jakobs, however, manufactures a variety of legendary Alien Barrel Weapons. Atlas is the only weapon manufacturer that does not manufacture Alien Barrel Weapons. Despite having similar appearances, alien barrels for different manufacturers have different effects. Most of them may come with an exclusive barrel accessory.

Enemies (mostly Children of the Vault, and Bonded) may also use Alien Barrel Weapons against Vault Hunters. Crimson Raiders can also carry Alien Barrel Weapons.

candidates.title: Combat Rifle/parts
candidates.text:
As with all weapons in Borderlands, the grip does not affect any of the combat rifle's attributes. Each grip design is specific to the weapon's manufacturer, therefore each combat rifle or machine gun of the same manufacturer will have the same grip.
