candidates.title: Borderlands 4 Gameplay Showcase
candidates.text:
You can also see the destructive power of some deadly weapons from Borderlands 4's eight unique manufacturers: Order, Ripper, Daedalus, Tediore, Maliwan, Jakobs, Vladof, and Torgue, each boasting their own devastating strengths. Longtime Borderlands fans will notice that three of these manufacturers are brand new, with fresh characteristics:

- Order guns focus on precision with high-powered bursts
- Ripper guns charge up to go fully automatic
- Daedalus guns are easy-to-use and incorporate multiple ammo types
- Tediore guns are reloaded by tossing them as grenades
- Maliwan guns specialize in elemental damage to burn, freeze, and shock
- Jakobs guns can fire bullets as fast as you can shoot with ricochets on critical hits
- Vladof guns have a high rate of fire and huge magazines
- Torgue guns have heavy-duty explosive rounds that can switch to sticky projectiles

With the new Licensed Parts system, you can find guns that incorporate the behaviors and abilities from multiple manufacturers into a single weapon, fueling our wildest loot variety yet. In addition, Borderlands 4 reworks the approach to the iconic Legendary guns that have unique effects you won't find on any other piece of gear. In Borderlands 3, Legendaries dropped too often, devaluing them and making other loot feel less special overall. In Borderlands 4's new system, not only do all guns feel great, but now Legendary drops will truly be special events.

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45157740/51cc33ecfa74a654c07bb8824f24d4603ce10a00.jpg

candidates.title: Weapons by prefix (Borderlands 2 & Pre-Sequel)
candidates.text:
Certain titles of weapons also have special prefixes that will override the grip prefix, but be overridden by the elemental or accessory prefix, e.g. a Dahl Minigun will always have the "Nonuple" prefix if it does not spawn with an element or an accessory. Note that this does not necessarily apply to unique weapons of the same body and barrel manufacturer. For example, Bandit Room Clener shotguns have the special prefix "Threpul" which overrides the grip prefix, while the unique Jolly Roger can occur with an ordinary grip prefix such as "bandity." The same is not true of all unique weapons; for example, the RokSalt may occur with the prefix "Duble Bareld," which is the special prefix of generic Stret Sweper shotguns.

Gemstone-rarity weapons will always apply their manufacturer prefix, overriding all others.
Bandit - Quartz
Dahl - Emerald
Hyperion - Diamond
Jakobs - Citrine
Maliwan - Aquamarine
Tediore - Cubic Zerconia
Torgue - Rock
Vladof - Garnet

Laser weapons added in Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel use their own naming system, separate from what is described above.

candidates.title: Borderlands 4 Parts System
candidates.text:
All items can have up to 3 slots for parts, depending on item type and rarity.
If a weapon or grenade shows 4 slots, the 4th one is its default trait (not a part slot).
Legendary parts take up 1 slot; legendary quality does not add capacity.
Higher rarity does not necessarily mean all part slots will be filled. The number of parts possible is simply the maximum.

Guns can have up to 3 slots for Licensed Parts or Underbarrel Attachments, depending on their rarity.
RarityMax. # of PartsCommon0Uncommon1Rare2Epic3Legendary2 + 1 Legendary part

Note that the above table is for guns only. The relationship between rarity and parts works differently for ordnance, shields, and repkits.

candidates.title: Manufacturer
candidates.text:
There are twelve official manufacturers in Borderlands, each with their own characteristics and trademarks. The manufacturers produce all of the offensive and defensive equipment encountered throughout the game. Each manufacturer also classifies weapons based on their strength which can be seen here.

Two of the manufacturers, Anshin and Pangolin, do not produce projectile weapons.

candidates.title: Borderlands 4 Parts System
candidates.text:
Underbarrel attachments cannot appear on guns if their manufacturers differ (e.g, Jakobs underbarrel attachments can't appear on Tediore guns and vice versa).
The only exceptions are manufacturer-specific parts that have a Licensed Part as its prefix: Atlas, Daedalus, & Maliwan.
Maliwan guns may spawn with different attachments, disabling their element-switching function.

candidates.title: Rocket Launcher
candidates.text:
Vladof heavy weapons are shouldered large-caliber, full-automatic anti-material rifles that shoot projectiles that is reasonably fast and modestly accurate over long distances. The projectiles are not as destructive as missiles but they compensate by having large magazine capacity and underbarrel attachments. They also has small or none splash damage radius.

Vladof heavy weapons come in three main varieties according to their underbarrel attachment:

Rocket tubes that will fire a small barrage of missiles.
A mortar capable of blanketing an area with explosives lobbed in an arcing/parabolic trajectory.
A "big boy rocket" with a wide blast radius.

There is a fourth variant featuring an alien barrel and no underbarrel attachment. In this variant, the large caliber projectile is replaced by a highly accurate energy pulse.

question: What are the inscriptions on the Hellbombs in HELLDIVERS™ 2, and what do they mean?

candidates.title: Super Earth calls for devotees with the latest Warbond: Servants of Freedom!
candidates.text:
Let’s be honest, Helldivers: Super Earth is worth it. No matter what “it” is. All Helldivers share this same belief, and fanatical loyalty is expected from all citizens of Super Earth. But the Helldivers need to demonstrate their allegiance. They need to look like the democratic disciples they are inside, and the only way we know to properly show it off is with the gear from our next Warbond*: Servants of Freedom.

[previewyoutube=7s2Es5g7fwA;full][/previewyoutube]

So what does true devotion to Democracy look like?

Hellbombs. It looks like Hellbombs. They really send a message: liberation is big, loud, and happening all around you. It gets the spirit of democracy soaring, and gets a lot of other things soaring, too, like buildings. Bile Titans. Automaton industrial sites. Now, imagine you’ve got that kind of freedom strapped to your back. That’s the B-100 Portable Hellbomb, a beacon of democratic truth in a convenient backpack format, which can be easily activated by you or a helpful teammate. Just be sure to drop the pack and clear the area once it's active, because the B-100’s got a 10 second countdown that can’t be canceled.

How do you make the Sickle do more? Overclock it and bring some heat. The LAS-17 Double-Edge Sickle is pure agony meets ecstasy as it starts to burn the wielder as well as everything in its path. Shoot through the pain, Helldiver.

To help you spread liberty around, you could equip the GP-20 Ultimatum–a front-loading grenade pistol for your secondary slot. The Ultimatum packs a punch like a grenade launcher on steroids, designed for closer range use. But handle it with care, or you might accidentally liberate yourself along with the enemy.

candidates.title: Major Orders
candidates.text: Additionally, a public relations campaign is being launched to remind our citizens that they are protected by the Galaxy's greatest fighting force. In support, the Helldivers are ordered to kill the enemies of Freedom that arise most frequently in citizen nightmares (list to follow). This mission is of utmost importance. It is imperative that our citizens' faith in the ability of Super Earth to protect them remains unshakeable. Arsenal Augmentation: The just decimation of the Voteless Fleshmobs by the Helldivers has inspired a boost in citizen War Bond purchases. High Command has authorized the temporary addition of the Recoilless Rifle Stratagem to all Helldiver loadouts for the next 24 hours. Remembrance Name Decided: The Super Earth Mega City of Remembrance, tragically destroyed by the Illuminate during the Battle for Super Earth, is being rebuilt. Following a Democratically Managed voting process, the new Mega City has been officially named Gun. This patriotic and glorious appellation will ensure that Remembrance will never be forgotten. Arsenal Augmentation: Righteous and furious extermination of Terminid Shriekers by the Helldivers has spurred our citizens to new heights of patriotic generosity. As a result, High Command has authorized the temporary addition of the Autocannon Stratagem to all Helldiver loadouts for the next 24 hours. Strategic Opportunity Seized: The Helldivers have successfully exterminated 5,000,000 Spore Burst Warriors on Fori Prime through effective employment of the Stalwart. A spike in citizen donations to the War Fund has made possible the short-term addition of the Orbital Railcannon Strike Stratagem to all Helldiver arsenals for the remainder of the current order. candidates.title: NUX-223 Hellbomb
candidates.text:
The Damaged Hellbomb is unexploded ordnance which can occasionally be found during missions. Shooting it will activate the Hellbomb, and it will explode a few seconds later. Damaged Hellbomb Description

Damaged Hellbombs are NUX-223s that appear to have been dropped from orbit, but failed to detonate for whatever reason. Despite this, these Hellbombs are armed and are primed to go off at the slightest provocation. The bomb's yield is not diminished in any capacity, and will still obliterate anything within 25m of the explosion.

Small-arms fire will result in triggering a detonation after a 3-second delay, indicated by a puff of fire and spark from the bomb. Most anti-armor weapons and explosives will cause them to explode instantly on hit.

Enemies attacking or stepping on them (atleast in the case of superheavy enemies like the Bile Titan), will also set them off. Hence it is not recommended for to start a firefight near an unexploded Hellbomb, without expectations of imminent martyrdom. Alternatively, it may be favorable instead, to lead large groups of enemies near an unexploded Hellbomb to take them out in a single strike.

candidates.title: NUX-223 Hellbomb
candidates.text: Hellbombs are able to be called in in order to take out heavily armored or massive structures such as Gunship Facilities and Shrieker Nests. They can also be called down for the destruction of a Rogue Research Station. Hellbombs have a short cooldown period of 20 seconds, but this period is universal. This means that if one teammate calls down a Hellbomb, other teammates may not call down another one until after 20 seconds. This can be particularly problematic with squads accomplishing separate objectives around the map, without proper coordination. Hellbombs are highly destructive and have a big radius of effect of 25m, anything within this radius is destroyed and it goes through walls. Run away as soon as it's armed and maintain a distance of atleast 45m. Going prone also mitigates potential unintended loss of life. Due to budget restraints, Hellbombs need to be manually armed with a 6 input code. One person should arm while the others defend from the onslaught. All friendlies in range will have 10 seconds to escape the blast or be turned into red mist. Damaged Hellbombs can be found across the landscape. Use this to your advantage by leading big hordes or heavy units into them; just don’t stand too close. Sometimes, enemies are found idling around the malfunctioning Hellbombs. Use this to your advantage as well. A particularly devious trick involving damaged Hellbombs is to lure enemies to them, then place a Tesla Tower right behind it as they are chasing you. Either the Tower will hit the bomb and set it off when enemies get within its range, or enemies will inevitably end up triggering the bomb on their own as they try to destroy the Tesla Tower. Shooting these damaged Hellbombs will cause it to break before detonating within 3 seconds. This gives the player a short time to retreat.

candidates.title: NUX-223 Hellbomb
candidates.text: Shooting these damaged Hellbombs will cause it to break before detonating within 3 seconds. This gives the player a short time to retreat. However, using explosives such as that from a GL-21 Grenade Launcher or EAT-17 Expendable Anti-Tank will cause a damaged Hellbomb to detonate immediately. Points of Interests have damaged Hellbombs with a writing which can be viewed. Some of these damaged Hellbombs have a support weapon lying on the ground near them. Recent adjustments to Hellbombs allow them to explode after destruction from enemy units. However, they only explode after the 8 digit code is entered. If destroyed beforehand, another Hellbomb will need to be called in its place. While the radius to call-in Hellbombs is limited, their deployment range is not. This means that one can request a Hellbomb near an objective, throw it elsewhere far away, and the Hellbomb will be deployed and ready to use regardless. Alternatively, one can request a Hellbomb, move around the map with the beacon ready to deploy, and it can be called down from anywhere, barring if it's covered by a Stratagem Jammer or Ion Storm. Enemies will prioritize attacking a Hellbomb if it's within their visual range, even if it's not armed. Caution should be exercised once it's armed during a fight, as enemies will still prioritize it, causing a premature detonation.

candidates.title: Biomes
candidates.text:
Arctic Biomes are, as the name indicates, extremely frigid planets that orbit a very distant start or receive barely enough light and heat from their star to be inhabitable. Arctic Biomes usually generate smoother terrain, albeit markedly having vastly more hills and elevation shifts than Sandy Biomes. However, these hilly terrains are also often interrupted by deep chasms, sinkholes, fjords, cliffs and rivers that will often be several meters below the floor level or will be too deep to be traversed on foot besides a few select crossing points that will appear on the map.

Besides these geographical features and the occasional ridge or mountain, the terrain itself is also dotted in ice stalagmites both big and small that will sometimes have undetonated Hellbombs encrusted into them far more frequently than on other planets. These Hellbombs will detonate shortly after being hit by gunfire, and will explode instantly if hit with explosives. While dangerous, these stray hellbombs can also be used during emergencies to take out pursuing enemy forces or even to destroy enemy ordnance and facilities should they be close enough.

candidates.title: Hive Lord
candidates.text: M-1000 Maxigun - Can be used to quickly wear down the inner flesh thanks to its high firerate. B-100 Portable Hellbomb / NUX-223 Hellbomb - Hellbombs deal 10,000 damage and have the highest demolition force in the game. They can be useful for both breaking the armor plates and damaging the inner flesh, as the explosion radius can hit most, if not all, of the flesh sections at once. It can take up to four Hellbombs to kill a Hive Lord reliably. The Portable Hellbomb stratagem is granted for free during Destroy Spore Lung missions but players can also try to use normal hellbombs if they happen to fight a Hive Lord close to a Shrieker Nest. Additionally, undetonated hellbombs can still be used against Hive Lords (even in Hive Worlds), though they are a rare sight and have limited usefulness unless you or a member of your team can reliably lure a Hive Lord into one of these. G-123 Thermite & G-48 Giga Grenade - These grenades both deal high anti-tank damage. With enough supplies nearby and competent throws, you can break a Hive Lord's armor with only 10 of either grenade. GR-8 Recoilless Rifle - Deals high anti-tank damage, allowing it to massively damage a Hive Lord's armor or even break it in just 7 shots in HEAT mode. When engaging a Hive Lord, it is recommended to focus anti-tank fire on one part of the exoskeleton as it will visually crack and eventually break to reveal the more vulnerable flesh underneath.

candidates.title: Biomes
candidates.text: Besides the Shrapnel Bushes and Geysers, Ashland biomes can generate undetonated hellbombs in any difficulty at a higher rate than normal. However, unlike in biomes such as the Glacial Fjords, these Hellbombs will often be strewn throughout the floor level instead of embedded on rocks or mountains, making them vastly more dangerous to operate vehicles or sentries around, as these Hellbombs will detonate shortly after being hit by gunfire, and will explode instantly if hit with explosives. Despite the obvious dangers posed by the unexploded ordnance, these stray hellbombs can also be used during emergencies to take out pursuing enemies or even destroy enemy equipment should they be close enough.

candidates.title: Hogwarts Legacy review
candidates.text: First and foremost, Hogwarts Legacy is a game for Harry Potter fans. It is gorgeous with a level of attention to detail that only fans of the books (more so than the movies) are likely to catch. Hogwarts itself is huge and spawling, and the world outside it even more so. Fundamentally however, there are missed opportunities here. Enemy variety is limited and only particularly challenging in the early game or in massive 10+ groups. Magical beasts and potions feel underutilized, serving only as resource nodes for gear upgrades and unnecessary temporary buffs respectively. Classes that ought to be a mainstay of student life are instead relegated to one-or-two time side quests instead of being repeatable. The world outside of Hogwards itself and Hogsmeade feels underdeveloped and empty, with lots of repeating "puzzles" to mark off a monstrous to-do list.Overall, Hogwarts Legacy plays like Skyrim or Breath of the Wild under a different IP. It definitely has room for improvement, but is nowhere near as bad as it could have been. Worth picking up on a sale, but only bother with full price if you're already a fan of HP.

candidates.title: Hogwarts Legacy review
candidates.text: Hogwarts Legacy é a realização dos sonhos de muitos fãs do universo de Harry Potter. Este RPG em mundo aberto nos leva ao coração de Hogwarts e do mundo mágico com uma liberdade e profundidade nunca antes experimentadas. Ambientado nos anos 1800, o jogo oferece uma experiência que é ao mesmo tempo nostálgica e renovadora, ideal tanto para os fãs de longa data quanto para aqueles que desejam explorar este mundo mágico pela primeira vez. Você joga como um novo aluno em Hogwarts, mas com um detalhe especial: seu personagem possui uma habilidade mágica rara que o coloca no centro de uma antiga conspiração. O enredo é envolvente e permite que você mergulhe na história da magia e nos mistérios de Hogwarts, enquanto aprende sobre a vida escolar e os perigos ocultos da época.A ambientação é fiel ao que os fãs esperam: uma Hogwarts ricamente detalhada, com todos os locais clássicos e muitos outros inéditos. Além do castelo, é possível explorar a vila de Hogsmeade, as florestas próximas, e diversas áreas icônicas que fazem do mundo bruxo uma experiência imersiva e mágica. Hogwarts Legacy traz um sistema de combate divertido e acessível, permitindo que você lance feitiços, crie combos e explore habilidades mágicas. Você pode personalizar seu arsenal de feitiços e enfrentar inimigos diversos, como bruxos das trevas, criaturas mágicas e outras ameaças. O combate é dinâmico e visualmente impressionante, com animações que refletem o poder e o impacto de cada feitiço.Além disso, o jogo incentiva o aprendizado de magias e habilidades conforme você avança na história, o que torna cada sessão uma oportunidade para expandir seu repertório mágico e desenvolver estratégias para enfrentar desafios mais complexos. O jogo oferece opções de personalização completas, desde a aparência do seu personagem até suas escolhas de casa e habilidades.

candidates.title: Hogwarts Legacy review
candidates.text: This experience is a mixed bag of pros and cons, especially as someone who has never watched a single Harry Potter film before playing this game.Pros:The story was engaging enough to keep me curious about what would happen next.The voice acting was phenomenal and consistently well-executed.The music was immersive and really drew me into the world.Even without maxed-out settings, the graphics and environment were stunning.The characters frequently interacted with the environment, often stopping me in my tracks to watch these moments unfold.The character side stories delves into the backstories and development of your main character's friends, creating a genuine bond.Combat felt smooth and unique to me, yet remained simple and not overly complex.Cons:However, the longer you play, the more the flaws start to stand out.Beneath the surface, there’s a lack of impact between good and evil dialogue choices—there’s no real morality system. Quest givers react the same way, regardless of how much of a jerk you are.The loot system feels odd. Gear is quickly and easily replaced throughout the early and mid-game, which disrupts the pacing. Plus, the value of equipment is based on its rarity, not its level, which feels off.On top of that, the only way to make money is to sell these said equipment in this game, but there's no mass or quick-sell option, making it tedious to sell items one by one. To make it worse, the limited inventory space forces you to constantly seek out shops to offload gear or regularly discard items.Overall, this game is a 6.5 / 10 in my books and is worth experiencing once if it is on sale

candidates.title: Teardown review
candidates.text: If you're looking for unbridled destruction with big explosions and buildings falling down... then you might want to play Red Faction Guerrilla.While at first sight Teardown might look like a game focused on causing destruction and with cool physics, it's more of a heist game than anything else. It's more akin to Puzzle than to Action.In each stage, you have to steal one or more things and reach your escape vehicle within one minute. The timer doesn't start right at the beginning of the level, only when you steal your first object and trigger the alarm.So, before you trigger the alarm, your job is to carefully survey the map and plan the fastest route that you can to steal the things you have to steal and escape. To do this, you will need to strategically destroy parts of your enviroment, position vehicles and use other tools to make the shortest route.Is it fun? Kinda. It's very frustrating sometimes, as at first it might seem like you are limited in the routes you can plan, as the destruction of buildings don't always function in the way you expect them too. It's very easy, for example, for a vehicle you are using to fall apart, when a building you wanted to fall apart doesn't because there's 1 pixel holding it in the air.While my review might sound negative, if you can get used to the quirks of the engine and accept the game for what it is (puzzle/speedrun/heist), it can be pretty fun to finally see a plan you made coming together. Just don't expect the kind of destruction and action you get in a game like Red Faction Guerrilla, unfortunately we have no true successor to that kind of fun yet.

candidates.title: Teardown review
candidates.text: Most levels are built out of objects made by voxels with various materials to form a pixelated representation of real world objects while the stages uses realistic lighting and water bodies. The materials of these voxels determine how destructible it is from your influence. While a few materials like rock and heavy metal are completely indestructible, others like wood can be burn and set aflame and cause chain reactions. Your starting sledgehammer can breakdown weaker structures, but guns and explosives get through stronger materials, and the blowtorch can burn things and cut some metal. Though there are still "floating voxel" scenarios. Other world systems include fire on flammable materials, which can be put out with the fire extinguisher that sprays a cloud of foam that will probably challenge your CPU, semi-realistic bodies of water, buildable wooden planks used to make personal bridges, protect objects, or tether objects to other structures. Some objects are connected to alarms in certain stages that will alert security to your presence and give you 60 seconds to complete your objective and escape before a mission failure. Usually there's an alarm that can be triggered, such as fire alarm after flames reach a certain density in the stage, water alarms when an item is wet, or usually theft alarms when an object is disconnected from a sensor. You gradually earn new tools able to be used in future and previously completed missions for better scores, which unlocks more missions. Completing missions and finding valuables give you money used to upgrade your tools. You may find yourself either bored or uninterested in finding a clever way to steal random cars and safes for a customer that amounts little more than an avatar with text on a computer screen. The campaign isn't bad, but it isn't what alot of players was expecting, and many do not find it fun.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: Nota pessoal / Geral: 9.5/10• OMORI é um jogo que saiu em 25 de Dezembro de 2020, tendo seu projeto iniciado em 2014, sendo um projeto feito com bastante carinho pela sua criadora, OMOCAT, e sua equipe de desenvolvedores, o jogo é um RPG com elementos de batalha de turnos. De início, pode ser dificultoso para pessoas inexperientes com o gênero, além de possuir uma dificuldade fixa, porém, o jogo ainda consegue ser aproveitado bem por qualquer pessoa, independente do seu nível de experiência.• Jogando o jogo por conta própria, eu realmente me senti interessado na história, não pode-se dizer muito sobre, pois o foco principal é um SPOILER gigantesco. Portanto, em breves palavras:• OMORI é um jogo que gira em torno do nosso protagonista, OMORI, que navega pelo ESPAÇO MENTAL (nome original: HEADSPACE) com seus amigos Aubrey, Kel e Hero, que procuram por seu amigo desaparecido Basil. Os personagens encontram vários inimigos e se encontram em situações bobalhonas em que nenhum jogador pode esperar, porém, ainda contando uma história sobre amizade e aproveitar seus amigos enquanto eles estão próximos. Para uma melhor experiência de jogo, é recomendado mergulhar de cabeça, sem pesquisar nada, pois na internet, a chance de conseguir um spoiler gigante é imensa.• O jogo é um RPG, portanto, é necessário não apenas atacar loucamente, mas realizar estratégias. Cada personagem em luta possui suas HABILIDADES, OMORI sendo o famoso "pau pra toda obra", tendo equilíbrio entre defesa, ataque e velocidade, a AUBREY, sendo um possível tanque pro time, o KEL sendo um canhão que pode dar gigantescas quantias de dano se utilizar de suas habilidades corretamente, e o HERO sendo o healer do grupo com sua culinária impecável.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: Let me first make clear that I have not finished the game yet, and currently have no intention to do so. I made it up until the end of the first day, after returning the photo album to Basil, before deciding that I wasn't interested in putting up with it anymore.Omori's problems as I see them were present pretty much from the game's introductory sequence. The first and most worst of these by far, and the whole reason why I lost all interest in seeing the game through to the end, is the pacing.The game is split into two different types of segments. First are those that take place in the headspace, a world that exists solely in the protagonist's dreams or imagination. Then there are the real-world segments that take place in the town of Faraway.Almost all of the game's story takes place in the real world, whereas the headspace segments feel like meaningless sidequests, yet the vast majority of the game itself takes place in the headspace.And the thing is, both the combat and the headspace story are at least serviceable when taken by themselves, but together they make the headspace segments feel meandering to the point of being tedious, taking too much time away from the actually interesting parts of the story. Had the story been tighter or the combat been removed entirely, as in many other games of this type, I probably would have been willing to bear through them and see the game through to the end.Now, I've seen some people say that these segments being disconnected from the main plot is their whole thematic point, as they are imaginary adventures the protagonist goes to in order to escape from the real world. That maybe so, but that point could have been sufficiently established within an hour of playtime. In order to justify the amount of time spent in the headspace there needs to be some further relevance to it, which there very rarely is.But even taking the headspace story on its own terms, it's still just kinda okay.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: This is hands-down one of my most favorite games ever. Stylistically, mechanically, and story-wise.Omori is packed with emotion. Ironic, considering the titular character is known for not showing any. You can jump from playing games with friends to twisted nightmares in the span of a few minutes - and the craziest thing about it is that none of it feels out of place. While cute, and definitely fun and lighthearted, Omori makes it very clear that something is wrong very early on, and that persists, only growing stronger the further you progress. While personally, I think this game is best experienced going in blind, without spoilers, please take heed of the warning screen that advises that it features depictions of depression, anxiety, and suicide, as well as photosensitive content.Some quick notes about gameplay for those who might be interested. The playthrough time is somewhere around 20 hours. At least, that's how long I spent the two times I played. Combat is turn-based with different emotions (happy, angry, and sad) acting as buffs/debuffs to your attack, defense, speed, and hit rate; essentially like rock-paper-scissors. You'll learn about it very early on and remembering to use its mechanic will make some boss/enemy encounters much easier (basically, don't be like me). Lastly, there are two routes and four endings. A good, a bad, and two neutral. I won't explain them here due to spoilers, but it's helpful information for achievement hunters or for after you complete a first playthrough and want to see what else there is to explore.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: Unfortunately, it only takes up around 5 hours of gameplay. Kel, Aubrey, Hero, and Basil are enjoyable characters and feel almost real, making their plights more interesting and making you feel for their characters. Watching the characters process and attempt to grow from their past is enjoyable and the overall message of moving forward from past actions and trauma is one that should be seen more in media and I am glad this game went to the effort to flesh out its messaging.I'd recommend watching a let's play over playing the game yourself, since that way you can trim the fat of the game if you want to avoid the overly long Headspace sections. There's one section towards the very end I'd say is worth playing, but it's so late in the game I can't justify telling someone to spend $20 just to experience a 30 minute to 1 hour long section when you could get the same experience as it from Yume Nikki or its various fan sequels or clones for free with the added bonus of a better atmosphere.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: I did not finish the game; I watched a let's play of the rest. This review contains spoilers.Omori is a story of guilt, self-loathing and isolation from friends because of what you think they think of you. The game is divided into two different realms: the real world and the psychedelic filler-world. The real world is where the actual game happens, and the psychedelic filler-world is there to, you guessed it, to pad the game time by about 400 % minimum.In the psychedelic filler-world you run from A to B doing silly stuff that doesn't matter and engaging in easy and simple RPG Maker battles. This section really is very padded. You have all kinds of mazes and puzzles that aren't difficult, but simply require you to go from place to place. The battle system is extremely simple, not deep and the battles very easy. From other reviews you can read about this interesting emotion mechanic in battles. Status effects have been in these kinds of games for tens of years, and the emotion mechanic doesn't relate in any way (not in any way) to the actual story happening, so I'm completely baffled as to what was so noteworthy here.Once you've done hours of the filler-world, you get to do half an hour of the real world, and that's where the game is good. You don't really fight battles there and you get the story exposition (which is, apparently, why you want to play this raved game anyway).Why the developer optet to tack on this psychedelic crappy RPG-Maker battle portion is beyond me. I cannot help but feel that for story and gameplay both it would've been more powerful to have it replaced with real-world sections of the past.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: His actions are a poor model for others, and the fact that the creator seems to endorse the mindset and behavior of Sunny is worrying and appalling. This game could retain large sweeps of its story and be great if the message wasn't so twisted by a need to make this poor behavior seem noble or correct. I played through Omori with the hope that I could see what others were seeing in this game. I absolutely adore stories that speak on dark themes or have complicated characters, but this story is not thought out and displays a dangerous selfishness without labeling it as such. I believe that most people who enjoy the game's story are good people, and most likely, they just ignore or have written off where this story has failed them as players. The aesthetic of Omori helps in enthralling some players to overlook these things, but if you are someone who has yet to play this game, I am telling you that it is not worth your time. If you decide to play it anyway, and you like it, then great, don't let anyone take that away from you, but please at least take the time to consider what the story might really be saying and how you inform or respond to it.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: TL;DR: Who knew trauma could be this fun? 10/10 would become a shut-in again.First things first - content warnings. The game contains sparse 32-bit depictions of self-harm and gore, though not particularly graphic in nature, is definitely done with the intent of catching the viewer off guard for story purposes. There are also drawn depictions of suicide in darker areas of the game, though these are considerably less jarring and more easily telegraphed to the viewer prior to appearing. There are discussions of death, loss, grief, depression, and self-destructive tendencies in conversations between the characters. Overall, not the most emotionally exhaustive game to play involving these themes, but the above instances are still worth noting to players who may have adverse reactions.The biggest strength I can claim this game has is its creativity. The battle system, the world building, the character writing, the art style, the soundtrack... All phenomenal.The opening act is a little slow, but once you get through the first twist of the protagonist's character arc, the game slowly opens up to reveal an incredibly engaging narrative that encourages you to explore every location you can to discover more. Every area in the game has a ton of little areas to search and discover new things in, which can be incredibly rewarding, even if most of these finds have little to do with the main plot. The branching narrative helps with this sense of exploration, as it makes you feel like the amount of effort you put into exploring the two main routes of OMORI's story is entirely up to the player. The typical completionist will likely play through 80% of the game at least twice to experience and discover all it has to offer, which is insane for an RPG Maker title.In a similar vein, the sheer level of emotional immersion I felt when playing through OMORI was unlike anything I'd ever experienced before.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: When I played this a while ago and I was quite fond of OMORI. OMORI made me cry like a ♥♥♥♥♥, laugh like a madman, and held a fond place in my heart as one of the most emotive games I've ever completed. OMORI has a psychedelic landscape that makes the game somewhat alive, not to mention one of the best video game OSTs known to man. As a fan, I bought posters, and I have the soundtrack on CD. But despite all this, I can't bring myself to actually like OMORI anymore.Recently I played Yume Nikki, which I only played because I knew it 'inspired' OMORI. After beating Yume Nikki (twice) I reflected on OMORI witch a certain hollowness. To call Yume Nikki an inspiration for OMORI is an understatement. Complete scenes (including the one of the literal endings of the game as well as the final areas of the game) are just straight up ripped from Yume Nikki. OMORI is unoriginal and, in my opinion, is more like a fan-fiction/artist rendition of Yume Nikki. This might not be an issue to some people, in fact to others OMORI might be an overall more enjoyable experience then Yume Nikki, but for me it's like a big slap in the face. Personally, Indie games and especially RPG-maker games as a medium are so appealing because they are a reflection of the creator. Indie games have a piece of soul that AAA's don't. So when OMORI advertises itself as it's own thing, and turns out to be some pseudo-original experience it just.... Sucks. I can't bring myself to like OMORI anymore. But for those who don't care about originality and are fans of games like undertale, LISA, and the mother series I strongly recommend OMORI.

candidates.title: Journey review
candidates.text: Journey is quite unlike anything I've played before. The title sums up the game very well. It doesn't hold your hand or force narrative down your throat. It just lets you explore while guiding you in a general direction, allowing players to figure things out as they go with no obvious goal or objective. Journey manages to evoke different emotions throughout with warm joyful feelings at some points and anxious fear in others. The highlights of journey are made when you bump into other players and share the journey together. With not a single word exchanged you are still able to share the experience of the journey together which I found quite special. The soundtrack is another great addition that adds a nice layer to the experience which is coupled well together with good visuals. Journey is an experience that encourages multiple play through's as there is quite a lot to explore and things I feel I've most definitely missed on my first play through which lasted only about 2 hours. This is a masterpiece in escapism and an experience worth having. I give it a 10/10.

And in my opinion the flow is very important here because of how you interact and traverse through the world.A simple dash would be nice to have instead of just walking when you don't have the "energy"."Real journey was the friends we made along the way" - as memey as that sounds, this was the best part of the game, don't really want to spoil it, if you are like me going in blind after many years then this should be a pleasant surprise.The graphics aren't as great anymore, the music isn't memorable and the journey is short, took me an hour and a half, which is closer to a stroll after dinner.It's not a bad game, it's just outdated and mid and there are better similar games.5/10My recommendations on what to play instead:If you want an actual journey/adventure - "FAR: Lone Sails"If you want fluid movement, nice visuals and fantastic boss fights - "The Pathless"If you want to play a work of art with a bit of puzzles and a bittersweet story that will keep you thinking after the credits - "GRIS"

candidates.title: Journey review
candidates.text: I do not understand why this interactive experience (it does not qualify as a "game") is so highly reviewed. What some see as an emotional, deep experience, I see as shallow and lacking commitment by its designers to a clear plot or narrative. Some may say that the narrative is open to interpretation and it may be compared to abstract fine art, but there is a line where art becomes so abstract it becomes meaningless noise. As work approaches this line it also becomes less clear what the creators' intent is. Journey is not meaningless noise, but it is unclear what the creators want to say and there is no plot for the player to become invested in. When I started playing it I thought it would make more sense as I played, but there is no narrative arc that explains what is going on. Journey was not entertaining and I did not grow emotionally or intellectually from it.Reviews that praise Journey as being art do not say much. Call of Duty is art. Achieving the status of art is a low bar. It took me some time to figure out the chime and flight mechanics. I did not know the left mouse button did anything until about halfway through. It would not hurt to use some words to explain such things to the player. (I don't understand why so many people are credited with localization when the only words in this are the menu.) I was also unaware of the co-op aspect until the end when it showed usernames. The game is also incredibly short and has little replay value. It is not worth $15.

candidates.title: Journey review

Having never played on the original platform(PS3), you could say I was somewhat late to the party.Still, it was better late than never, and I still cherish every single moment I waded through with fellow wayfarer even to this day. The masterpiece soundtrack, and in-game screenshots has accompanied me - whether it be on my PC, or my phone. Journey has been, simply put, that memorable.If only that was the case with this cursed PC release.The game itself should be great if it actually works.What I don't understand is that why this PC port is marred with problems, and why such problems still persist even after almost 2 years of release.Personally, I found these three issues:1) (Supposedly) Music problem: Apparently, companion music is messed up compared to PS version. Cannot say for sure, because for the short amount of playtime(1.2 hrs) graciously bestowed upon me by Jinxed God of Journey PC Port, I was not able to meet a single buddy. Still, people have reported problem regarding this: you can google-fu some workaround with this issue... which entails there is a problem in the first place.2) Visual stuttering: I was surprised that a decade old game would stutter on my 2021 rig, however humble it is. FPS counter reports 60+FPS, but stutter persists. Good thing that turning off in-game VSync rectified this problem. Still, not a good sign.3) CTD at a specific point: This is what broke the metaphorical camel's back. In the underground section, a... dragon-like creature gobbles up a rug-like fish-thingy. And voila, the game crashes at that point constantly. Apparently, this issue was not limited to myself, given that there are some poor souls reporting the very issues on the steam forum... And that thread started in 2020!

Highpool is a small settlement located South East from the Ranger Citadel that was a popular camping ground before the war as well as the site of a large water reservoir that supplies drinking water to the region. It comes under raider attack early in the game and the Rangers have to choose between saving it or the agricultural center.

Entering Highpool automatically destroys the ag center. Note that if the Rangers enter Highpool to save it, they cannot withdraw from the location. Leaving Highpool and entering the world map will cause it to be destroyed by the Wrecking Crew automatically.

candidates.title: Wasteland 2 endings
candidates.text:
Without Highpool's regular deliveries of clean water, many communities are going thirsty and watching their crops wither to ash. Now farmers with nothing to eat are turning to banditry, and bloody conflicts are raging over the ownership of the few remaining springs and wells. Even the Desert Rangers are feeling the pinch, with many teams going out on patrol with empty canteens and cracked lips. Many mourn Katie Preston and Sean Bergin, opposites in so many ways, but united in their determination to keep Highpool alive, and now united in death. Save Highpool, but leave the Wrecking Crew alive at their camp.Thanks to your timely intervention and thoroughness in Highpool - saving their irrigation system and decisively defeating the Wrecking Crew - the fortified town's safety has been assured and its reservoirs remain strong and secure, insuring that the Arizona wastes will have plentiful drinking water and irrigation for the foreseeable future. Save Highpool, prevent the reservoir from exploding, wipe out the Wrecking Crew.Sadly, all the credit for your good works is being attributed to the late Sean Bergin, who the citizens of Highpool are also calling the martyred savior of the rangers, bacause of his heroic death during the battle for Ranger Citadel.

In honor of his memory, Highpool has elected a new mayor just as biased toward the RSM as Bergin was, and though the treaty with the RSM means that Highpool should be friendly to the rangers, they still hold a grudge, and are shorting the new Ranger Citadel on water deliveries every chance they get.

candidates.title: Highpool (Wasteland 2)
candidates.text:
Highpool is half a combat area. The area between the entrance and the dam is littered with Wrecking Crew raiders and requires getting through them to reach the base of the dam, where Jackhammer is trying to blow it up. Just before the dam approach is a small enclave to the side, where Alexey Chuklin resides and will ask you to find his love. The approach can be made easier to fight through if you adjust the mortar and decide to direct it against the raiders (firing it without adjustment will kill Highpool denizens on top of the dam).
Note that one of the enterable buildings in the lower area contains Jess-Belle and a toaster that contains lenses for Dr Baum at the Temple of Titan.
Once Jackhammer is dead, he will let the Rangers up and be nonplussed that they aren't the RSM, but will eventually grudgingly allow them to roam around. The upper terrace is centered around the massive pumps and offers several methods to help Highpool, including helping Mark Stachowiak put out his burning house, finding Adam Doochin's dog, and finding Jess-Bells' dowry. The real work is below the ground, where the Rangers have to help Kate Preston save the town's reservoirs from exploding.

candidates.title: Highpool
candidates.text:
Originally a reservoir and water treatment plant, with a nearby summer camp, Highpool's remote and altitude allowed society of sorts to continue after the bombs fell, as the children and adults present at Camp Highpool realized they had nowhere to go. As the area was located in a sheltered valley, with its own source of water and readily available infrastructure, it became a small, yet thriving wasteland community. Its key asset is the water purifier, taking water from the lake and purifying it, allowing Highpool to provide the Arizona Wasteland with the most reliable and abundant source of fresh water in the region. The arable soil and large-scale farming are just the cherry on top.Wasteland 2 Director's Cut Manual p.58: "Highpool was a reservoir and water treatment plant before the war, with a nearby camp for kids. Its remote, high location allowed the children and adults there to survive not just the war itself, but also the anarchy that followed. The town itself is small, but well-fortified,and it serves a critical function in the Arizona Wasteland, with its water purification plant the most reliable and bountiful source of fresh water available."

The lake itself is an artificial reservoir created by the dam and sustains a vibrant ecosystem, including red-tailed hawks. The valley Highpool itself rests in is bounded by limestone cliffs, dotted with seashells and worm tracks.Environmental descriptions in Wasteland.

candidates.title: NHighpool
candidates.text:
Used mainly as a troop staging area, Highpool is almost always full of Ranger HQ troops and recruits.

Areas of interest :

1) Troop barracks. On the north side of highpool, they all map to the same room. Until an encounter check is passed, they are all 'live' since they point to the same space. Once an encounter check (for various faction affiliation) is passed they become 'dead' and are static from that point on.

2) Store. Slightly changed from the old store.

3) Small house. Maps to room with chests. Who is in the middle? Bobby you say?

4) Shrine. Memorial to youths killed by rangers over 20 years ago. Ranger HQ stopped trying to stamp it out after the Free Rangers split off from them.

5) Residential housing. Lower section. Can't enter these.

Plot ideas:

Highpool
Originally a summer camp for children, Highpool became a sheltered, safe town after the nuclear war. By 2087, it's a small town suffering from a water shortage on account of a broken water purifier, which requires an engine from the Rail Nomads to repair.

The camp consists of some two-story adobe buildings that resemble dorms, a playground with swings and slides and fields watered by canals that gets its water from the two feet deep Highpool Creek which flows through the settlement and ends in a small lake. A larger building in the center of the camp forms the Community Center. Most adults are absent, busy raiding outlaws prowling the surrounding areas, with children pretty much the only denizens Rangers are likely to meet.

candidates.title: Besiege review
candidates.text: I've played this game for so long I followed its development on imgur like half a decade ago. Besiege is really one of the first of its kind - a game about building vehicles to meet the demands of the mission at hand. Before Simple Planes or Trailmakers, there was Besiege. The game really just gives you a tool box full of blocks, motors, spikes, and bombs and asks you to complete deceptively simple missions. The fun of the game comes from what you decide to do to solve the problem at hand. Technically, a helicopter with a grabber and a bomb can finish like 4/5ths of the original campaign, but the real meat and potatoes of the game comes from building inefficient, unoptimized solutions. If you have an inkling of a creative bone in your body, this is the game for you. The building mechanics are solid, the gameplay loop is fun, the game is graphically pretty good for an indie title, and the sound design of the game is memorable. The performance is pretty good considering the physics at play and the degree to which you can crank the graphical fidelity. If you like building solutions to problems, this is a fun game to pick up!

candidates.title: Building Planes
candidates.text:
In Besiege there is a variety of easy to build A/G and A/A weapons.

Rules for building planes also apply for rockets and bombs.
Heavy payload changes CoM (and also CoL if propellers are involved), as well as dropping it. Heavy bombs, etc. should be attached as close to CoM as possible.
Make sure that the plane’s landing gear is able to support the plane with the payload and land with it. Check if the plane is able to takeoff and land in a reasonable space.

candidates.title: Balloon
candidates.text:

They are also used to counteract the weight of bombs and other detachable components on aircraft where precision tuning is necessary.

candidates.title: Achievements
candidates.text:
Like most modern games, Besiege has Achievements, which are linked with Steam.

Complete them for a sense of pride and accomplishment.

__TOC__

Icon Name Description A Swift Siege 3 Complete a campaign level under 2 seconds. This can be achieved by putting a Bomb behind the Starting Block in the first level. Or shooting it with a Cannon. The Handyman 3 Complete a campaign level with under 3 blocks. See the description for A Swift Siege. Gotta Go Fast 3 Go faster than 60 km/h with your machine. See the description for A Swift Siege. If you don't want to cheese it, build a plane or something. Thunderstruck 3 Get hit by lightning. In The Duke's Plea, there is a thunder cloud directly between the left and center towers, which will occasionally spew lightning. Roll your machine under it. You'll know it's worked when your machine catches fire. Pyromaniac 3 Set yourself on fire. Set yourself on fire. All Under Control 3 Put out a burning block using water. Set a block on fire with a Flamethrower and then immediately use a Water Cannon to put it out. Freezing Frontier 3 Reach enough altitude to freeze your machine. Usually, the ice layer is at approximately 1700 metres above the ground, but on some levels (e.g. The Frozen Path), it's much lower. To get there, put four bombs two blocks below the starting block and detonate them. Or use a flying machine. See Piloting 101. Carnage 3 Defeat 1000 AI units. You can probably get this by doing The Queen's Fodder a few times after completing the campaign, or a lot of times if not. Raw Fodder 3 Beat Queens Fodder without using fire or explosives. A basic log frame with 2x-speed Powered Large Wheels should be more than enough to do this. Just don't hit any bombs.

candidates.title: Penitent Tower
candidates.text:
This is a legitimately difficult level with no easy solution - you really do have to reduce the entire fortress to smoking ruins, and it's not small, and it's not lightly defended. With over 30 axethrowers that can hit things up to 80 metres away for double damage, it is a daunting target to assault from the ground or from the air.

You can deliver Bombs to each of the five towers, making sure to hit the soldiers near or on them. Or, you can use a vehicle with Circular Saws or Drills to face them head-on.

If attacking from the ground, you'll need an armoured vehicle - preferably a fast one, with a frame built from sturdy blocks like Logs. The spearmen can smash weak frames, even if armoured. If you're carrying bombs, you'll need to keep them protected from axes and the aforementioned spearmen until you're in a position to launch them.

If attacking from the air, you either need a plane (with bombs) that can outrun the axes or a quadcopter that is stable enough to drop bombs accurately from 100 metres in the air. The Hot Air Balloon block can also help when multiple are used in conjunction. This can lead to instability, as well however, so a gyroscope of sorts can be necessary.

candidates.title: Besiege review
candidates.text: Uh, man. Long day of work, late dinner, cat ripped up all the napkins, pantry shelf broke, again. I need to unwind.Oh! I know!Lets blow up a castle in Besiege.Now I've always been a big fan of sandbox/physics based games, so Besiege fit right in with my prefered playstyle. You start the game and the first level is just a simple little house that you must destroy. Many levels later and suddenly your getting sucked up by tornados and fighting angry farmers who wish to protect their crops. You'll even encounter a few animals with bombs on their backs ready to blow up in your face.Ah, there's a Castle in my way! I'll blow it up.Oh no, I'm floating in the sky! I'll make plane.Not another group of angry knights! I'll shoot them with my wall of rockets.Besiege is a great sandbox game where in each level you are tasked to either destroy, steal, deliver or get to the objective. In one level your killing massive flocks of sheep and in another your destroying towns. Build whatever you need to conquer the objective. A plane? Drone? Tank? A bomb of spikes? The choice is yours! Your imagination is your only limit.Even when you beat all of the levels, there's still a great sandbox testing map for you to enjoy. On that map there are many things to test your vehicle with, like killing chickens, going up anti-gravity pads, destroying the home of a few peasants, and blowing up a little tower which a few knights must guard so desperately.You built something really awesome? Share it with the community! On the Steam Workshop you can upload your creations or download other people's builds.And, you don't have to build a vehicle.

candidates.title: Basic Siege Engine
candidates.text:
Siege mortars are primitive Cannons - they use gunpowder to launch the projectile. Using a Shrapnel Cannon to fling the bomb won't look like a cannon, but it will work like one, and deliver exceptional range and speed.

As long as the bomb is in the air and free to move, a shrapnel cannon blast will not detonate it. This can be abused to send the bomb flying. Tilting the shrapnel cannon to direct the blast to the top or bottom of the bomb can alter the trajectory.

Place a Steering Hinge. Set its speed low with the keymapper (about 0.20x).
Place a shrapnel cannon on top of the hinge. Set its power as high as it will go.
Place a Grabber two blocks in front of the hinge. Set its detach key to the same as the cannon firing key.
Place a bomb on top of the grabber.

It's quite fun.

A more 'mortar'-like appearance might be achieved with a reloadable version of this, but that is not a 'basic' siege engine.

candidates.title: Brace
candidates.text:
Brace are usually used as structural reinforcement, or used aesthetically to represent reinforced bars or poles.

Because the Brace does not have any Solids, anything can phase through it (including the ground). They can be safely used in places where other blocks cannot (like, say, in the path of a catapult arm).

The second endpoint of a Brace is unique - it can connect to multiple blocks at once. By taking advantage of this, it is possible for two braces to do the work of six (or more). CCCanyon's Notes on Block and Brace Connections

However, braces are brittle, heavy, and comparatively weak. While they are useful, spamming them everywhere will not save a poorly-constructed creation.

candidates.title: Circular Saw
candidates.text:
See Also: Powered Wheel
The Circular Saw is basically a Powered Wheel, except for more speed, sharper edges, and the fact that it can't be turned off (See that page for more details).

It is easily the best melee weapon in the game; it doesn't break as easily as the Drill, and doesn't require an external source of power like the Metal Blade. It can be used for a variety of anti-personnel and anti-installation tasks.

It also has a hidden connection point embedded inside it with an 0.225m offset. This can be used to connect other blocks to it (like Propellers, or other Saws).

+ The Traveler, aka Siffrin The main protagonist of the game. Their primary Craft type is Scissors, and as the fastest party member, their skills focus on speed and Scissors attacks. They have a Craft skill that lets them pass their turn to another ally.

Their special skill is "(Just Attack.)": obtained as the Prologue progresses, it inflicts strong Scissors damage to all enemies. The Housemaiden, aka Mirabelle Mirabelle is a nervous and caring Housemaiden. She has both Scissors and Paper Craft types. Blessed by the Change God, she is the only party member who cannot be Frozen in time; she specializes in healing skills, such as one that can bring back defeated allies, or heal everyone, although she also possesses one skill of each Paper and Scissors types.

Her special skill is "Lovely Moving Cure": obtained with story progression, it is capable of unfreezing allies, being the only thing (skills and items combined) that can do so in the game. The Fighter, aka Isabeau Isabeau is a Defender with a heart of gold, who cares deeply for his people and friends. His primary Craft type is Rock; his skills focus on buffing his allies' Defense, and strong Rock attacks — although similarly to Siffrin, he also has a skill that lets him pass his turn to another ally, buffing them up.

question: What new items are available in the in-game store for Lost Ark during the summer update?

candidates.title: Team Update - Awaiting Paradise
candidates.text:
As previously announced, the July update will introduce the Luminous Gem system into the Western version of Lost Ark. Our region’s player to player market was more resilient than other regions, and the price of level 10 damage gems today have barely decreased from their price when the original announcement was shared in Korea. As level 10 damage gems have retained nearly all of their value and they will still be fully usable by their owners, the compensation sent out in some other regions of Lost Ark will not be distributed in the Western version.

We’re excited for the new and fun customization opportunities that the Luminous Gem system will provide for all players, with greater freedom to try out new builds, and that the new T4 Luminous Gems in the Solo Shop help new and returning players gear up for the challenges that await them in the war against Kazeros.

Sidereal Energy

Similarly, our region didn’t experience major price fluctuations for Sidereal Energy when Elgic Infuse II was introduced, so the compensation sent out in KR won’t be distributed. However, we will be awarding an exclusive Relic icon title and class symbol in the July update to those who have completed Elgic Infuse II.

The July ‘Welcome to Paradise’ update arrives next week on July 23! As normal, the release notes will be available the day before, covering the massive amount of changes arriving in this update. We’ll see you in Paradise, next week!

candidates.title: Team Update - June 2025
candidates.text:
While we saw a lot of positive feedback reinforcing the decision to tie Mokoko status to 10x Raid Clears, we also saw some player concerns about the system still having an Item Level cap after we shared the planned changes, so we wanted to share the planned level. When the Mokoko Bootcamp returns this summer with the adjustments, it will be extended to include Aegir (Act 1) Hardmode and Brelshaza (Act 2) Normal Mode. For these raids, we plan for the Item Level cap to be at 1689, so that players aren’t punished for continuing to progress after reaching the respective Item Levels for those raids at 1680 and 1670. We will continue to lookout for feedback on the system, and appreciate the feedback we’ve received so far!

Skin Collection Book

Quick context; it’s a feature that allows for a more organized cosmetic collection and expands the number of available slots to stash cosmetics in your inventory. This will release alongside the Paradise system this summer, without the power increase and ranking systems found within other versions of Lost Ark. We hope this is a helpful tool for expanding the closets of Arkesian fashionistas, but don’t want there to be additional pressure to collect every skin.

Una’s Task Improvements

In the last player survey, we had specific questions about your thoughts on dailies. The feedback provided by you, the Lost Ark Community, helped us during discussions about changes for the Western version of the game. As a direct result, we are very excited to bring the following change to the West.

Daily Una’s Tasks will be improved to help balance the amount of daily/weekly ‘homework’ activity when the Paradise system is added into the game. Daily tasks will remain, but once the reputation milestones are reached, the tasks will disappear. Daily Una’s rewards will be moved to weekly quest rewards.

General QoL

candidates.title: Jump-Start Server Update
candidates.text:
For players looking to further enhance their characters, the Jump-Start in-game store will have special packages and items. With heavily discounted material packages to boost vertical and horizontal progression (such as Card Packs, Pheons, Silver, and Honing Materials), we want to ensure players on Jump-Start Servers looking to dive into the end-game have options that give them value. And for those looking to vanquish the demonic hordes in style, a variety of cosmetics will be returning from the vault, available exclusively on Jump-Start Servers. Jump-Start players will have plenty of cosmetic customization options available.

Looking Ahead

candidates.title: Peglin review
candidates.text: Peglin is a delightful blend of classic pachinko mechanics with roguelike gameplay, resulting in a fresh and surprisingly strategic experience. The premise is simple yet fun—you play as a cute little goblin (the titular Peglin) who embarks on a journey through various stages, battling enemies by launching orbs and aiming for pegs to deal damage.The gameplay is both easy to understand and enjoyably challenging. Every level presents new peg layouts and enemy types, making each encounter feel unique. As you progress, you gather different orbs with special effects and relics that enhance your powers, allowing for creative strategies and new approaches each time you play. The game does a great job of balancing luck with skill, so while there’s an element of chance to where your orb lands, the upgrades and your aim add a solid layer of strategy.The art style and animations are charming, adding a lot of personality to the simple gameplay. Peglin is also refreshingly straightforward, making it easy to jump into for short sessions but engaging enough to keep you playing for hours.Overall, Peglin is a well-crafted game that’s both relaxing and exciting, with enough depth to keep players coming back for “just one more round.” It’s a great pick for fans of casual roguelikes and physics-based games alike. Highly recommended!

candidates.text:
Voghiln is a versatile party member whose stats allow him to play many roles on the battlefield. By default he is equipped with Voghiln's Helmet, Bracers of Defense AC 6, Warhammer +1, Buckler +1, 40 Throwing Axes +1, and 40 Throwing Axes. He also has 5 Potions of Healing, 2 Potions of Freedom and 1 Potion of Mind Focusing. As a bard, he is the only recruitable party member who can use bard-only magic items and equipment like musical instruments. candidates.title: System reorganization update notice
candidates.text:
A system update is planned for (re)release this Friday (September 18th).
Incorporating the feedback we received from the September 11th update,
we've adjusted and improved a number of aspects.

The changes to the system are intended to emphasize two things:

Our goals with this update include:

- Encouraging the player to utilize a variety of Combat Pages, Key Pages, and Passive Abilities
- Allowing the player to freely customize their Key Pages within given limits
- Increasing the freedom and diversity of deck setups
- Reducing the repetition of fighting the same battles over and over for leveling up and acquiring items (lessening "the grind")

1. Added a "Key Page Editing" feature

- A "Key Page Editing" feature has been added, with which you may "attribute" unequipped Key Pages to another Key Page to make use of the passive abilities belonging to them.
- By editing a Key Page, it is possible to equip passive abilities from several different Key Pages.
- However, the passive abilities of the main Key Page cannot be unequipped or swapped out for another passive.
- Also, it is not possible to equip the same passive ability multiple times on a single Key Page.
- Depending on the perceived value of the passive ability, some limits may be imposed in the future in the forms of passive ability costs, equip limits per passive ability type, or other restrictions.
- The changes to passive abilities themselves are as follows:

- Minor (yellow) passive abilities will be removed (e.g. "Pierce Mastery I/II/III").
- No changes will be made to the existing Unique (blue) passives (e.g. "Instant Cooking").
- Shi Association's negative passive abilities will be integrated with other relevant passives in order to save space for slots.

2. Removed levels from Key Pages.

question: What are the file extensions for material, texture, model, and configuration files used in the game Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic?

candidates.title: General modding
candidates.text:
A: There are four kind of files:
Maps - a .png file that is not bigger than 1 MB for your workshop and in-game preview (can be changed later) and a .txt file for your description (can be changed too).
Reskins - a .png file that is not bigger than 1 MB for your workshop and in-game preview (can be changed later) and a .txt file for your description (can be changed too). For the reskin itself you need to copy the diffuse.dds and material.mtl file of the vehicle you’re reskinning, and put them in you workshop folder. From there you can start fun with editing them.
Vehicles - a .png file that is not bigger than 1 MB for your workshop and in-game preview (can be changed later) and a .txt file for your description (can be changed too). Besides that, you’ll need a .nmf file of your vehicle (can be created by converting an .obj file to .nmf in Modelviewer), an .mtl file (can be also created through Modelviewer) and a script.ini file (which you can copy from a folder of another vehicle from the same type you’re modding).
Buildings - a .png file that is not bigger than 1 MB for your workshop and in-game preview (can be changed later) and a .txt file for your description (can be changed too). Besides that, you’ll need a .nmf file of your building (can be created by converting an .obj file to .nmf in Modelviewer), an .mtl file (can be also created through Modelviewer) a building.ini file (which you can copy from a folder of another building from the same type you’re modding) and a renderconfig.ini file.

candidates.title: Resources
candidates.text: Resources are a core component of Workers & Resources, as it's even in the name. Almost everything in Workers & Resources requires resources to function, and if playing without unlimited money, resources are needed to export for money or construct infrastructure without using money. Almost all resources fall into one of four categories: aggregates, open storage resources, warehouse resources, liquids, and misc. resources that do not fall into any of these categories (i.e., meats, livestock, asphalt, and concrete). Meat and livestock require their own storage and transportation, while asphalt and concrete cannot be stored and must instead be manufactured on demand and transported via dump trucks and mixer trucks, respectively.

.nmf - mesh file. It is the model of your vehicle/building
.ini - config file. It is used to write properties of your mod in the game, eg. capacity of your vehicle or to place the light(s)

She's supposed to be a badass?? Honestly, she looks 10x better than she did in all the other games. I think people are mad that she doesn't wear a tube top anymore and finally looks like a real woman. She was for sure intended for the female gaze in this game and I am not complaining... because I am a woman. I am convinced that she was handcrafted by Aphrodite herself. She is just so... perfect. This game really made me like her. I love her. Did I mention that I am in love with Jill Valentine? I think I'm getting off track....I have a few complaints. I would've liked to see a longer game. One closer to the original. I noticed that some parts were cut out that would've made the experience better. Nonetheless, I recommend playing it.

candidates.text:
手を入れた箇所で言うと、今作のモデルのジルで「バイオハザード1」の身分証を作っているんですが、ファンの方からどう受け止め られるか少し心配しています。他に少し手を入れたところで顕著なのがレベッカかもしれないですね。あそこのレベッカ、実はすごく 若くしています。やっぱり「バイオ」や「バ イオ1」の時の若々しく可愛らしい印象が強いと思うので、その時のイメージになるようにしています。クレアも「RE2」ではフェイスモデルが違うので、後ろ向きにして見えないよう工夫しました。Is that why you were suggested an additional scene where you go into the water?

Yes, Jill wasn't planned to go into the water at the beginning, or rather, until just before production began for the final scene.However, as we progressed with the production and more and more pictures were nearing completion, we naturally felt like, "There's water here, so why not go in it? It's strange not to use it all, isn't it?" So this time, when we spoke to the director from the set, he said, "Oh, is that okay?" We also said, "We want to do it, so please let us do it," and that's how we came to the process. It felt like that scene had already been created with great momentum.

Speaking of water scenes, the licker in the underground passage was also impressive.

Honestly, I wanted to increase the amount of water involved. But rather than getting too hung up on things here and there, I thought I'd put all my effort into the last part. In that selection process, I took the time to make sure that the licker was clearly shown in that scene, including every detail. It's dark over there, so a darker screen would have been nice.

I thought the scene where Licker's tongue almost hits Jill was a killer shot.

candidates.title: Resident Evil 3 (2020)/plot
candidates.text:
Several minutes earlier, Jill crawled out of the subway car, realizing that she is the only one to survive the train derailment, so she tries to contact Carlos but is out of range; she manages to reach the city park near the Saint Michael's Clock Tower Plaza and hears the roaring pain of Nemesis. Jill crosses the walkway bridge where she sees a burning Nemesis tumble his way down the riverbank, and she contacts Carlos afterwards and informs him of what has transpired after he left. In the midst of the call, she was attacked by mutated Nemesis, who emerges from the river, where it had lost the makeshift coat it had, having mutated into a quadrupedal, ferocious canine-like creature with huge claws. Jill runs from it until she is cornered in the plaza, and is forced to fight. Jill knocks the creature out with the explosive rounds after a long duel, but before she can leave the area, Nemesis attacks her again, grabbing her by the feet until she shoots the chain that is holding the metal portcullis. The portcullis falls and amputates the arm of the Nemesis, but it regrows the arm in the form of a tentacle, and it manages to attack and infect her by impaling her arm with a bone spike, before they both fall to the ground, losing consciousness. Nikolai appears smiling and thanks her for doing him a big favor.

Half a day later, Carlos finds Jill and carries her to the Spencer Memorial Hospital hoping Bard could cure her, he radios Tyrell telling that they would meet there. On September 29, 9:20 PM, Carlos manages to reach the hospital and puts Jill down on the bed in the Makeshift Sickroom, he then goes out and searches for the vaccine.

candidates.title: Resident Evil 3 (2020)/plot
candidates.text:
Afterward, Jill Valentine experiences a nightmare, where she closes her window and stumbles into her bathroom. She shuts off the faucet of the sink, only to see blood patter into the sink. When she looks up, she sees herself beginning to transform, and recoils in terror, retreating into the darkness. When she reemerges into the light, she sees she has physically transformed into a zombie. Knowing she has little time left, she picks up a nearby handgun and presses the barrel to her temple. She then fires, before waking up.

The game is set on September 28, 8:07 PM. Jill reawakens, having slept while doing investigations on Umbrella from her apartment, and receives a frantic phone call from Brad Vickers. He warns her that she has to leave, before being abruptly cut off by the Nemesis bursting through the wall. She narrowly manages to escape its clutches by dashing into the hallway and another apartment, then reaching the fire escape. Going down, she briefly absorbs the carnage that Raccoon City has fallen into before reentering the apartment building. Jill is once again ambushed by the Nemesis and is nearly caught, once by its tentacle, moments later by it attempting to use the debris of the building to pin her, before she escapes.

candidates.text:
Carlos then tells her that he is a part of Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service (or U.B.C.S. for short). After hearing this, Jill lashes out at Carlos saying that Umbrella was responsible for the chaos occurring in Raccoon City. But having left with no choice, she decides to go with him. He then introduces her to Captain and platoon leader Mikhail Viktor, who asks her for help in evacuating some survivors via the subway train, Jill reluctantly agrees, but only because she wishes to save the civilians and not the U.B.C.S. members. Carlos then hands her a radio, informing her that they should stay in touch, while also nicknaming her "Supercop".

Jill reaches the topside of Raccoon city streets and is instructed by Carlos to head for the substation, and once she reaches the main road, he then tells her to go through the alley, but she discovers it has been set ablaze. She then traverses the streets and alleys to acquire a fire hose, and puts out the fire by attaching the fire hose to a nearby fire hydrant. Once inside the building, she finds an injured Murphy Seeker, but before she can treat him, Nikolai Zinoviev appears from behind and shoots Murphy in the head. Shocked and outraged, she angrily tells him that he might not have been infected, but he retaliates by taunting her, saying that all of the S.T.A.R.S members are soft and suggest she to go back for the subway station, as they don't need "a bleeding heart like her" getting in the way.

candidates.title: Resident Evil 3 (2020)/plot
candidates.text: Jill resumes her pursuit of Nikolai. On the roof, she finds Carlos knocked unconscious, Nikolai then attacks and knocks Jill's gun out of her hand, he tosses her the vaccine canister only to shoot it, thus dooming the city. Outraged by this, she asks him if he has any idea what he had just done but he only responds that he doesn't care, as his client asks him to reduce Umbrella to rubble. Nikolai prepares to kill Jill until Carlos tackles him and the two engages in combat, Carlos then puts Nikolai in a chokehold and shouts for Jill to shoot him, she is reluctant at first for fear of the bullet hitting Carlos, but finally complies and shoots Nikolai in the shoulder. She rushes to Carlos's aid, he tells her that he couldn't just leave her in a world without him for that will be too cruel. Jill then again asks an injured Nikolai why he had destroyed the vaccine, he responds cryptically and she asks him who he was working for but instead of an answer, he pleads that he would tell and pay if she gets him out of here, Jill decides to leave him on the roof but not before Nikolai warns her that if he dies then she will never find out the truth but Jill responds that she doesn't mind a little detective work and so Carlos and Jill board the helicopter, seemingly leaving Nikolai to die with the city.
