When Umbrella soldiers threaten an shoot out, Jill calls everyone to run from the gunshots. She runs down the streets of RC accompanied with Peyton and the reporter Terri Morales, who Jill had seen in the site of Raven's Gate Bridge checkpoint. The trio headed for Dilmore Place, which led to a run-down residential area as to avoid detection by Undeads when most citizens head for Route 22 and Western Boulevard. They head for a church to seek sanctuary but is met with hostility by an man. Terri manages to force their way in, letting all three of them inside the church.

Jill and Terri converse with one another with Terri claiming to have cover some of her cases shortly before her suspension. Jill takes a notice to the handheld camera that Terri has been holding all the way with her claiming that this footage will get her famous and recognition to her career back. When they heard a strange sound coming from the church, Jill decides to investigate and looks into the room behind the altar. She spots the priest's wife and notices that she has become an Undead, Jill tries to kill the zombified woman but is stopped by the priest. The woman's right hand eventually breaks free of the restraints and attacks the Priest, who she bites on the neck. Jill kills both of them and the shot is echoed throughout the sanction.

candidates.title: Story/Pre-1.0
candidates.text:
Balboa Island
The final location of the first chapter is Balboa Island: an Evergreen Island inhabited by Bears. Among these bears lives a boss-level bear fittingly named Mama Bear. Dealing half the player's health in damage and having a life pool the size of roughly five Sharks, she is the toughest enemy the player has faced so far. It's recommended to bring several Metal Spear or plenty of arrows because the number of Bears faced are too many to be handled with a single weapon. The Island has several entrance points all of which lead to dirt paths with direction signs. Around the Island, the player may find a couple of new Materials: Honeycombs harvested from Natural Beehives, Birch Seeds, and Pinecones found from felling the Island's trees. The main story objective consists of activating three antennas atop the islands three relay stations. After activation, the next code for the receiver is revealed on a screen, leading to Caravan Island, marking the start of the Second Chapter. A Machete is required to clear some vegetation blocking a path leading to Relay Station 6. To obtain this Machete, the player must either lure Mama Bear away from her cave by collecting Wild Berries from bushes around the Island and feeding them to her in a large container near her cave, or kill her.

candidates.title: Raft review
candidates.text: I have had a love hate relationship with this game. I got it in early access before the story. and whilst there was only so much to do. I really enjoyed the chill, isolated vibe. Where you must stay alive and make life comfortable. but as the game has progressed although the story and new stuff for your raft is a welcome addition the chill isolation has descended into a slaughter fest boss battle platformer. After playing half the game of building out your raft, painting it, decorating it and becoming almost self sufficient. The late game drags you into a dystopian mad max. killing spree. as the chapters progress you suddenly get a boss fight then another and another with a platformer in between. who in there right mind wants that after 20 or so hours of painting and farming. and if you do. Do you want to wait for 20 hours of painting and farming to get to your bit of the game. the late game seems so jarringly at odds with the first half. knowing what I know now I don't think I would have bought it in the first place. so all in all a really good survival builder game that loses it's way at endgame.

candidates.title: Game Mechanics
candidates.text:
Islands and Flotsam spawn relative to the center of the Raft. When coming within a certain range of the center, Islands are loaded into the Ocean of Raft to give the illusion that all islands are spawned in at all times. In reality, non Story-related Islands spawn at random intervals just outside the player's view range, and within the specific biome the player is currently sailing. Story Islands receive a randomized spawn point within a predefined distance-range relative to the raft before being loaded into the game. In other words, when the player attempts to locate a Story Island using the Receiver, the game decides on specific location for the Island to spawn, and will then spawn the Island on that point when the raft center comes within range of the Island.

Flotsam always spawns on a line perpendicular to the raft's current heading, and within a 14 Foundations width of the center of the raft. It is spawned ahead of the raft, much in the same way as Islands, in order to make it seem like the Ocean is filled with it.

Alexandre Lacazette (French pronunciation: ​[alɛksɑ̃dʁ lakazɛt]; born 28 May 1991) is a French professional footballer who plays as a forward for Ligue 1 club Olympique Lyon and the France national team.

Lacazette came into prominence as a member of the academy at Lyon, where he made his professional debut aged 19. He helped the club win the Coupe de France and Trophée des Champions in 2012, and was named the Ligue 1 Player of the Year in 2014–15.[3] During his time in France, Lacazette cultivated a reputation as a prolific goalscorer and poacher, recording multiple twenty-goal seasons, which earned him a move to Arsenal in a then club-record £46.5 million (€53 million) deal in 2017.[4]

ver since debuting for the national side, Lacazette has represented France across all youth levels. He was a key player in France's victory in the 2010 UEFA European Under-19 Championship, where he scored the match-winning goal in the final against Spain.[5] He then made his senior international debut in June 2013, scoring his first goal in March 2015.

Known for dribbling, pace, and ability with both feet, as well as his persistence to press and tackle when out of possession, Lacazette has been compared to former Arsenal forward Ian Wright by Gérard Houllier.

candidates.title: Robin van Persie
candidates.text:
On 20 October, Van Persie scored United's second goal in a 4–2 win over Stoke City, opening up his body and guiding a cross into the far corner with his left foot. In the next Premier League game against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, he scored his seventh goal in the league, with a sidefoot finish from Antonio Valencia's driven cross to put United 2–0 up. He also played a part in the first goal, firing a shot against the post that cannoned off David Luiz and into the net, in a 3–2 United win. On 3 November, he scored against his former club Arsenal in a 2–1 victory. This meant that he had scored against all 20 current Premier League clubs. On 9 December, Van Persie scored a last minute winner from a deflected free kick in a 3–2 victory over Manchester City, his Manchester derby debut. This goal ended City's unbeaten Premier League record in the 2012–13 season and also their unbeaten home record extending into the previous season.

After scoring against Everton on 10 February 2013, Van Persie went ten games without scoring, finally ending his barren run when he scored a penalty against Stoke on 14 April. Against Queens Park Rangers on 23 February, he had to be substituted after falling against a television camera and injuring a hip, but was fit for United's next match.

On 22 April, he netted a first-half hat-trick against Aston Villa, confirming Manchester United's 20th league title with four games in hand. His second goal came from a Rooney pass from behind the halfway line, which he volleyed into the net from outside the box. Supporters of Manchester United voted Van Persie as the Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year for the 2012–13 season. Van Persie was nominated by UEFA into the 10-man shortlist for the 2012–13 Best Player in Europe award.

On 1 March 2011, he was ruled out for three weeks, which would see him miss the Champions League return leg with Barcelona. However, he recovered in time for the return leg at Camp Nou. During the game, he received a yellow card in the first half for a foul. In the second half, he was sent off after he received a second yellow card when the referee, Massimo Busacca, deemed him to be time-wasting by taking a shot at goal after the whistle was blown (one second earlier) for offside. Barcelona went on to score twice more and advanced to the quarter finals on a 4–3 aggregate result. Afterwards, Van Persie branded Busacca's decision as a "total joke", claiming that with the noise of the 95,000-strong crowd he could not hear the whistle. On 19 March 2011, he scored the equalizing goal in a 2–2 against West Bromwich Albion at The Hawthorns. The match finished 2–2 with Arsenal still five points behind the current leaders, Manchester United.

On 10 April 2011 in a match against Blackpool, Van Persie put in a Man of the Match performance to give Arsenal a crucial 3–1 win as he set up a goal and scored the third. On 24 April 2011, he became the first player to score in seven successive Premier League away games when he scored against Bolton, beating Didier Drogba's record who was on six successive away games, between August and November 2009. candidates.title: Robin van Persie
candidates.text: On 8 May 2011, Arsenal lost 3–1 against Stoke City at the Britannia Stadium. In the last home game of the season, he scored against Aston Villa, but Arsenal lost the match 2–1. In the last game of the season away to Fulham, he managed to score in his ninth consecutive away match, bringing his goal tally for the season to a personal record of 18 league goals. He also equalled the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo and Thierry Henry by scoring 18 league goals from the turn of the year to the end of the season. He ended the season just two goals behind joint league top scorers, Carlos Tevez and Dimitar Berbatov in the race for the golden boot, despite being injured for half of the season. candidates.text:
Van Persie opened his 2008–09 account on 31 August with a brace in Arsenal's 3–0 league victory over Newcastle United. On 29 October, he scored his fiftieth career Arsenal goal in a 4–4 home draw with North London derby rivals Tottenham, but was hit with his first red card of the season on 1 November after knocking down goalkeeper Thomas Sørensen with a shoulder charge in a 2–1 loss to Stoke City. Sørensen later admitted to "teasing" Van Persie in an attempt to provoke a reaction. On 30 November, he scored a brace against Chelsea to help Arsenal come from behind and pick up a 2–1 victory at Stamford Bridge. On 21 December 2008, he scored a spectacular goal against Liverpool, which was later named the second BBC Goal of the Month of his career. With captain Cesc Fàbregas injured and regular stand-in skipper Manuel Almunia rested, Van Persie captained Arsenal for the first time on 3 January 2009 for the club's 3–1 FA Cup Third Round victory over Plymouth Argyle. Van Persie scored Arsenal's first and third goals, while the second was a result of his cross being deflected into the net by a Plymouth player for an own goal.

In January 2009, every Arsenal goal that month was either scored or assisted by Van Persie, which earned him the club's Player of the Month award. His most inspirational display being against Hull City, where he struck the post with a freekick, and provided three assists to his teammates; he later received the Man of the Match award. On 24 February, Van Persie scored a crucial penalty that earned Arsenal a 1–0 win over Roma in the UEFA Champions League Round of 16 encounter, after he was fouled by defender Philippe Mexès. He followed it up with a fifth Champions League goal by converting another penalty against Villarreal in a 3–0 victory.

candidates.title: Robin van Persie
candidates.text:
Before the start of the 2010–11 season, Van Persie changed his squad number to 10, previously worn by Arsenal and Netherlands legend Dennis Bergkamp. He made his 200th appearance on 28 August but an ankle injury suffered in the same game placed him on the sidelines once again. He returned as a substitute for Arsenal's 1–0 home defeat to Newcastle United on 7 November.

On 1 January 2011, van Persie scored his first goal of the season in a 3–0 away win over Birmingham City. On

15 January, he added two more goals to his tally in a comfortable 3–0 win over West Ham. This made him only the fourth Dutchman to reach 50 goals in England's top division. Van Persie scored his first career hat-trick in a 3–0 win over Wigan Athletic on 22 January and two goals against Newcastle United in a 4–4 draw on 5 February. Continuing his fine form, he hit a brace the following week against Wolverhampton Wanderers scoring both Arsenal goals in a 2–0 win including a volley from inside the box. The ten goals he scored between 1 January and 12 February set a new Premier League record for most goals scored in the first two months of a calendar year.

Van Persie set the Emirates alight with a goal from an almost impossible angle in Arsenal's fightback against Barcelona in the UEFA Champions League Round of 16, which ended 2–1 in favour of the Gunners. On 27 February 2011, Van Persie captained Arsenal at Wembley Stadium in the League Cup final, scoring the first half equalizer for the Gunners. It was his first goal at Wembley and his first in a cup final for Arsenal. However, he was later taken off in the second half with a knee injury he picked up while scoring the goal.

After the international break, he scored both Arsenal goals against Norwich City to help the Gunners to a 2–1 win on 19 November 2011. In Van Persie's fifth Champions League match of the season he scored twice in the 49th and 86th minute to lift Arsenal to a 2–1 victory over Borussia Dortmund and to qualify Arsenal for the knockout phase on 23 November 2011.

After failing to score against Fulham, Van Persie scored again for Arsenal, this time against Wigan Athletic to make the score 4–0 to Arsenal on 3 December 2011. He then added to his tally with the only goal of the game against Everton, an exquisite volley from an Alex Song long ball. The following match, versus Aston Villa, saw him score a penalty and provide an assist. Van Persie's final goal of the 2011 calendar year came in Arsenal's one-goal win over Queens Park Rangers on the last day of the year. The goal took his tally for the year to 35 goals, one short of Alan Shearer's Premier League record.

The following calendar year started in the same fashion for Van Persie, but Arsenal began to falter, losing three consecutive matches against Fulham, Manchester United and Swansea City, even though the Dutchman scored in the latter two. On 29 January, he rescued his team, scoring two penalties against Aston Villa in the fourth round of the FA Cup to help Arsenal to a 3–2 win after falling 2–0 down in a Man of the Match performance. It was also his 120th goal in an Arsenal shirt, equalling fellow Dutch legend Dennis Bergkamp's total. On 4 February, he overtook Bergkamp as the 10th highest scorer in Arsenal's history, scoring another hat-trick as Arsenal beat Blackburn 7–1 at home, with three close-range goals from crosses by Theo Walcott and Francis Coquelin. He was also credited with two assists in the game as he set up Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's first Premier League goal and unselfishly passed to Thierry Henry enabling him to score his first Premier League goal since returning on loan.

candidates.title: Alfheim
candidates.text:
The Prose Edda says that these two groups of elves were “unalike in appearance, but by far more unalike in nature.” Many have assumed that these dark elves were the same race as the svartalfar, or black elves, mentioned elsewhere. Although neither source described Alfheim itself, descriptions of the elves themselves likely provide insight into what their world would have been like. The light elves were said by Sturluson to be beautiful, radiant beings. Most interpretations of Alfheim suppose that the land these elves lived in would be similarly bright and fair.

Another passage in the Prose Edda is often assumed to refer to Alfheim, although the name is not specifically given. The text explains Norse cosmology and mythology explained through a character who recounts what he knows in a test of knowledge. When asked about the heavenly realms that will survive Ragnarok, the character names three and says that the highest of them is called Vidblain. Vidblain, “Wide Blue,” is where the character believes that the hall of Gimle lies. After Ragnarok, Gimle will become the heavenly abode of the honored dead. Now, however, the character says that only the light elves live in the land of Vidblain. Because the light elves live there, scholars believe that Vidblain and Alfheim may have been one and the same. Because the sources have so little information about either, however, this cannot be proven for sure.

candidates.title: Vanaheim
candidates.text:
It should come as no surprise, then, that the sources are completely silent as to what kind of world Vanaheim is. However, its name may contain an indication of the place's character. One of the primary ways the pre-Christian Norse and other Germanic peoples classified geographical spaces (as well as psychological states) was with reference to their concept of the distinction between the innangard and utangard. That which is innangard (“inside the fence”) is orderly, law-abiding, and civilized, while that which is utangard (“beyond the fence”) is chaotic, anarchic, and wild. This psychogeography found its natural expression in agrarian land-use patterns, where the fence (the -gard or, in Old Norse, -garðr of the above terms) separated pastures and fields of crops from the wilderness beyond them.

Of the Nine Worlds, two are innangard spaces: Asgard and Midgard, the world of human civilization. Both of these contain -gard in their names and are depicted as having a fence or fortification surrounding them. The rest of the Nine Worlds’ names end in -heim, and there's no reference to their being enclosed in any way, which seems to indicate that they're essentially utangard places. Such a designation is certainly in keeping with the way these places are described in Old Norse literature. Thus, we can infer that Vanaheim, like the Vanir themselves, is somewhat more wild or “natural,” and less “cultural,” than the world of the Vanir's Aesir counterparts, or even that of humanity.

candidates.title: Skills and Abilities
candidates.text:
Abilities are the unique attributes of each character in the game. For the avatar, they can be chosen during character creation, the decendants inherit them from the parents. These attributes are also influenced by events in the gameplay, as well as various items in the character's inventory.

To show the attributes during the game, select a character and then click on the Detailed information button right of the character's name, or use the I key. This works for all characters, even if they do not belong to the player's dynasty.

candidates.title: News/January Team Update
candidates.text:
What are the Character, Stronghold, and Guild Naming restrictions?
The following are restricted: Special characters (!@#$%, etc.), capitalized letters other than the first letter of the name (e.g., McFly, WeIrDoGuY), and spaces.
How does character name reservation and deletion work? How long after I delete a character until it is available again? Do I need to play with a character in order to reserve the name or just create the character?
Completing the character creation process will reserve the name for that character. Character names are not automatically released again after character deletion. Releasing names for re-use is a manual process that we will likely run at some point in the future but it is not something we expect to do regularly or start doing in the near future.
What is the minimum and maximum number of letters that are allowed to be used in a character’s name or guild?
Guild names are limited to 2 - 20 characters, character names are limited to 2 - 16 characters. Note that spaces, numbers, and multiple capital letters cannot be used in either guild or character names.
Will character voice selection be available at launch?
Yes, you will be able to select a voice for your player. Each class will include 3 - 4 options for you to choose from!

candidates.title: Expeditions: Samurai - Dev Diary #2: Character Progression
candidates.text:
[img src=" in Expeditions: Rome, equipment is the primary way you define a character's abilities in combat. Weapons provide up to 4 active abilities each, and the character's outfit and hat or helmet provide another 2 abilities. Weapon abilities are most often attacks, while outfit and headwear abilities are more focused on defense and utility. Unlike Expeditions: Rome, an item's abilities are no longer randomized; each type of item comes in a few set varieties with specific ability loadouts. When you pick up an "Ornate Naginata", you will know that it has different abilities than your "Balanced Naginata", but the exact same abilities as any other Ornate Naginata.

Any character can equip any piece of equipment, but apart from the most basic couple of abilities on each weapon, using the abilities of your equipment will require you to invest into the Proficiency perks mentioned above. Thus, any character can wear a heavy set of armor and benefit from its protection, but only those who are trained in its use will be able to activate its ability.

[img src=" goal with designing Expeditions: Samurai has been to ensure that each choice doesn’t feel overwhelming for new players, but over the course of the game will create a vast range of options and leave lots of space for theory-crafting and build-making if desired.

If you've made it all the way through this text, we're sure you have lots of thoughts on the changes we've made from Expeditions: Rome. Why not join our Discord server and jump into the discussions there?

And remember to check out our Dev Diary #1 - Story Writing - on the Expeditions: Samurai Steam page.

candidates.title: Operation Underground
candidates.text: Squad Conquest is set almost entirely within the Underground Station, with only each team's deployment areas being above ground. candidates.title: Muton (XCOM: Enemy Unknown)
candidates.text:
Standing over 2 meters, this humanoid creature is physically powerful and aggressive, but mentally weak. They appear to be the least intelligent and very vulnerable to psi-attacks. However, studies showed that their memory is imprinted with high amount of knowledge in combat tactics and weaponry. Furthermore, based on autopsies, it is clearly evident that the Muton is genetically designed and modified for combat. As such, one must take great care not to underestimate the capabilities of the Mutons.

candidates.title: Makes Space Suits, Won't Travel
candidates.text: After completing this section of the quest, Celeste will task the player with tracking down Primal Leather, Raptidon flank hide and Mantiqueen chitin. The latter two of those items can be bought at Sebastian Adam's store. If you planned ahead, Stefan Garcia at the Botanical Lab in Emerald Vale sells Primal Leather, but, you have to buy it before you complete the Geothermal Plant, especially if you switch over Edgewater. Once Stephan relocates to Edgewater (in the Cantina), he will no longer sell anything. Primal Leather can be acquired rather easily in either Emerald Vale (Primal Nest) or on Scylla. Every size Primal drops it while the quest is active on almost every kill, and these items didn't exist until the quest started (aside from Stefan as stated above I guess?) They go in your quest items inventory and the quest itself updates when you have enough. Mantiqueens and Raptidons are abundant on Monarch, although both are somewhat difficult to kill, especially in packs. Once the player has the required animal pelts, they can return to Celeste in Byzantium.

candidates.title: Manufacturing Desk
candidates.text:
Hello! Improvements continue respecting the manufacturing department. The new desk should ease dealing with your selection of already created products by listing and allowing to send them to manufacturing units directly.

Manufactured products having a slight color variation depending on ingredients was going to arrive in this update but has been delayed as it heavily conflicts with a product optimization being done in the background when placing products and more investigation is required or a good workaround. Also, next update could feature more manufactured products so suggestions are welcomed.

Changelog:
- Implemented a new prop: the manufacturing desk. Located in both the manufacturing tab and devices tab it allows to: check available recipes/number of manufacturing units and check the type and number of manufactured products present in your store or storage and send them to a global queue, then they will be sent automatically to manufacturing units as they are available.

- Added a freezer version for manufactured products. Salads, sandwiches, etc. are now placed there. Cakes may move too in the future.

- Added an unlabeled version of the manufacturing storage shelf.

- Fixed an issue which would make manufacturing shelves overlap with themselves or actually anything.

- Pending items in any manufacturing unit’s queue can now be removed when clicking on them.

- NPCs shouldn’t go through the toolbox organizer anymore.

- The perk that allowed player’s holding a box to visualize shelves with the product in the box now should work too for manufacturing.

- Removed the temporary button in employees’ tab used for fixing manufacturing level.

- Further reduced the scale of some items in the manufacturing unit tray so every possible ingredient can fit.

- Employees in the role of manufacturing will give a warning message if they cannot continue to gather ingredients for a manufactured product due to having no existences of that ingredient.

- Corrected brightness/light acting weird in the new manufacturing areas at the end of the store/storage.

candidates.title: Goods and Items in The Guild - Europa 1410
candidates.text:
[img src=" can order their workers to “Look for Ingredients” to gain resources for the production of goods.

Intermediate Products
[p align="start"]Intermediate products serve as the bridge between raw materials and resources and end products. They transform resources into more refined and usable forms - for example, as a Smith, you can use iron and silver ingots, which are made from ore. You can combine the ingots to create an end product, like a silver ring. But if you want to create more profitable items, you will need to craft an intermediate product first, such as fittings, that can then be used to create, for example, short swords.
[p align="start"]Other intermediate products, such as joining material, can be used to create more profitable items. Generally, intermediate products can be found on the marketplace or crafted in a workshop, though selling them often doesn't pay off.

[img src=" can forge fittings as a Smith, or purchase them from the marketplace. Fittings are an ingredient for some end products, such as…

[img src=" Short swords, which are useful for combat…

[img src=" Or silver chains, which you can use to influence others' opinions of you in the political scene.

Let’s take the Alchemist for another example. Paint can be made by your workers in your workshop, and you can easily sell it. Or, you can choose to keep it as an ingredient and combine it with iron ingots to make something a little bit more dangerous…

question: What are the current supply concerns for the player's forces in the game?

candidates.title: Against the Storm review
candidates.text: Every game is about rewards to the player. So then what are the rewards that AtS offers?Well, they are scant. AtS is not really a city builder or a management game per se, these are just the mechanics of the game. AtS is primarily a puzzle game, as this is the principal mechanic for victory and the primary reward of the game is more puzzle pieces.So, then, the player is not rewarded with a city or supply chains to continually develop and view. You do not build a stable foundation from which to grow. The mechanics are such that the player repetitively makes the same group of buildings, in pretty much the same manner. The supply chains may vary, but it's still just a question of which steps are solved on map or by trade. In any event, none of this is permanent, because every 30 minutes or so you 'solve' the map and then begin another at square one.The game has many positives. It is artistically beautiful, stable and bug free. I enjoyed the game play enough to put in 60 hours, and then realized the only reward was climbing the tech tree. So if you enjoy repetitive puzzle solving, then this game is a 10 out of 10 for you. I was looking for a city builder, so 2 out of 10 for me.

candidates.title: Hero's Hour review
candidates.text: 길게 적어볼려했으나 그럴필요가없다. 결국은 물량망겜인데 물량은 제한되있고 싸울때마다 병력은 줄어듬 그렇다고 뭐점령한다고해서 물량이늘어나는것도아님(조금씩은늘어남) 전략적요소는 ㅈ도없지 그렇다고 영지발전의 재미는 있나? 없지 상대가 나보다 발전이느리더라도 전투로 병력빠졌을떄 들어오면 생성제한이걸려있어서 영지가 좋든 나쁘든 상관없이 져야함 플레이어가 변수를 창줄할 기회가 적으니 재미도 없고 스트레스만 생김 일반난이도조차 어찌할수없는 부조리가 보이는데 그 윗단계는 어떨지 상상이안가네 돈이아깝다고 생각하는 게임은 사펑이후로 처음이다

candidates.title: Satisfactory review
candidates.text: A game with a lot of potential but badly balanced. The enemies are much stronger than you, and you don't have a lot of weapons so I highly recommend to play without agresive aliens. Most of the time you will be walking instead of designing your factories cause the resources are far far away. The energy is a problem all the time and doesn't looks like you will reach a point when everything will be automatic. I miss a lot of content that can fix this details, it's like the developers doesn't played their own game.

candidates.title: The Great War: Western Front™ review
candidates.text: So this game has MASSIVE potential and i really cant wait to see the future. The games main problems come from main core game play of the battles and not the overview of the full war That being said the game can be very hard to play at times. Obviously I'm not everyone but the games battles feel's too much like a table top game that has major negatives. What i mean is that if one of the enemies groups of men push towards you and only 1 out of the 50 soldiers enter the trenches it stops all your soldiers being able to fire at them that includes other trenches. And then you have to wait until all of them enter to begin the battle and its so annoying to see all of the enemies to walk in without being shot at! Another issue similar to this is when soldiers just don't listen, what i mean is when i order them to halt and to fight an enemy they just stand there taking gun fire waiting until all of the soldiers get in place just staring at the enemy! And this can be especially annoying when they just keep turning around or walking backwards just leading to there demise. Another point I like to point out is the supply in battles and there inconstancy. For example i pay 90 supplies to play artillery but it cost 6 to fire it each time. This can be extremely annoying as I feel like its useless to buy something with no supplies then to pay for it after you bought it. Some inconstancy is the damage output from these supplies such as the bomber planes as they can just destroy a few machine gun nest in a swoop but it takes 4 heavy artillery shots to take out just one. And then those same machine guns can be take out in just a few seconds if a platoon gets barley even close to it throw hundreds of grenades.

candidates.title: HUMANKIND™ review
candidates.text: 战略资源太少（即使调到最高），兵种需求太高。导致近代却得用近战兵，希望官方尽快修改战略资源产生的条件

candidates.title: Dwarf Fortress review
candidates.text: But as a modern game it just feels too unpolished. I would not put the negative review if this was an Early Access, but after 11 years of development I've been expecting much more.Main killer feature of the update - graphics - are not really used to give the player information about what's happening on the screen. Neither does the menus.I would really want to love this game. In it's current state, though, it's still too harsh for those get used to modern game design.P.S. Feel free to call me a casual player if you'd like.

candidates.title: Ready or Not review
candidates.text: The game feels bogged down by unfinished content, Redundant equipment and over powered AI. Crashes mid op, Hunting for the last civi on the map. The Forced Commander mode wher ei need to manage stress and unlock the maps.This game just hasnt kept its quality high throught its development. Could really do a with some Actual open feedback Gathering as currently the game just refuses to hit a solid mark.

candidates.title: Blood Bowl 3 review
candidates.text: Long story short, the current state of the game is bad.Cons- It's only got 12 teams currently. The current team release schedule is one new team every 3 months. Which means it's going to take a couple years before every team was in the game- You get disconnected from the servers regularly which forces you to restart single player games from the beginning- Star Players Skills are missing from the game. They don't have plans to add them until November 2023 making star players essentially useless for the entire year- Multiple Block skill is missing from the game- The microstansactions are SUPER anti-consumer and currently all cosmetics are microtransactions. This basically means to outfit your team to make them look unique, you'd have to spend 4,950 Warpstones which comes out to ~$45. The biggest issue here is that these items can only be used once. You put them on a player an no other player can use them unless you remove them from the other player. This means if you want to outfit all of your teams you have to purchase the same cosmetic item multiple times- Menu UI is constantly disappearing- Offline doesn't have the same progression as your online. If you play the "story" while connected to online and you suddenly can't reconnect to the servers then you would have to start from the beginning offline. You also don't have any of the teams you made while connected to the servers when offline- Competitive is non-existent until May- The customization options like pitch, cheerleaders, balls, etc aren't in the game and only cheerleaders and balls are in the game if you purchased the brutal edition- For some reason Fouling refuses to work every time.

candidates.title: IXION review
candidates.text: I played twice, let's talk about what's retarded about this game1. Failure probability that is too far off the mark. I can understand that failures occur due to overtime or fatigue, but I can't understand that meals are eaten every five cycles. The industry elite who can get on board the spaceship will have an accident every 2-3 cycles only if they work overtime. If there are two accidents, you can't repair the ship. Let's wait for game over.2. The same resource scheduling as the failed design. The year 2022 is almost 2023. Your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game does not support automatic resource scheduling between two sectors. How dare you design for players to operate by hand? Just like you play with and play the role of governor, what should we do if our industrial planet is short of mineral resources? I must set up my own plan to dispatch minerals from another mineral planet for production. I can understand that personnel need to be manually dispatched. Mobilizing resources by hand is a pure torture.3. Unreasonable maintenance speed. I still haven't figured out how to build a 1000 blood spaceship. Why can I only maintain single digit durability every cycle, and lose 50 points of durability every week when ship boom twice? Indian planes are more stable than your ship.4. Lack of people, lack of people, lack of people. Since the beginner tutorial in the prologue, I have never received manpower for the whole game, which is why I re opened it once, and then found no one. Did you not put a fixed place for me to connect to the freezer at all in Chapter 1? This game also makes me crazy by distinguishing between workers and non workers. Children in the can do non dangerous work. You go on strike every day when you don't work. You are proletarian than the proletariat, you product not at all!5. Other minor problems.

candidates.title: The Universim review
candidates.text: I want to recommend this game, or I would if the game didn't have the most frustrating end game and mid-game ever. Around the modern period is when it gets absolutely annoying as everything takes increasingly more advanced resources which... well wouldn't be a problem. IF THOSE RESOURCES COULD BE PRODUCED FAST ENOUGH. Did I mention that all resources are produced at angonizingly slow rates where you will be waiting for steel and electronics for hours? Did I mention that half of the creator powers will make your people hate you even when you're helping them? (Telekinesis for picking up dead bodies or resources and lightning bolts to kill enemies even when no friendlies are hit by said bolt) Did I mention that half the buildings in the Modern Period ESPECIALLY engineers take educated workers? Did I mention that schools can only teach three people and requires advanced resources like steel (Which take educated workers to produce) to be upgraded to the next level? Vehicles CANNOT store large amounts of resources. People will take resources by hand, sit with it on their lap, and go to places to build things so don't go thinking vehicles help. And to get to the worst, absolutely worst part... POWER. If you use power that will not kill the planet that your popluation lives on over time (Ie the wind power) you will NEVER HAVE POWER late game. I have over 30 Wind turbines in my city. But guess what, Wind power is global so if one runs out of wind? Then all of them do on the entire planet. And even if you turn off the news sounds? The 'power shortage' will play endlessly without fail or stopping until your wind turbines are able to squeeze out a single bit of power into your batteries.. and then immediately stop working. This forces you, outright, to use things that outright produce pollution because if you don't, you literally will not have power at all.

candidates.title: Grand Tactician: The Civil War (1861-1865) review
candidates.text: 1) The AI needs to abide by readiness, supply and weapons supply rules in the same way as the human. If the AI can't do that, the solution is to re-write it, not have two separate and unequal game systems.2) The Southern AI should not invade north from Virginia until summer of 1862, should respect Kentucky neutrality (if it exists)until 1862. Both sides should deploy only minimal forces in West Virginia. The AI needs to give up its insane fixation on West Virginia and the Shenandoah.3) The AI should combine its forces into solitary armies (or operate corps in close proximity) rather than have multiple forces of 5k magically swarm and make combined attacks. Next to a war with allies and a fighting withdrawal, a combined attack is the hardest military operation. But since the AI doesn't have readiness, supply or weapons issues...4) The AI needs to build brigades based on what it needs and/or what the other player is building, rather than magically cheating up a hundred thousand at a time and hurling them at the enemy. Over and over and over.5) Take forts and depots out of the game or permit any army remaining still long enough to build them. The expense is game-breaking. Drop the expense of provisions to a manageable level.6) Either take buildings, building railroads and the entire production of goods out of the game or make them usable. Nobody can afford to build them because of the expense, and because the human is having to spend every penny raising every possible brigade in order to fight off the AI horde.I've uninstalled and re-installed this four times. This is a mound of delicious frosting with a cardboard cake underneath.

candidates.title: Satisfactory review
candidates.text: Don't get me wrong, the game is fun. I'm afraid of what the devs just did in update 4.They created a power storage device, which is neat. However, in order to create cases in which you would need it (Instead of the thing you would usually do, like have solar panels, wind turbines, etc that charge them and then you can use that power at night), they nerfed things to try to get you to use them. Even then, the use cases for it is still not a valid use case (You can use them for Geysers, which now have fluctuating power generation. The stage at which you get those generators is pretty late in the game, which you usually already have a good power grid setup.) I'm afraid that this is going to keep happening. I'm afraid of developers forcing a player to play the way they want you to play, instead of letting you have your own choices. Sure, the nerf isn't too bad, since things have unlimited resources. However, I'm more afraid of what the future holds with this kind of action. I wish there was a Mixed or Neutral review.

candidates.title: Kerbal Space Program 2 review
candidates.text: I cannot recommend this game in the current state. If you want to enjoy KSP and you are not a current player, I recommend buying KSP1. It is a true classic, and absolutely rock solid and playable. If you want early access in order to supply the developers with a continuous stream of bugs (and OH BOY you are going to be finding bugs) and you have a pile of cash you want desperately to be rid of, then by all means buy this EARLY ACCESS version.

candidates.title: Lightyear Frontier review
candidates.text: 如果是格子危机，我想我能够理解……但是负重危机……为什么仓库有重量限制，未来开发成网游卖负重吗……建造类感觉并不建造，只是玩摆件，并不是很有趣背景格子血红色辣眼睛，高暖色调更是痛苦，肯定有人被此折磨过……优点：高达农场种菜，有新意有新鲜感（很短），优化帧率尚可，基本不丢帧，沙盒世界仍然眼前一亮缺点：无自动化，重复劳作强迫升级科技，恶性循环。无方块建造仅有摆件设置，负重极其苛刻却又无超重惩罚，支援生产类建筑仍然需要优化，重复操作令人难受总结：和朋友杀会时间是不错的选择，但是长线经营起来，仍然让人感觉不如幸福工厂，当前可游玩内容不太多，多人可能一会就结束了，建议观望游戏折扣后期较为完整后再考虑入手刚需：优化生产列表、生产方式，仓库储存方式，负重限制

candidates.title: Terminator: Dark Fate - Defiance review
candidates.text: The game has its fun points, and has potential, but there is some significant tweaks needed to the supply system. Any improvement in your units rapidly drives up the supply cost... and higher supply cost forces you to have fewer units. In fact, the game will force you to give up hard-won units, just to make it to the next area. Its obvious the developer wants it to feel like you're constantly scraping by and having to scrounge desperately to keep some semblance of an army going... but the current implementation of the supply mechanic... something which punishes you for making progress... just isn't fun.

candidates.title: Loop Hero review
candidates.text: I wish we had more skill based options because the current skill ceiling is just based off your deck building and land placement. The last major negative is the meta progression. Normally in a rogue lite you can slowly gain power for future runs so even if you die you gain some small advantage, in loop hero you are punished for dying by losing 70% of all resources you picked up. Usually a dev will expect a player to die and not punish them this harshly, the idea of losing future resources you could have made being enough, this forces you to retreat back to camp and throw away the current run to build up your camp. For a normal player they will crawl through the meta progression unless they throw away runs and skilled players just won't bother with camp because they can just beat the game and fight the secret boss in 7 runs. This makes the deck progression slow as well since getting most new cards is tied to making new camp tiles so the most interesting choices in the game are locked behind a slow grind or are just never used. There is also passive items you can bring to runs but they do so little besides the really strong one that it's obvious which to choose from a glance. Overall this game just needs more, more heroes, more item effects, more ways to progress and more choices.

candidates.title: Age of Mythology: Retold review
candidates.text: Having played Age of Mythology for nearly 20 years, I have a deep appreciation for it. However, I have some concerns about its current state, particularly regarding the A.I. I was hoping for an experience similar to Age of Empires IV, but instead, the A.I. in this game struggles significantly. It can't navigate water, and when on land, it engages in overly aggressive tactics without adequate defense. While I still enjoy many aspects of Age of Mythology, the A.I. is a critical component that falls short. Given these issues, I find it hard to recommend the game in its current state.

candidates.title: Brighton (PC2)
candidates.text:
Success here is bittersweet, Herr General.

­While your forces are again to be commended for their efforts against the British, the devastation of the Kriegsmarine is the most serious setback to our invasion plans yet.

Your immediate supply situation is not in danger, I have made arrangements for fuel and ammunition to be airlifted to the airfields you have so far secured.

As for the prospects of the invasion as a whole; I must consult with High Command before I can give you any kind of answer to that question.

Historically, any invasion of Britain would be challenged by the British Royal Navy. While the German Kriegsmarine could only muster a handful of warships in the autumn of 1940, the Royal Navy boasted well over 100 warships and more than 1000 total vessels.

candidates.title: V Rising review
candidates.text: you have players wait in a spectator box until its their turn to duel. That will give spoils to the victor. Or even a supply drop mechanic AT THE VERY LEAST. Because right now all the game does is allow for people to raid each other when the opps is offline or camp farming spots desperate for player interaction, thats all what people are going to do until you give them something more meaningful.

candidates.title: The Great War: Western Front™ review
candidates.text: Related to the above, if both player and AI could pull tricks like making a force look larger in a certain area (or smaller than it really is), it could produce some exciting and unexpected battles. I really do enjoy the game, it scratches a certain strategic itch around positioning forces and ensuring they have the right supply and support...then playing as those forces in real time, very nice. I just get a little disheartened after 10 turns moving pieces around without any action, then find the battles themselves a bit lackluster, especially early on when supply is short.
